title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄序
皇上御宇之十年壬午秋八月應
天府復當鄉試士于是提學
御史臣李時成臣姚士觀暨
諸曹六館所簡士四千九百
有奇濟濟咸集矣府尹臣劉
庠府丞臣曹大埜先期以
===
請
上命贊善臣鯉修撰臣懋孝典試
事得乘傳以往是時
上方深
詔執事之臣取士純用經術
崇雅道毋得以恢虛奇誕之士
進視昔加飭厲焉而臣遣自
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄序
皇上御宇之十年，壬午秋八月，應天府復當鄉試士。于是提學御史臣李時成、臣姚士觀暨諸曹六館所簡士四千九百有奇，濟濟咸集矣。府尹臣劉庠、府丞臣曹大埜先期以請，上命贊善臣鯉、修撰臣懋孝典試事，得乘傳以往。是時，上方深詔執事之臣，取士純用經術，崇雅道，毋得以恢虛奇誕之士進，視昔加飭厲焉。而臣遣自
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn of the renwu year, the tenth year of His Majesty's reign (1582), it was once again time for Yingtian Prefecture to examine scholars in the Provincial Examination. Thereupon, the more than four thousand nine hundred scholars selected by Education-intendant Censors Your servants Li Shicheng 李時成 and Yao Shiguan 姚士觀, together with those from the various agencies and the Six Halls of the National University, had all gathered in flourishing numbers. Prefect Your servant Liu Xiang 劉庠 and Vice Prefect Your servant Cao Daye 曹大埜 petitioned in advance, and His Majesty commanded Admonisher Your servant [Shen] Li 鯉 and Senior Compiler Your servant [Shen] Maoxiao 懋孝 to take charge of the examination affairs, granting them permission to travel there by post relay. At this time, His Majesty had just issued a profound edict to the officiating ministers that in selecting scholars they must rely purely on classical learning and esteem the orthodox and refined Way, and that they must not allow grandiloquent, empty, strange, or preposterous scholars to advance—admonishing and encouraging them even more strictly than in the past. And Your servant, dispatched from…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
講幄奉
明詔詔士于數千里外有如士風
文體不廓然一變人心學術
不從化以遷則將何藉而還
報且此
都人士
國家豐鎬所樂育四方士所覶
===
前茅而攺行易趨者也　臣　蚤
夜瞿瞿與　臣　懋孝相毖勉計
何以默回雅道鎔範人文且
令四方士有則焉比至內外
執事咸在同考則推官　臣　民
式敎授　臣　懋循　臣　櫝學正　臣
眉壽　臣　學醇敎諭　臣　相　臣　行
punctuated: 講幄，奉明詔，詔士于數千里外。有如士風文體不廓然一變，人心學術不從化以遷，則將何藉而還報？且此都人士，國家豐鎬所樂育，四方士所覶前茅而攺行易趨者也。臣蚤夜瞿瞿，與臣懋孝相毖勉，計何以默回雅道，鎔範人文，且令四方士有則焉。比至，內外執事咸在。同考則推官臣民式，敎授臣懋循、臣櫝，學正臣眉壽、臣學醇，敎諭臣相、臣行
translation_en:
… the Classics Mat, bearing the illustrious edict to proclaim it to the scholars several thousand li away. Should the ethos of the scholars and their literary style fail to undergo a sweeping transformation, and should human minds and academic learning fail to follow His transformative influence and reform, on what grounds could I return to report on my mission? Moreover, the scholars of this Auxiliary Capital are those whom the dynasty takes delight in nurturing in its Feng and Hao [the ancestral capitals], and whom scholars of the four quarters look to as the vanguard by which to amend their conduct and alter their direction. Day and night your servant was filled with anxious vigilance, mutually cautioning and encouraging Your Servant Mao Xiao [Wang Maoxiao 王懋孝], taking counsel on how we might quietly restore the orthodox way, mold and fashion literary culture, and furthermore provide a model for the scholars of the four quarters.

When we arrived, the officiating officials of the inner and outer wards were all present. Serving as Associate Examiners were Prefectural Judge Your Servant Min Shi; Prefectural Directors of Studies Your Servant Mao Xun [Zang Maoxun 臧懋循] and Your Servant Du; Subprefectural Directors of Studies Your Servant Mei Shou and Your Servant Xue Chun; District Directors of Studies Your Servant Xiang, Your Servant Xing…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
知　臣民紀　臣準　臣脩賢訓導
臣義對而御史　臣應訓　臣一
鯤曁　臣于有年　臣郭惟賢嚴
稽關內外府尹　臣季勳府丞
臣己職提調惟謹肅　臣等以
入鎖院三試士掄其可者遵
制取百三十五人將竣事　臣迺以
===
士文視諸　臣而告之曰士猶
有恢虛奇誕詭于經術者乎
澄汰不盡者乎僉曰無之文
體近雅正乎曰可矣乃次士
名氏錄其文之可者以
獻謹拜手言曰今日之士他日
之公卿執事也公卿百執
punctuated: 知、臣民紀、臣準、臣脩賢，訓導臣義對；而御史臣應訓、臣一鯤，曁臣于有年、臣郭惟賢，嚴稽關內外；府尹臣季勳、府丞臣己，職提調惟謹。肅臣等以入鎖院，三試士，掄其可者，遵制取百三十五人。將竣事，臣迺以士文視諸臣而告之曰：「士猶有恢虛奇誕、詭于經術者乎？澄汰不盡者乎？」僉曰：「無之。」「文體近雅正乎？」曰：「可矣。」乃次士名氏，錄其文之可者以獻。謹拜手言曰：今日之士，他日之公卿執事也。公卿百執
translation_en: …Zhi 知, Your Servant Minji 民紀, Your Servant Zhun 準, and Your Servant Xiuxian 脩賢, and Assistant Instructor (訓導) Your Servant Yidui 義對. Meanwhile, Censors (御史) Your Servant Yingxun 應訓 and Your Servant Yikun 一鯤, together with Your Servant Yu Younian 于有年 and Your Servant Guo Weixian 郭惟賢, strictly inspected the interior and exterior of the examination compound; Prefectural Governor (府尹) Your Servant Jixun 季勳 and Vice Prefectural Governor (府丞) Your Servant Ji 己 discharged their duties as Proctors (提調) with utmost care. They respectfully ushered Your Servants into the locked examination compound. Across the three sessions of testing the scholars, we selected those who were acceptable and, in compliance with the imperial system, admitted one hundred and thirty-five men. As the affair neared completion, Your Servant then showed the scholars' essays to the various officials and said to them: "Among the scholars, are there still any who are grandiose and hollow, bizarre and absurd, or at odds with classical learning? Are there any who have not been thoroughly weeded out?" All replied: "There are none." "Are the literary styles close to elegance and orthodoxy?" They replied: "They are acceptable." Thereupon we arranged the scholars' names in order and recorded their acceptable essays to present to the throne. With hands bowed in reverence, I venture to say: The scholars of today are the grandees, ministers, and functionaries of another day. Grandees, ministers, and the hundred functionaries…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
事天下之治所繇出也其心
實其學正文必象其人溫醇
而博大發之事業悠遠而光
明文之恢虛心不誠也文之
奇誕學不正也不端不慤何
以事
君臣
猶及見長老稱說弘治以前
===
士大夫純尚經義訓發講解
至白首不倦即納事還里中
猶日課習五經性理諸書訓
其後生蓋孜孜畜德而無他
娛焉士之老於儒者即不仕
不棄故業其人皆重彝倫守
規度後生望而嚴事之進而
punctuated: 事，天下之治所繇出也。其心實，其學正，文必象其人，溫醇而博大，發之事業，悠遠而光明。文之恢虛，心不誠也；文之奇誕，學不正也。不端不慤，何以事君？臣猶及見長老稱說：弘治以前，士大夫純尚經義，訓發講解，至白首不倦。即納事還里中，猶日課習《五經》、《性理》諸書，訓其後生，蓋孜孜畜德而無他娛焉。士之老於儒者，即不仕，不棄故業。其人皆重彝倫，守規度，後生望而嚴事之。進而
translation_en: … officials, from whom the governance of all under Heaven proceeds. When their minds are sincere and their learning is orthodox, their writings will necessarily mirror the men themselves—gentle, pure, broad, and great—and when expressed in practical undertakings, these will be far-reaching and illustrious. When writing is grandiose and hollow, it is because the mind is not sincere; when writing is bizarre and absurd, it is because the learning is not orthodox. Without uprightness and good faith, how can one serve the Sovereign? Your servant still lived early enough to hear the elders recount that prior to the Hongzhi era (1488–1505), scholar-officials purely esteemed the meaning of the Classics, elucidating and explaining them tirelessly even until their hair turned white. Even after resigning from office and returning to their home villages, they still daily studied and practiced the Five Classics, the works on Human Nature and Principle (Xingli), and other books to instruct the younger generation, diligently cultivating their virtue with no other amusements. As for scholars who grew old in Confucian learning, even if they never held office, they did not abandon their original studies. Such men all valued the constant human relationships and abided by the established norms, so that the younger generation looked up to them and served them with reverence. When they advanced to…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
有名位于
朝者莫不崇禮義懷忠信不苟
得于富貴士稍踰閑越檢懼
掛清議不齒鄉黨有甚乎刑
戮矣至乎諸子百家二氏淆
雜之書父兄訓子弟輒以爲
記家不儲市不鬻也爾諸士
===
聽鹿鳴而至也鄉之長老有
誦說如所聞者乎蓋自近世
二三才俊斲觚剖樸雅道淪
矣有新奇之道德竊佛老而
附于儒者有新奇之事功拾
管韓而緣以儒者有新奇之
文章摽綴秦漢句字而厭薄
punctuated: 有名位于朝者，莫不崇禮義、懷忠信，不苟得于富貴。士稍踰閑越檢，懼掛清議，不齒鄉黨，有甚乎刑戮矣。至乎諸子百家、二氏淆雜之書，父兄訓子弟輒以爲記，家不儲，市不鬻也。爾諸士聽《鹿鳴》而至也，鄉之長老有誦說如所聞者乎？蓋自近世二三才俊，斲觚剖樸，雅道淪矣。有新奇之道德，竊佛、老而附于儒者；有新奇之事功，拾管、韓而緣以儒者；有新奇之文章，摽綴秦、漢句字而厭薄
translation_en: …held renown and rank at court, there were none who did not revere ritual and righteousness, cherish loyalty and trustworthiness, and refuse to obtain wealth and honor by improper means. If a scholar slightly overstepped the bounds of propriety or transgressed the rules of conduct, he feared being caught up in pure criticism (qingyi) and despised by his local community, considering this worse than corporal punishment or execution. As for the promiscuous and heterodox writings of the Various Masters and Hundred Schools or the Two Sects [Buddhism and Daoism], fathers and elder brothers in instructing their sons and younger brothers always treated them as taboo [reading 諱 for 記?]; households did not store them, and markets did not sell them. Now that all of you scholars have come upon hearing the "Cry of the Deer" (Luming), do the elders in your home communities still recount such things as what I have heard? Indeed, ever since two or three talented men of recent times carved up the square block and split the unworked wood, the elegant Way has sunk into decline. There are those with novel and strange doctrines of morality who steal from the Buddha and Laozi and attach them to Confucianism; there are those with novel and strange doctrines of practical achievement who pick up from Guan Zhong and Han Feizi and fringe them with Confucianism; and there are those with novel and strange literary compositions who pluck and patch together phrases and words from the Qin and Han dynasties while disdaining…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
儒言以爲不足稱述者其才
力文辭皆足鼓動當世操觚
士靡然豔慕之
上之所禁俗之所尚責其實而愈
虛求其純而彌詭此其故歟
夫士方未遇時稍誦非聖書
已足毀成法抗公論規度之
===
內迂而不信也他日爲公卿
大夫將何如此風起于數十
年間而關繫世道人心其害
且見於數十年之後有識屢
歎之　臣　所以欲令四方士視
此舉有則焉蓋不敢不以斯
文爲已責也頃者
punctuated: 儒言，以爲不足稱述者。其才力文辭，皆足鼓動當世操觚士，靡然豔慕之。上之所禁，俗之所尚，責其實而愈虛，求其純而彌詭，此其故歟？夫士方未遇時，稍誦非聖書，已足毀成法、抗公論，規度之內，迂而不信也。他日爲公卿大夫，將何如？此風起于數十年間，而關繫世道人心，其害且見於數十年之後，有識屢歎之。臣所以欲令四方士視此舉有則焉，蓋不敢不以斯文爲已責也。頃者
translation_en: … the words of the Confucians, regarding them as unworthy of mention. Their talent, vigor, and literary style are all sufficient to stir up the writers of the present age, who are swept along in admiring envy of them. What the Emperor prohibits is what popular custom prizes; the more one demands substance from them, the more hollow they become, and the more one seeks purity in them, the more perverse they grow—is this not the reason? Now, when scholars have not yet achieved official advancement, merely reciting non-canonical books a little is already enough to make them subvert established laws and defy public opinion, regarding what lies within the bounds of rules and standards as pedantic and unworthy of belief. When in the future they become Grandees and Great Officers, how will they behave? This trend arose over the past few decades, yet because of its bearing on the moral order of the world and on people's minds, its harm will become manifest decades from now; men of insight have repeatedly lamented it. The reason your servant wishes to make scholars of the four quarters look upon this examination and find a standard in it is that I dare not fail to take the cause of this culture as my own responsibility. Recently, when …

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
德音一下
都人士斐然嚮風在所收者似
一日而改觀焉豈臣等心思
才力所及哉臣以此仰歎
祖宗德化積累深涵
上之風敎捷于桴鼓埏埴而士不
知也若以化耳目爲精神轉
===
移心術還之大雅事在有漸
而已爾諸士自今以往益務
正心實行以經術爲師毋惑
于諸子百家二氏之說夫文
之吏也不旬月行之成也以
終身其毋易視焉雖然臣言
多矣力行不在多言顧與諸
punctuated: 德音一下，都人士斐然嚮風，在所收者，似一日而改觀焉。豈臣等心思才力所及哉？臣以此仰歎祖宗德化積累深涵，上之風敎捷于桴鼓埏埴，而士不知也。若以化耳目爲精神，轉移心術，還之大雅，事在有漸而已。爾諸士自今以往，益務正心實行，以經術爲師，毋惑于諸子百家、二氏之說。夫文之吏也，不旬月；行之成也，以終身，其毋易視焉。雖然，臣言多矣，力行不在多言，顧與諸
translation_en:
… the benevolent imperial pronouncement was handed down, the scholars of the capital brilliantly turned toward the moral wind; among those whom we have selected, it seems that their outlook has been transformed in a single day. How could this be within the reach of the thoughts and abilities of Your servants? Because of this, Your servant looks up in admiration at how the moral transformation wrought by the Imperial Ancestors has accumulated and soaked in deeply, and how His Majesty’s wind of instruction is swifter than the beat of a drumstick or the molding of clay, though the scholars themselves do not realize it. As for transforming what merely pleases the eyes and ears into true spiritual vigor, shifting the orientation of the mind, and returning literature to great elegance—this is a matter that can only be achieved gradually.

From this day forward, all you scholars should increasingly devote yourselves to rectifying your minds and practicing实质 [substantial] conduct, taking classical scholarship as your teacher, and not being deluded by the doctrines of the Various Masters and Hundred Schools or the Two Sects [Buddhism and Daoism]. To alter [吏 for 更?] one's literary style takes less than ten days or a month, whereas the completion of one's moral conduct takes an entire lifetime—do not regard this lightly! Even so, Your servant has already said much; strenuous practice does not lie in many words, and I only wish to join with all you…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
士共勗之
左春坊左賛善兼翰林院檢
討沈鯉謹序
punctuated:
士共勗之。
左春坊左賛善兼翰林院檢討沈鯉謹序。
translation_en:
…scholars to strive together in this.
Respectfully prefaced by Shen Li 沈鯉, Left Admonisher of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy.

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
萬曆十年應天府鄉試
提調官
應天府府尹游季勳〔懋甫江西豐城縣人　壬戌進士〕
應天府府丞李己〔懋推河南磁州人　乙丑進士〕
考試官
左春坊左贊善兼翰林院檢討沈鯉〔仲化河南商丘縣籍　歸德衛人乙丑進士〕
翰林院修撰沈懋孝〔幼貞浙江平湖縣人　戊辰進士〕
同考試官
直隸松江府推官徐民式〔用敬福建浦城縣人　庚辰進士〕
===
湖廣荆州府儒學教授臧懋循〔晉叔浙江長興縣人　庚辰進士〕
江西南昌府儒學教授錢槓〔仲美浙江會稽縣籍　山陰縣人庚辰進士〕
河南開封府鄭州儒學學正祝眉壽〔介卿江西德興縣人　甲子貢士〕
廣西梧州府鬱林州儒學學正鄭學醇〔承孟廣東順德縣人　丁卯貢士〕
陝西西安府盩厔縣儒學教諭曹相〔子良山西太平縣人　丁卯貢士〕
河南開封府杞縣儒學教諭從行知〔光大湖廣鍾祥縣人　甲子貢士〕
浙江杭州府於潛縣儒學教諭萬民紀〔時振江西南城縣人　辛酉貢士〕
山西平陽府絳州稷山縣儒學教諭王準〔平甫陝西同州人　辛酉貢士〕
廣東潮州府普寧縣儒學教諭鄧脩賢〔忠父廣東南海縣人　甲子貢士〕
punctuated:
萬曆十年應天府鄉試

提調官：
應天府府尹游季勳〔懋甫，江西豐城縣人，壬戌進士〕。
應天府府丞李己〔懋推，河南磁州人，乙丑進士〕。

考試官：
左春坊左贊善兼翰林院檢討沈鯉〔仲化，河南商丘縣籍，歸德衛人，乙丑進士〕。
翰林院修撰沈懋孝〔幼貞，浙江平湖縣人，戊辰進士〕。

同考試官：
直隸松江府推官徐民式〔用敬，福建浦城縣人，庚辰進士〕。
湖廣荆州府儒學教授臧懋循〔晉叔，浙江長興縣人，庚辰進士〕。
江西南昌府儒學教授錢槓〔仲美，浙江會稽縣籍，山陰縣人，庚辰進士〕。
河南開封府鄭州儒學學正祝眉壽〔介卿，江西德興縣人，甲子貢士〕。
廣西梧州府鬱林州儒學學正鄭學醇〔承孟，廣東順德縣人，丁卯貢士〕。
陝西西安府盩厔縣儒學教諭曹相〔子良，山西太平縣人，丁卯貢士〕。

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
賢賢易色事父母能竭其力事君能致其
身與朋友交言而有信雖曰未學吾必
謂之學矣
道之不行也我知之矣知者過之愚者不
及也道之不明也我知之矣賢者過之
不肖者不及也人莫不飲食也鮮能知
味也
以善服人者未有能服人者也以善養人
然後能服天下天下不心服而王者未
之有也
===
易
彖曰泰小往大來吉亨則是天地交而萬
物通也上下交而其志同也內陽而外
陰內健而外順內君子而外小人君子
道長小人道消也象曰天地交泰后以
財成天地之道輔相天地之宜以左右
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
賢賢易色，事父母能竭其力，事君能致其身，與朋友交，言而有信。雖曰未學，吾必謂之學矣。
道之不行也，我知之矣：知者過之，愚者不及也。道之不明也，我知之矣：賢者過之，不肖者不及也。人莫不飲食也，鮮能知味也。
以善服人者，未有能服人者也；以善養人，然後能服天下。天下不心服而王者，未之有也。

易
彖曰：「泰，小往大來，吉亨。」則是天地交而萬物通也，上下交而其志同也。內陽而外陰，內健而外順，內君子而外小人，君子道長，小人道消也。象曰：天地交，泰；后以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
"If a man honors the worthy rather than beauty, in serving his parents can exert his utmost strength, in serving his ruler can devote his life, and in his dealings with friends is trustworthy in what he says—though others may say he has not learned, I would certainly say he has learned." [Analects 1.7]
"I know why the Way is not practiced: the wise go beyond it, and the foolish do not reach it. I know why the Way is not understood: the worthy go beyond it, and the unworthy do not reach it. There is no one who does not eat and drink, yet few are able to know the flavors." [Doctrine of the Mean 4]
"One who seeks to subdue others by goodness has never been able to subdue them. One who nourishes others with goodness can thereby subdue the whole world. There has never been anyone who became a true king without the whole world submitting in their hearts." [Mencius 4B.16]

Classic of Changes (Yi)
"The Commentary on the Decision (Tuan) says: 'Peace (Tai): the small departs and the great approaches; good fortune and success.' Thus Heaven and Earth are in communion and the myriad things have free course; the upper and lower are in communion and their wills are the same. The yang is within and the yin is without; strength is within and docility is without; the gentleman is within and the petty man is without. The way of the gentleman waxes and the way of the petty man wanes. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: Heaven and Earth in communion form Peace (Tai). The ruler thereby fashioning and completing the way of Heaven and Earth, and assisting the suitability of Heaven and Earth, so as to aid and guide [the people]…" [Hexagram 11, Tai]

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
民
上九鴻漸于陸其羽可用爲儀吉
易則易知簡則易從
是故君子安而不忘危存而不忘亡治而
不忘亂是以身安而國家可保也
書
帝曰俞允若玆嘉言罔攸伏野無遺賢萬
邦咸寧稽于衆舍己從人不虐無告不
廢困窮惟帝時克
無輕民事惟難無安厥位惟危
===
王敬作所不可不敬德我不可不監于有
夏亦不可不監于有殷
我聞曰至治馨香感于神明黍稷非馨明
德惟馨爾尚式時周公之猷訓惟日孜
孜無敢逸豫凡人未見聖若不克見既
見聖亦不克由聖爾其戒哉爾惟風下
民惟草
詩
punctuated:
民。
上九，鴻漸于陸，其羽可用爲儀，吉。
易則易知，簡則易從。
是故君子安而不忘危，存而不忘亡，治而不忘亂，是以身安而國家可保也。

《書》
帝曰：「俞！允若玆，嘉言罔攸伏，野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。稽于衆，舍己從人，不虐無告，不廢困窮，惟帝時克。」
無輕民事，惟難；無安厥位，惟危。
王敬作所，不可不敬德。我不可不監于有夏，亦不可不監于有殷。
我聞曰：「至治馨香，感于神明。黍稷非馨，明德惟馨。」爾尚式時周公之猷訓，惟日孜孜，無敢逸豫。凡人未見聖，若不克見；既見聖，亦不克由聖。爾其戒哉！爾惟風，下民惟草。

《詩》
translation_en:
… the people.

Top Nine: The wild goose gradually advances to the high plateau. Its feathers can be used for ceremonial ornaments. Auspicious.

With ease, it is easy to know; with simplicity, it is easy to follow.

Therefore, the noble man, when secure, does not forget danger; when preserved, does not forget ruin; when in order, does not forget disorder. Thus his person is secure and the state can be preserved.

Book of Documents (Shu)

The Sovereign said, "Yes! If indeed it be like this, admirable words will nowhere lie hidden, no worthy men will be left neglected in the wilds, and all the myriad states will enjoy peace. To consult with the multitude, to set aside one's own views and follow others, not to oppress the helpless, and not to neglect the distressed and impoverished—only the former sovereign was able to do this."

Do not make light of the affairs of the people; think only of their difficulty. Do not rest at ease in your position; think only of its peril.

May the king make reverence his dwelling place; he must not fail to revere virtue. We must not fail to take as our mirror the lords of Xia, nor must we fail to take as our mirror the lords of Yin.

I have heard it said: "Government at its perfection is a fragrant aroma that moves the spirits. Millet is not the true fragrance; bright virtue alone is the fragrance." May you take as your model these counsels and instructions of the Duke of Zhou, being diligent day by day, and never daring to indulge in ease and pleasure. Ordinary men, before they have seen a sage, feel as though they could never succeed in seeing one; yet having seen a sage, they are still unable to follow the sage. Be on your guard! You are the wind; the common people are the grass.

Book of Odes (Shi)

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
星言夙駕說于桑田
菁菁者莪在彼中陵既見君子錫我百朋
無怨無惡率由羣匹
濬哲維商長發其祥洪水芒芒禹敷下土
方外大國是疆幅隕既長有娀方將帝
立子生商玄王桓撥受小國是達受大
國是達率履不越遂視既發相土烈烈
海外有截帝命不違至于湯齊湯降不
遲聖敬日躋昭假遲遲上帝是祗帝命
式于九圍
===
春秋
秋公會衛侯于桃丘弗遇〔桓公十年〕
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉〔僖公元年〕
晉侯伐衛〔文公元年〕晉陽處父帥師伐楚
以救江〔文公三年〕
公會晉侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯曹伯莒子
邾子滕子薛伯齊世子光吳人鄫人于
punctuated:
星言夙駕，說于桑田。
菁菁者莪，在彼中陵。既見君子，錫我百朋。
無怨無惡，率由羣匹。
濬哲維商，長發其祥。洪水芒芒，禹敷下土方。外大國是疆，幅隕既長。有娀方將，帝立子生商。玄王桓撥，受小國是達，受大國是達。率履不越，遂視既發。相土烈烈，海外有截。帝命不違，至于湯齊。湯降不遲，聖敬日躋。昭假遲遲，上帝是祗，帝命式于九圍。

春秋
秋，公會衛侯于桃丘，弗遇。〔桓公十年〕
八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉。〔僖公元年〕
晉侯伐衛。〔文公元年〕晉陽處父帥師伐楚以救江。〔文公三年〕
公會晉侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、齊世子光、吳人、鄫人于
translation_en:
“When the stars appeared, he ordered his carriage early in the morning, and halted among the mulberry fields.”
“Luxuriant grows the tarragon, in the midst of that large mound. Having seen the noble lord, he bestows upon me a hundred sets of cowries.”
“Giving no cause for resentment or hatred, he follows the example of all his peers.”
“Profoundly wise was Shang, and long had its auspicious signs appeared. When the floodwaters were vast and boundless, Yu spread out the regions of the earth below. The great states beyond he bounded, and the territory became wide and long. Then the house of Yousong began to be great, and God appointed the son of its daughter to give birth to Shang. The Dark King vigorously governed; whether granted a small state he succeeded, or granted a great state he succeeded. He followed the rules of conduct without transgression; wherever he looked, his influence went forth and was answered. Xiangtu was ardent andillustrious, and beyond the seas all was brought into order. The mandate of God did not fail, until in Tang it came to convergence. Tang’s birth was not too late, and his sage reverence daily ascended. His bright virtue reached on high slowly and surely; God on High he revered, and God appointed him to be a model to the nine regions.”

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
“In autumn, the Duke went to meet the Marquis of Wei at Taoqiu, but did not meet him.” [10th year of Duke Huan]
“In the eighth month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and a man of Zhu at Cheng.” [1st year of Duke Xi]
“The Marquis of Jin invaded Wei.” [1st year of Duke Wen] “Yang Chufu of Jin led a force to invade Chu in order to rescue Jiang.” [3rd year of Duke Wen]
“The Duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, Heir Apparent Guang of Qi, a man of Wu, and a man of Zeng at …”

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
戚〔襄公五年〕春公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹
伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊
世子光會吳于柤〔襄公十年〕
禮記
命大師陳詩以觀民風命市納賈以觀民
之所好惡
詩云肅雝和鳴先祖是聽夫肅肅敬也雝
雝和也夫敬以和何事不行爲人君者
謹其所好惡而已矣君好之則臣爲之
上行之則民從之詩云誘民孔易此之
===
謂也
天子有善讓德於天
射之爲言者繹也或曰舍也
第貳場
論
王道本乎人情
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢下州郡檢覈墾田戶口詔〔建武十五〕
punctuated:
戚〔襄公五年〕；春，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光會吳于柤〔襄公十年〕。

禮記
命大師陳詩，以觀民風；命市納賈，以觀民之所好惡。
《詩》云：「肅雝和鳴，先祖是聽。」夫肅肅，敬也；雝雝，和也。夫敬以和，何事不行？爲人君者，謹其所好惡而已矣。君好之，則臣爲之；上行之，則民從之。《詩》云：「誘民孔易。」此之謂也。
天子有善，讓德於天。
射之爲言者，繹也；或曰舍也。

第貳場
論
王道本乎人情。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢下州郡檢覈墾田戶口詔〔建武十五
translation_en:
… at Qi [Fifth year of Duke Xiang]; In spring, the Duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Little Zhu, and Guang, Heir Apparent of Qi, to meet Wu at Zha [Tenth year of Duke Xiang].

Record of Rites (Liji)
He orders the Grand Music Master to present the poems in order to observe the customs of the people; he orders the market अधीक्षक to report prices in order to observe what the people like and dislike.
The Book of Odes says: "Solemn and harmonious are the blended sounds; the ancestors hearken to them." Now "solemn, solemn" means reverence; "harmonious, harmonious" means harmony. When there is reverence coupled with harmony, what enterprise cannot be carried out? He who is a ruler of men simply takes care regarding what he likes and dislikes, and nothing more. What the ruler likes, the ministers will do; what the superior practices, the people will follow. The Book of Odes says: "Guiding the people is very easy." This is what is meant by it.
When the Son of Heaven has some goodness, he yields the credit of the virtue to Heaven.
The word "archery" (she) means "to unfold" (yi); or it is said to mean "to lodge in" (she).

Second Session
Discourse
The Kingly Way is rooted in human feelings.

Edicts, Mandates, and Memorials [One topic to be answered from among these]
An imitation of the Han dynasty edict ordering the regions and commanderies to inspect and verify cultivated land and household population [Fifteenth year of the Jianwu era…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
年
擬唐以韓愈爲京兆尹誥〔長慶三年〕
擬宋御邇英閣講讀寶訓尚書左僕射呂

策〔五道〕
問自昔哲王守成業致盛治者率皆祗遹
先猷動遵成憲所以弘繼序而紹前休
也商周令主克終允德學有緝熙考之

Third Session
Policy Questions [five items]
Question: Since antiquity, wise kings who preserved an established patrimony and brought about flourishing governance have generally all reverently followed the plans of their predecessors and adhered in every action to established statutes; this was how they enlarged the line of succession and continued the fine achievements of the past. As for theworthy rulers of the Shang and Zhou dynasties, who were able to bring their sincere virtue to completion and whose learning had continuous brightness, when we examine what is set forth in the instructions and announcements, they largely attained this by "looking to their meritorious ancestors" and "displaying and extolling their glorious merits" …

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:

神孫萬年之法守者也猗歟盛矣恭惟我
皇上問學日新明習政體自
punctuated: 者爲多。商、周以上，古帝王豈無可法者？而近法厥祖，義乃何居？唐、宋間有進讀十卷《政要》者，有編進《三朝寶訓》者，有願以故事爲楷模者，有見《實錄》欣慕不能釋卷者，有讀《正法》、《謹罰》篇而太息者，有讀《正心》、《剛斷》篇而悅服者。唐、宋又非商、周比也，亦各近述其先，豈所稱「法後王者便」歟？仰惟我二祖開基，列聖纘緒，奎章睿謨載在《寶訓》，神功駿烈紀之《寶錄》，金匱石室所藏，炳若日星，輝映天地，眞足登函三、五，超邁近代，而貽聖子神孫萬年之法守者也，猗歟盛矣！恭惟我皇上問學日新，明習政體，自
translation_en: …for the most part. Above the Shang and Zhou dynasties, how could there be no ancient emperors and kings worthy of emulation? Yet they took as their model their own recent ancestors—what is the meaning behind this? During the Tang and Song dynasties, there were those who presented and read the ten-chapter Essentials of Government (Zhengyao), those who compiled and presented the Precious Instructions of Three Reigns (Sanchao baoxun), those who wished to take dynastic precedents as their standard and model, those who upon seeing the Veritable Records (Shilu) admired them so fondly they could not put the scrolls down, those who sighed deeply upon reading the chapters on "Rectifying the Law" (Zhengfa) and "Prudence in Punishments" (Jinfa), and those who were gladly convinced upon reading the chapters on "Rectifying the Mind" (Zhengxin) and "Resolute Judgment" (Gangduan). Moreover, the Tang and Song were not comparable to the Shang and Zhou, yet each likewise closely followed their own forebears; is this not what is meant by the saying that "it is more convenient to model oneself on the later kings"? Looking up in reverence, we reflect upon how Our Two Progenitors founded the dynastic enterprise and the Successive Sagely Emperors carried on the line of succession: their imperial writings and wise counsels are recorded in the Precious Instructions (Baoxun), and their divine achievements and magnificent exploits are chronicled in the Veritable Records [printed 寶錄 for 實錄]. What is preserved in the golden caskets and stone chambers is as radiant as the sun and stars, illuminating heaven and earth; it is truly sufficient to match and encompass the Three August Ones and Five Emperors, surpass recent eras, and bequeath a standard for our sagely sons and divine grandsons to observe for ten thousand years. Oh, how glorious! Reverently reflecting upon how His Majesty the Emperor renews his inquiry and learning daily and thoroughly understands the principles of governance, apart from…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
講讀經史
裁決章奏外復
俞輔臣所請屬儒臣編輯
累朝訓錄
進講于
文華後殿
垂神諫慕孜孜如有不及郎商周令主何加焉
爾多士欣逢
盛事對揚
===
國美亦嘗獲聞類編所列四十事者而能言
其概乎夫賢者識其大試言
訓錄中大要安在用裨法
祖之治于萬一言果當也執事者將採擇以
獻
問天人相與之際微矣自周武訪雒書于
箕子乃陳洪範庶徵後世言五行者宗
焉兩漢書各本範意作五行志言六沴
之應以五事爲配雜采前古及漢已事
punctuated:
講讀經史、裁決章奏外，復俞輔臣所請，屬儒臣編輯《累朝訓錄》，進講于文華後殿。垂神諫慕，孜孜如有不及，郎商、周令主，何加焉！爾多士欣逢盛事，對揚國美，亦嘗獲聞《類編》所列四十事者，而能言其概乎？夫賢者識其大，試言《訓錄》中大要安在，用裨法祖之治于萬一。言果當也，執事者將採擇以獻。

問：天人相與之際微矣。自周武訪《雒書》于箕子，乃陳《洪範》庶徵，後世言五行者宗焉。《兩漢書》各本《範》意作《五行志》，言六沴之應，以五事爲配，雜采前古及漢已事，
translation_en:
…lecturing on and reading the Classics and Histories, and deciding upon memorials and petitions, He has further approved the request of the Grand Secretaries and charged the Confucian courtiers with compiling the Precious Instructions and Veritable Records of Successive Reigns (Leichao xunlu), to be presented and lectured upon in the Rear Hall of the Hall of Literary Brilliance (Wenhua dian). Fixing His spirit in earnest admiration [? 諫慕, for 欽慕/羨慕], He is tirelessly diligent as if fearing to fall short—even the excellent rulers of the Shang and Zhou dynasties could add nothing to this! You many scholars happily encounter this grand affair and respond by extolling the splendors of the state: have you also been privileged to hear of the forty topics arranged in the Classified Compilation (Leibian), and can you state their general outline? Now, the worthy remember what is of great importance; try to state wherein lies the essential import of the Instructions and Veritable Records, so as to contribute one part in ten thousand to the governance that models itself upon the Ancestors. If your words are indeed fitting, the officials in charge will select them for presentation to the Throne.

Question: The mutual interaction between Heaven and man is subtle indeed. Ever since King Wu of Zhou inquired of Jizi concerning the Luo Writing (Luoshu), whereupon the latter set forth the "Various Verifications" of the "Great Plan" (Hongfan), those in later ages who speak of the Five Phases have taken it as their standard. The History of the Former Han and History of the Later Han (Liang Hanshu) each based themselves on the meaning of the "Great Plan" to compose their "Treatises on the Five Phases" (Wuxing zhi); in speaking of the responses of the six noxious气的 disturbances (li), they matched them with the Five Demeanors, drawing variously from remote antiquity as well as past events of the Han to…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
著必信之徵其說與範合歟然觀漢世
日食地震水旱等詔魏相丙吉鮑昱丁
鴻諸大臣所言與儒者董仲舒劉向之
徒之論彼其君臣未嘗不以五行五事
爲重而精言之也豈漢去古未遠自有
此學作史者特志之歟然宋儒研理乃
稱孔子作春秋不著事應漢儒著事應
者無當于春秋其確論歟姑無論六沴
之說郎𫖯子言五事配五行休咎以類
===
至其文明甚視夫應惟影響貿若草木
之指何如昔有告其君以天變不足懼
第當修人以應之此與公孫僑晏嬰之
論何以異而世乃以爲譏吾以謂言天
不言人誣也知人不知天陋也儒者宜
通天人各以所學著其義于篇
問法者古聖王陶冶人羣之術故弗容廢
也假令法廢則所以整齊約束之者失
其具玆所係非輕尠矣或乃云法僅馭
punctuated:
著必信之徵，其說與《範》合歟？然觀漢世日食、地震、水旱等詔，魏相、丙吉、鮑昱、丁鴻諸大臣所言，與儒者董仲舒、劉向之徒之論，彼其君臣未嘗不以五行、五事爲重，而精言之也。豈漢去古未遠，自有此學，作史者特志之歟？然宋儒研理，乃稱孔子作《春秋》不著事應，漢儒著事應者無當于《春秋》，其確論歟？姑無論六沴之說，郎𫖯子言五事配五行，休咎以類至，其文明甚；視夫應惟影響、貿若草木之指何如？昔有告其君以「天變不足懼，第當修人以應之」，此與公孫僑、晏嬰之論何以異，而世乃以爲譏？吾以謂言天不言人，誣也；知人不知天，陋也。儒者宜通天人，各以所學著其義于篇。
問：法者，古聖王陶冶人羣之術，故弗容廢也。假令法廢，則所以整齊約束之者失其具，玆所係非輕尠矣。或乃云法僅馭
translation_en:
… setting forth verifications that were deemed infallibly trustworthy. Does their doctrine accord with the "Great Plan" (Hongfan)? Yet when we examine the Han-dynasty edicts issued upon solar eclipses, earthquakes, floods, and droughts, the statements of great ministers such as Wei Xiang 魏相, Bing Ji 丙吉, Bao Yu 鮑昱, and Ding Hong 丁鴻, and the discourses of Confucian scholars such as Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒, Liu Xiang 劉向, and their peers, those rulers and ministers never failed to attach great weight to the Five Phases and the Five Demeanors, discussing them in subtle detail. Could it be that because the Han was not yet far removed from antiquity, this learning naturally existed, and the historians merely recorded it? Yet Song-dynasty Confucians, in investigating principle, claimed that when Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), he did not record event-correspondences, and that the Han Confucians who recorded event-correspondences missed the mark of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Is this a definitive judgment? Even setting aside the theory of the six noxious气的 disturbances (liuli), say that the Viscount of Ji (Jizi 箕子) [reading 郎𫖯子 as 卽箕子?] spoke of the Five Demeanors matching the Five Phases, with auspicious and inauspicious signs arriving according to their kind—its text is exceedingly clear; how does it compare with the purport that responses follow like shadow and echo, or that things are as insensate and muddled as grass and trees? In the past, there was one who told his ruler that "celestial anomalies are not worth fearing; one ought merely to cultivate human affairs to respond to them." How does this differ from the arguments of Gongsun Qiao 公孫僑 and Yan Ying 晏嬰, and yet the world criticizes it? I hold that to speak of Heaven without speaking of Man is deceitful, while to know Man without knowing Heaven is shallow. Confucian scholars ought to comprehend both Heaven and Man; let each set forth the meaning of this in his essay according to what he has learned.

Question: Law is the art by which the sage-kings of antiquity molded and governed the multitude, and therefore it cannot be dispensed with. Suppose the law were abolished; then the means of ordering and restraining people would lose its instrument, and what hinges upon this is neither light nor slight. Yet someone says that law merely controls …

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
中材耳豪傑之士不專藉於此其言將
有所據歟往古亡論已三季以來有以
征伐托重謗書至盈篋弗視者有以權
指寄心捐金恣所出弗問者有矯制發
粟不惟不罪反以爲賢者有堅意留田
郎三違璽書不顧卒能成功者此宜非
令甲所有矣而昉之數子果皆豪傑其人歟
惟我
國家當
===
經綸創造之初
風烈嚮臻魁奇泉湧垂鴻熙而樹駿茂者彪
炳鼎彝無不人人豪傑也乃其時
上下一心推誠屬任鼓舞之道亦有出繩約之
外而遠軼前代者歟方
今
聖明在御瑩精太平文武吏士奮炎揚懿率斤
斤効職惟謹毋敢踰寸趾于檢柙之外
斯亦斌濟之盛際已然稍遇緩急輒稱
punctuated: 中材耳，豪傑之士不專藉於此。其言將有所據歟？往古亡論已，三季以來，有以征伐托重，謗書至盈篋弗視者；有以權指寄心，捐金恣所出弗問者；有矯制發粟，不惟不罪，反以爲賢者；有堅意留田，郎三違璽書不顧，卒能成功者。此宜非令甲所有矣，而昉之數子，果皆豪傑其人歟？惟我國家當經綸創造之初，風烈嚮臻，魁奇泉湧，垂鴻熙而樹駿茂者，彪炳鼎彝，無不人人豪傑也。乃其時上下一心，推誠屬任，鼓舞之道，亦有出繩約之外而遠軼前代者歟？方今聖明在御，瑩精太平，文武吏士，奮炎揚懿，率斤斤効職惟謹，毋敢踰寸趾于檢柙之外，斯亦斌濟之盛際已。然稍遇緩急，輒稱…
translation_en:
…men of middling talent, whereas extraordinary heroes do not rely exclusively upon it. Is there any basis for this statement? Leaving remote antiquity aside, since the decline of the Three Dynasties, there was one who entrusted a commander with the weighty charge of a punitive campaign and refused to look at slanderous letters against him even when they filled a whole chest; there was one who confided his strategic designs to a subordinate and bestowed gold upon him to spend at will without asking for an accounting; there was one who forged an imperial decree to distribute grain from the granaries and not only escaped punishment, but was on the contrary regarded as worthy; and there was one who was determined to remain and establish military agricultural colonies, disregarding sealed imperial rescripts three times [note: 郎 here is likely a woodblock/transcription error for 即] and yet ultimately succeeding in his enterprise. Surely none of these actions were provided for in the statutory code! Yet were those several men in whom such deeds originated all truly heroes?

When our own dynasty was at the beginning of its founding and ordering of the realm, heroic spirits gathered in response, and men of towering distinction surged forth like springs. Those who handed down vast splendour and established magnificent achievements are resplendently recorded on the ritual bronzes—every single one of them a hero. Yet at that time, when ruler and ministers were of one mind and positions were entrusted with complete sincerity, did the ways of inspiring and rousing them also go beyond the confines of rules and restraints, far surpassing those of former dynasties?

Right now, the sacred and enlightened Sovereign is on the throne, devoting his pure spirit to Great Peace. Civil and military officials and officers exert their ardour and display their excellence; all are scrupulously diligent in performing their duties, none daring to step an inch outside the bounds of regulations. This too is an era of flourishing and abundant talent. Yet whenever a slight emergency arises, people immediately complain of…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之人何以故或謂奉法于外者未熟悉
德意致綰結太嚴使壞雋韜美議欲少寛文法
間舉漢魏故事偶一行之不識可當於
事機否夫法與人固交用以治也偏任
人則上失其御其弊也肆偏任法則人
無以展其能其弊也拘玆欲以人行法
不以法圍人而人又不敢肆于法何道
而可諸士脫穎在玆其尚評閱品倫銓
裁要極悉著于篇以補苴用材之缺即
他日所自用可知也
===
問方今東南諸郡稱隩區沃壤歲漕挐輸
半出其間此
國家根本地也比年所在災傷上廑
宸慮
特霈渥恩爲發儲行賑蠲積逋以鉅萬計東南
之民仰戴
聖德曠然若更生焉及此時也奉宣
主恩求民疾苦思以厚根本者安在夫昔所病
punctuated:
乏人，何以故？或謂奉法于外者未熟悉德意，致綰結太嚴，使壞雋韜美，議欲少寛文法，間舉漢、魏故事偶一行之，不識可當於事機否？夫法與人固交用以治也。偏任人，則上失其御，其弊也肆；偏任法，則人無以展其能，其弊也拘。玆欲以人行法，不以法圍人，而人又不敢肆于法，何道而可？諸士脫穎在玆，其尚評閱品倫，銓裁要極，悉著于篇，以補苴用材之缺，即他日所自用可知也。

問：方今東南諸郡稱隩區沃壤，歲漕挐輸半出其間，此國家根本地也。比年所在災傷，上廑宸慮，特霈渥恩，爲發儲行賑，蠲積逋以鉅萬計，東南之民仰戴聖德，曠然若更生焉。及此時也，奉宣主恩，求民疾苦，思以厚根本者安在？夫昔所病
translation_en:
…a shortage of capable men—for what reason is this? Some say that those who uphold the laws in the provinces are not thoroughly familiar with His Majesty's benevolent intentions, resulting in restrictions that are overly severe and causing men of extraordinary talent [壤雋 for 瑰雋?] to conceal their virtues. They propose slightly relaxing the letter of the law and occasionally putting into practice precedents from the Han and Wei dynasties; yet we do not know whether this would suit present exigencies. Now, laws and men are inherently used together in governance. If one relies one-sidedly on men, the ruler loses his control, and the resulting abuse is unrestrained license; if one relies one-sidedly on laws, men have no way to display their abilities, and the resulting abuse is rigid constraint. Now, if we wish to use men to carry out the laws, not hem men in with the laws, and yet ensure that men dare not flout the laws, by what way can this be achieved? Gentlemen, your opportunity to distinguish yourselves is right here. May you evaluate the categories and grades of talent, weigh the ultimate essentials, and set them forth fully in your essays to remedy the deficiencies in the employment of talent; from this, how you yourselves will serve in the future may also be known.

Question: At present, the various prefectures of the southeast are renowned as rich regions and fertile soil; half of the annual grain tribute and revenues transported to the capital come from among them. This is the foundational territory of the State. In recent years, natural disasters and crop damage everywhere have aroused the concern of the Imperial Mind. He has specially showered down bountiful grace, releasing grain reserves to carry out relief and remitting accumulated tax arrears amounting to tens of millions. The people of the southeast look up in gratitude to His Sacred Virtue, feeling a vast sense of relief as if given a new lease on life. Availing ourselves of this moment, wherein lies the way to proclaim and spread the Sovereign's grace, inquire into the sufferings of the people, and seek to strengthen the foundation of the realm? As for what formerly afflicted…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
民說者謂墨吏之罰不嚴也郵傳之供
太濫也曩屬軍興額加者未盡去也豪
右齮齕吾民而賦役不平也數年來法
紀肅如郵傳兵廩至有司額外一切歲
歲議裁節且盡賦役竝均豪右無敢冒
濫以逞數者去矣則民宜肥乃瘠更甚
邑里蕭條盜掠多有所以致此曷故焉
將奉行失指
上意不宣歟病民之政有在焉者歟主司者蒿
===
目民艱然不若諸生之習第爲具本末
言之毋以文辭
問立政之要蓋莫急於官人矣
國家三歲而舉士士之入官者率三歲而計
功養之豫而察之詳斯二者交重以佐
治也遡稽隆古人才沛艾而起無盛虞
周然其立法似有可言者虞廷奏績必
加三考乃學校造士自司徒典樂之外
未可詳焉何養之者略而求之者備也
punctuated:
民，說者謂墨吏之罰不嚴也，郵傳之供太濫也，曩屬軍興、額加者未盡去也，豪右齮龕吾民而賦役不平也。數年來，法紀肅如，郵傳、兵廩至有司額外一切，歲歲議裁，節且盡；賦役竝均，豪右無敢冒濫以逞。數者去矣，則民宜肥，乃瘠更甚，邑里蕭條，盜掠多有，所以致此，曷故焉？將奉行失指，上意不宣歟？病民之政有在焉者歟？主司者蒿目民艱，然不若諸生之習，第爲具本末言之，毋以文辭。

問：立政之要，蓋莫急於官人矣。國家三歲而舉士，士之入官者，率三歲而計功。養之豫而察之詳，斯二者交重以佐治也。遡稽隆古，人才沛艾而起，無盛虞、周。然其立法似有可言者：虞廷奏績，必加三考，乃學校造士，自司徒、典樂之外，未可詳焉，何養之者略而求之者備也？
translation_en:
… the people, commentators said that the punishment of corrupt officials was not strict; that the provisions for postal relay stations were too extravagant; that the surcharges added in the past on account of military mobilizations had not been completely eliminated; and that powerful families gnawed away at our common people so that taxes and corvée labor were inequitable. Yet over the past several years, laws and discipline have been strictly enforced. From postal relays and military rations down to all extra-quota exactions by local authorities, reductions have been deliberated year after year until they have been nearly exhausted; taxes and labor services have been equalized together, and powerful families dare not indulge in fraudulent exemptions to get their way. Now that these several evils have been removed, the people ought to be prosperous, yet they are even more impoverished: towns and villages are desolate, and robberies and raids frequently occur. What is the reason that has brought this about? Is it that in carrying out policies their intent has been lost, so that the Sovereign's will is not diffused? Or is it that there are still other policies harmful to the people? Those in charge of this examination look with anxious eyes upon the hardships of the people, yet they are not as familiar with them as you students are. Simply set forth the root and branches of the matter in full, without resorting to mere literary flourish.

Question: In establishing governance, surely nothing is more urgent than appointing men to office. The dynasty recommends scholars every three years, and for scholars who have entered officialdom, their merits are generally evaluated every three years. Nurturing them beforehand and examining them thoroughly afterward—these two aspects are given equal weight in order to assist in governance. Looking back to high antiquity, men of talent arose in splendid abundance, never more flourishing than under Yu [Shun] and the Zhou. Yet regarding the laws they established, there seems to be room for discussion. At the court of Yu, when achievements were reported, three triennial evaluations were invariably conducted; yet as for training scholars in schools, apart from the Minister of Education (situ) and the Director of Music (dianyue), the details cannot be known. Why was the nurturing of men so sketchy while what was demanded of them was so exhaustive?

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
周以六德六行貢士于鄉歷試而後詔
王授之爵秩至其肆朝之典僅見于六
計弊羣吏察之之略而舉之之詳又曷
故焉將無互有詳略係其時歟抑自有
交重而不偏者歟周以後法以世殊漢
之三目六條唐之三由四善九等二十
七最宋之貢舉制科相兼審官考課並
設視古即不逮然其沿革之槩有可考
鏡者歟抑亦互有詳略否歟夫師虞憲
===
周損益近代以求眞才需時用則
今制稱大備已其詳可稱述歟說者猶謂人
才漸不逮古百執事未盡得人將
今之法亦有稍異于古歟抑行之久而失實
也茲欲養士者皆爲可用得士者皆藉
其實用則奚施而可士且舉于有司任
事有日試酌古儀今言舉士課吏之道
俾官人者有稽焉此亦士所挾持而欲
展也
punctuated: 周以六德、六行貢士于鄉，歷試而後詔王授之爵秩；至其肆朝之典，僅見于六計弊羣吏。察之之略而舉之之詳，又曷故焉？將無互有詳略，係其時歟？抑自有交重而不偏者歟？周以後，法以世殊：漢之三目、六條，唐之三由、四善、九等、二十七最，宋之貢舉、制科相兼，審官、考課並設，視古即不逮，然其沿革之槩有可考鏡者歟？抑亦互有詳略否歟？夫師虞、憲周，損益近代，以求眞才、需時用，則今制稱大備已，其詳可稱述歟？說者猶謂人才漸不逮古，百執事未盡得人，將今之法亦有稍異于古歟？抑行之久而失實也？茲欲養士者皆爲可用，得士者皆藉其實用，則奚施而可？士且舉于有司，任事有日，試酌古儀今，言舉士課吏之道，俾官人者有稽焉。此亦士所挾持而欲展也。
translation_en: Under the Zhou, scholars were presented for tribute from the local districts on the basis of the Six Virtues and Six Conducts, and only after undergoing successive trials was the King petitioned to confer ranks and emoluments upon them; yet as for the statutes of their court assessments, these are seen only in the use of the Six Criteria to evaluate the host of officials. Why, in turn, was the scrutiny of them so brief while the selection of them was so detailed? Could it be that this mutual alternation of detail and brevity depended upon the times? Or was there in fact a balanced emphasis without bias in each? After the Zhou, the institutions varied from age to age: the Three Categories and Six Articles of the Han; the Three Origins, Four Virtues, Nine Grades, and Twenty-Seven Superlatives of the Tang; and the Song system of combining tribute examinations with decree examinations while simultaneously establishing the Bureau of Personnel Evaluation and the Bureau of Merit Ratings—even if these do not match antiquity, can the general outline of their evolution and reforms be examined as a mirror for governance? Or did they too alternate between detail and brevity? Now, taking the Yu as our teacher and the Zhou as our model, while adapting the practices of recent eras so as to seek true talent to meet the needs of the time, our present institutions may already be called grandly complete; can their particulars be recounted? Yet commentators still say that talent gradually falls short of antiquity, and that the百執事 (various administrative offices) have not entirely found the right men. Could it be that our present laws also differ slightly from those of antiquity? Or is it that after being practiced for a long time they have lost their substance? If we now wish that all who nurture scholars render them fit for use, and that all who obtain scholars rely upon their practical utility, what measures should be put into effect to achieve this? You scholars are about to be recommended by the authorities, and the day when you will assume office is not far off; try to deliberate upon antiquity and take the measure of the present, and speak of the way of selecting scholars and evaluating officials, so that those charged with appointing men to office may have something to consult. This, too, is what you scholars cherish within yourselves and wish to unfold.

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
賢賢易色事父母能竭其力事君能致其
身與朋友交言而有信雖曰未學吾必
謂之學矣
陸化淳

以實勝者也如是而與其爲學也夫何疑子夏
以爲世之學者貴聞見而人之論學者亦曰多

translation_en:
First Session.

Four Books.

"If a man esteems the worthy instead of beauty; if in serving his parents he is able to exert his utmost strength; if in serving his ruler he is able to devote his life; and if in his dealings with friends his words are trustworthy—though men may say he has not learned, I would certainly say that he has learned."

By Lu Huachun 陸化淳.

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Cao comments: 〔Stripped of all flowery verbiage, retaining only fundamental substance; this is a writing that rejects superficiality and returns〕 to simplicity. A successful scholar.

Examiner and Senior Compiler Shen comments: 〔Refined and classical, worthy of serving as a model.〕
Examiner and Left Admonisher Shen comments: 〔Able to grasp the spirit of the passage.〕

When the worthy discusses learning, he grants recognition to those who possess genuine learning. Now, fulfilling human relationships with sincerity is where learning excels through substance; to grant that one who acts thus is learned—what doubt could there be? Zixia 子夏 considered that learners in the world value what is heard and seen, and those who discuss learning likewise say, "Hear much, and that is learning; see much, and that is learning." As I speak of it, learning does not merely refer to hearing and seeing; it refers to illuminating human relationships and truly possessing them within oneself. title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之賢而易其好色之心親吾之親而竭其得爲
之力其事君惟知有君不知有身也其處友相
示以情弗載以僞也斯人也即吾所謂學者也
蓋人紀克脩則學識其大君子之誦詩讀書以
求不愧于人者如是焉而已其多聞與否弗論
也躬行已至則道有諸身君子之日就月將以
求盡乎所性者如是焉而已其多見與否弗論
也故見其學也未見其行也人謂之學吾不敢
遽以爲學也見其行也因論其學也雖曰未學
===
吾必謂之學矣彼有學其所學者豈吾所謂學
也歟此子夏示學者以務實也然亦非子夏之
言也三代之學以明人倫夫子曰躬行君子吾
未有得蓋本之此也子夏以文學名豈廢學者
而以此立訓其亦古尚行之意歟夫有博文約
禮會倫之精以立人極者又不但可謂之學吾
以爲學之至也斯子夏不言之意也
道之不行也我知之矣知者過之愚者不
及也道之不明也我知之矣賢者過之
punctuated:
之賢，而易其好色之心；親吾之親，而竭其得爲之力；其事君，惟知有君，不知有身也；其處友，相示以情，弗載以僞也。斯人也，即吾所謂學者也。蓋人紀克脩，則學識其大；君子之誦詩讀書，以求不愧于人者，如是焉而已，其多聞與否，弗論也。躬行已至，則道有諸身；君子之日就月將，以求盡乎所性者，如是焉而已，其多見與否，弗論也。故見其學也，未見其行也，人謂之學，吾不敢遽以爲學也；見其行也，因論其學也，雖曰未學，吾必謂之學矣。彼有學其所學者，豈吾所謂學也歟？此子夏示學者以務實也。然亦非子夏之言也，三代之學以明人倫，夫子曰「躬行君子，吾未有得」，蓋本之此也。子夏以文學名，豈廢學者？而以此立訓，其亦古尚行之意歟！夫有博文約禮，會倫之精，以立人極者，又不但可謂之學，吾以爲學之至也。斯子夏不言之意也。
道之不行也，我知之矣：知者過之，愚者不及也。道之不明也，我知之矣：賢者過之，
translation_en:
… the worthiness of others and replaces his fondness for beauty with it; who cherishes his own parents and exhausts whatever strength he is capable of; who, in serving his ruler, knows only that he has a ruler and not that he has a self; and who, in associating with friends, reveals his true feelings to them and carries no falsehood. Such a person is precisely what I call a man of learning. For when the bonds of human relationships are successfully cultivated, one's learning grasps what is great. When a gentleman recites the Odes and reads the Documents in seeking not to feel ashamed before others, it comes down to nothing more than this; whether he has heard much or not is beside the point. When personal practice has reached its utmost, the Way is possessed within oneself. When a gentleman makes daily progress and monthly advances in seeking to fulfill his innate nature, it comes down to nothing more than this; whether he has seen much or not is beside the point. Therefore, if I see a man's estudiar [learning] but have not yet seen his conduct, though others may call it learning, I dare not hastily regard it as learning. If I see his conduct and from that judge his learning, even if it is said he has not studied, I will certainly say he has learned! As for those who merely study what they call learning, how could that be what I call learning?

In this way Zixia 子夏 showed learners that they must attend to substance. Yet these were not merely Zixia's own words. The schools of the Three Dynasties were meant to clarify human relationships, and when the Master said, "Living the life of a gentleman in my own person is something I have not yet attained," his words were rooted in this same principle. Zixia was renowned for literature and scholarship—how could he have been one to discard learning? That he established his teaching by these words reflects the ancient intent of valuing conduct above all. Moreover, if there is someone who broadens himself with culture and restrains himself with ritual, grasping the essence of human relationships so as to establish the ultimate standard of humanity, he can not only be called a man of learning—I would consider his the perfection of learning. This is the unstated meaning of Zixia's words.

"I know why the Way is not practiced: the wise go beyond it, and the foolish do not reach it. I know why the Way is not understood: the worthy go beyond it, …"

味也
王士騏

人以不察而失之寧獨其稟之偏乎中庸述夫
子之言曰人受天命之中以生而率之爲道焉
自此中鮮能于民而道之不明不行久矣亦知
其故乎蓋力行常始于能知而真知尤得于能
行道之不行非獨失之行也我知其由于知之
punctuated:

道之弊於人也，由其不察焉。夫道無過不及也，人以不察而失之，寧獨其稟之偏乎？《中庸》述夫子之言曰：人受天命之中以生，而率之爲道焉。自此中鮮能于民，而道之不明不行久矣，亦知其故乎？蓋力行常始于能知，而真知尤得于能行。道之不行，非獨失之行也，我知其由于知之
translation_en:
…and the degenerate do not come up to it. There is no one who does not eat and drink, yet few are able to know the flavor.”

Wang Shiqi 王士騏

Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Deng 鄧 comments: 〔The structure is natural, and both diction and reasoning are well-realized. The second half of the essay especially grasps the fundamental purport; reciting it makes the meaning leap to life.〕
Associate Examiner, Instructor Wang 王 comments: 〔The personal realization of the meaning is genuine and earnest, and the diction is moreover elegant and pure. Selected.〕
Associate Examiner, Instructor Cong 從 comments: 〔It brings out the purport of the theme with refined thoroughness, while its bearing is serene, elegant, and unhurried—surely a scholar who understands the Way.〕
Associate Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng) Zheng 鄭 comments: 〔Washing away ornate artifice, he directly pours forth his unadorned nature. It is recorded here to show the many scholars how to [curb?] [?] superficiality.〕
Examiner, Senior Compiler (xiuzhuan) Shen 沈 comments: 〔Concise and unpretentious.〕
Examiner, Left Admonisher (zuo zanshan) Shen 沈 comments: 〔Of great elegance.〕

That the Way suffers impairment among men stems from their failure to examine it. Now, in the Way itself there is neither going beyond nor failing to come up; when men lose it through failing to examine it, how could this be due solely to the partiality of their natural endowments? The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) recounts the Master’s words, saying: Man receives the Mean of Heaven’s decree at birth, and following it constitutes the Way. Ever since this Mean has rarely been practiced among the people, the Way has long ceased to be understood or practiced—yet do they know the reason for this? For strenuous practice always begins with the ability to know, and true knowledge is especially attained through the ability to practice. That the Way is not practiced is not merely a failure of practice; I know that it stems from knowledge…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
過不及焉知者窮高視道無足行者而愚者識
卑又不知所當行也各持其所見道何待而行
乎道之不明非獨失之知也我知其由于行之
過不及焉賢者抗行視道無足知者而不肖者
才弱又不求所當知也各溺于所守道何待而
明乎是人也均之離乎道矣而道豈離於人哉
故夫道者日用飲食也人不得無以生也道之
有中是飲食中之味也人鮮能察而知也精微
寓於平淡之中而過求者常失真易簡自有無
===
窮之味而循習者多不著此其所以過不及也
夫道亦何難明與行之有吁試一反求則習而
察矣中固渾然在焉而知與行合矣大抵世所
取常在賢知而騁其才智害道乃滋甚聖人至
與愚不肖同類而譏非過也然賢知常欲出聖
人上聖人自視每出衆人下故菽粟尚其用大
羹尚其眞至味無異味焉夫聖人之用中亦以
此
以善服人者未有能服人者也以善養人
punctuated:
過不及焉。知者窮高，視道無足行者；而愚者識卑，又不知所當行也。各持其所見，道何待而行乎？道之不明，非獨失之知也，我知其由于行之過不及焉。賢者抗行，視道無足知者；而不肖者才弱，又不求所當知也。各溺于所守，道何待而明乎？是人也，均之離乎道矣，而道豈離於人哉？故夫道者，日用飲食也，人不得無以生也。道之有中，是飲食中之味也，人鮮能察而知也。精微寓於平淡之中，而過求者常失真；易簡自有無窮之味，而循習者多不著。此其所以過不及也。夫道亦何難明與行之有？吁！試一反求，則習而察矣，中固渾然在焉，而知與行合矣。大抵世所取常在賢知，而騁其才智，害道乃滋甚。聖人至與愚不肖同類而譏，非過也。然賢知常欲出聖人上，聖人自視每出衆人下。故菽粟尚其用，大羹尚其眞，至味無異味焉。夫聖人之用中，亦以此。

「以善服人者，未有能服人者也。以善養人，
translation_en:
…going too far or falling short. The wise strain toward the lofty and regard the Way as containing nothing worth practicing; while the foolish are lowly in insight and do not even know what ought to be practiced. With each clinging to his own view, how can the Way ever come to be practiced? That the Way is not made clear is not merely a failure of knowledge; I know that it comes from practice going too far or falling short. The worthy exalt their conduct and regard the Way as containing nothing worth knowing; while the unworthy are weak in talent and do not even seek what ought to be known. With each mired in what he holds to, how can the Way ever be made clear? Such men have alike departed from the Way—yet how could the Way depart from men? For the Way is like daily eating and drinking, without which men cannot live; and the Mean within the Way is like the flavor within eating and drinking, which few are able to discern and know. Subtlety resides within plainness, yet those who seek too far often lose its truth; ease and simplicity naturally possess an inexhaustible flavor, yet those who merely follow routine rarely become aware of it. This is why people go too far or fall short. What difficulty, then, is there in making the Way clear and practicing it? Alas! If one but turns to seek it within oneself, one will practice it with discernment; the Mean is inherently present in its wholeness, and knowledge and practice are united. On the whole, what the world values is usually the worthy and the wise, yet when they give free rein to their talents and intelligence, the harm done to the Way grows all the worse. That the Sage went so far as to class them together with the foolish and the unworthy in his criticism was no exaggeration. Yet the worthy and the wise constantly wish to rise above the Sage, whereas the Sage in his own eyes always places himself below ordinary men. Thus beans and grain are prized for their utility, and the unseasoned sacrificial broth is prized for its genuineness: the supreme flavor is no exotic flavor. It was in this spirit, too, that the Sage practiced the Mean.

"One who seeks to subdue men by goodness has never been able to subdue them. Only when one nourishes men with goodness…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
然後能服天下天下不心服而王者未
之有也
方嶽

〔剖晰幾微善形容王道氣象是以錄之〕

人君服天下而王惟其公天下以善也蓋以善
養人則其心公故能服天下而王也而謂私已
===
者能乎哉孟子意曰人知力之不足以服人也
而用善以服之以爲惟善足以屈人不善也然
而不能也存一私已之心人且病吾之私也有
能服人者否也存一上人之心人亦爭處其上
也有能服人者否也必也以善養人者則不但
服人也而能服天下又不但服力也而能服其
心閔人之不善而汲汲引翼之若父母于子也
亦何意服之也而至公所感天下歸心焉有不
自爲德而民徧德者斯王業之所由一統乎樂
punctuated:
然後能服天下。天下不心服而王者，未之有也。
方嶽

人君服天下而王，惟其公天下以善也。蓋以善養人，則其心公，故能服天下而王也；而謂私已者能乎哉？孟子意曰：人知力之不足以服人也，而用善以服之，以爲惟善足以屈人不善也。然而不能也。存一私已之心，人且病吾之私也，有能服人者否也？存一上人之心，人亦爭處其上也，有能服人者否也？必也以善養人者，則不但服人也，而能服天下；又不但服力也，而能服其心。閔人之不善而汲汲引翼之，若父母于子也，亦何意服之也？而至公所感，天下歸心，焉有不自爲德而民徧德者？斯王業之所由一統乎！樂
translation_en:
… Only then can he win the submission of the world. It has never happened that one became a True King without the world submitting in its heart.

By Fang Yue 方嶽.

Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Wang, comments: [The distinction between the True King and the Hegemon begins in how one establishes one's mind. This essay alone is able to dissect the subtle beginnings and aptly portray the spirit of the Kingly Way; therefore I have selected it.]
Examiner, Senior Compiler Shen, comments: [Vigorous and mature; without wasting words, the meaning penetrates thoroughly. An excellent piece.]
Examiner, Left Admonisher Shen, comments: [Clear and smooth.]

A ruler wins the submission of the world and becomes a True King solely because he shares goodness impartially with the world. For when one nurtures others with goodness, one's mind is impartial, and therefore one can win the submission of the world and reign as a True King. How could anyone claim that someone who acts out of selfish regard for himself is capable of this?

Mencius's meaning is this: People know that force is insufficient to make others submit, and so they use goodness to make them submit, supposing that goodness alone suffices to bend others' lack of goodness into submission. Yet they cannot succeed. If one harbors a mind of selfish regard for oneself, others will resent one's selfishness—has anyone ever been able to make others submit like this? If one harbors a mind set on surpassing others, others too will compete to place themselves above one—has anyone ever been able to make others submit like this?

Only he who nurtures others with goodness not only wins the submission of individuals, but can win the submission of the whole world; and he not only wins the submission of their strength, but can win the submission of their hearts. Pitying others' lack of goodness, he urgently guides and supports them, just like parents toward their children—what intention does he have of making them submit? Yet moved by his supreme impartiality, the world turns its heart to him; so there comes to be one who does not count his own kindness as a favor, while the people universally receive his virtue. Is this not how the enterprise of the True King achieves unification? Delighting in…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
人之有善而孳孳成就之若天地于物也亦何
意服之也而一念所孚羣心丕應焉有不自爲
大能成其大者斯王道之所爲無外乎借曰天
下不心服而王者未之有也夫服人而至于心
服而後爲服人之深善能使天下心服而後滿
吾善之量此惟公善者能之而私者不能也公
私之辨豈獨力與善之間哉雖然太上知有之
次親之譽之人親譽我者我投以迹也無意則
忘忘則人亦忘我焉而天下化斯治古之極而
養之至乎然在所自養矣
===
易
象曰泰小往大來吉亨則是天地交而萬
物通也上下交而其志同也內陽而外
陰內健而外順內君子而外小人君子
道長小人道消也象曰天地交泰后以
財成天地之道輔相天地之宜以左右
民
王士騏
punctuated:
人之有善，而孳孳成就之，若天地于物也，亦何意服之也？而一念所孚，羣心丕應焉。有不自爲大、能成其大者，斯王道之所爲無外乎！借曰「天下不心服而王者」，未之有也。夫服人而至于心服，而後爲服人之深；善能使天下心服，而後滿吾善之量。此惟公善者能之，而私者不能也。公私之辨，豈獨力與善之間哉？雖然，太上知有之，次親之譽之。人親譽我者，我投以迹也；無意則忘，忘則人亦忘我焉，而天下化。斯治古之極，而養之至乎！然在所自養矣。

易
「《象》曰：『泰，小往大來，吉亨。』則是天地交而萬物通也，上下交而其志同也。內陽而外陰，內健而外順，內君子而外小人，君子道長，小人道消也。《象》曰：天地交，泰；后以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。」
王士騏
translation_en:
… when others possess goodness, and tirelessly brings it to completion, just as heaven and earth treat all things—what intention is there of subduing them? Yet through the sincerity of a single thought, the hearts of the multitude grandly respond. When one does not consider oneself great and thus is able to achieve greatness, is this not why the Kingly Way has nothing outside it? Even if one were to say that someone attained true kingship without the world being subdued in heart—such a thing has never existed. Now, only when subduing others reaches the point of subduing their hearts is it a profound subduing of others; only when goodness is able to make the whole world subdued in heart does it fulfill the full measure of our goodness. Only one who makes goodness public can do this, whereas one who is selfish cannot. Is the distinction between public-mindedness and selfishness merely that between force and goodness? Even so, of the highest ruler, the people merely know that he exists; of the next, they draw near to him and praise him. That people draw near to and praise me is because I present them with visible traces; when there is no deliberate intention, one forgets, and when one forgets, others likewise forget me, and the world is transformed. Is this not the pinnacle of ancient governance and the ultimate perfection of nourishing others? Yet it all depends on how one nourishes oneself.

Book of Changes (Yi)
"The Commentary on the Decision [printed as Commentary on the Images (Xiang)] says: 'Peace (Tai): the small departs and the great approaches; auspicious and亨 (pervasive success).' This means that heaven and earth are in communion and the myriad things move freely; above and below are in communion and their will is the same. The yang is within and the yin is without; strength is within and compliance is without; the noble man is within and the petty man is without. The way of the noble man waxes, and the way of the petty man wanes. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: 'Heaven and earth are in communion: Peace (Tai). Thus the sovereign regulates and completes the way of heaven and earth, and furthers and assists the suitability of heaven and earth, so as to aid the people.'"
By Wang Shiqi 王士騏

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭曹　批〔簡而莊無一剩語〕
同考試官學正祝　批〔雄渾典雅治世之文〕
同考試官教授錢　批〔格莊詞雅想見泰和氣象〕
考試官修撰沈　批〔聯絡得體〕
考試官左賛善沈　批〔健朗〕
觀泰之象象而見天人之相成焉夫泰之時天
人之盛際也元后有賛化之治而泰其頼以成
乎甞謂天地開聖人之先聖人終天地之功此
世所爲稱隆也吾於泰之象象見焉象則謂夫
===
卦以乾坤交而爲泰是二氣訢合泰和在宇宙
矣君相同心泰和在廟堂矣由是陽者健者君
子者其道常得以自伸浸隆浸昌胥爲君子可
也陰者順者小人者其道不得以自肆浸消浸
亡盡無小人可也此以謂之小往大來而吉亨
也然天非人不成人非天不因故象又謂當此
泰交之會元后者宜握其權而致太平焉天地
交矣不有沕穆未開者乎裁成其道以制所不
能辨而民志以啓萬物通矣不有生養未周者
punctuated:
同考試官教諭曹　批〔簡而莊，無一剩語。〕
同考試官學正祝　批〔雄渾典雅，治世之文。〕
同考試官教授錢　批〔格莊詞雅，想見泰和氣象。〕
考試官修撰沈　批〔聯絡得體。〕
考試官左賛善沈　批〔健朗。〕

觀《泰》之《象》、《象》，而見天人之相成焉。夫泰之時，天人之盛際也。元后有賛化之治，而泰其頼以成乎！甞謂天地開聖人之先，聖人終天地之功，此世所爲稱隆也，吾於《泰》之《象》、《象》見焉。《象》則謂夫卦以乾坤交而爲《泰》，是二氣訢合，泰和在宇宙矣；君相同心，泰和在廟堂矣。由是陽者、健者、君子者，其道常得以自伸，浸隆浸昌，胥爲君子可也；陰者、順者、小人者，其道不得以自肆，浸消浸亡，盡無小人可也。此以謂之「小往大來」而「吉亨」也。然天非人不成，人非天不因。故《象》又謂當此泰交之會，元后者宜握其權而致太平焉。天地交矣，不有沕穆未開者乎？裁成其道，以制所不能辨，而民志以啓。萬物通矣，不有生養未周者
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Cao comments: 〔Concise and dignified, without a single superfluous word.〕
Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Zhu comments: 〔Vigorous and classic in elegance; prose of a well-governed age.〕
Associate Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Qian comments: 〔Dignified in form and refined in diction; one can envision an atmosphere of great harmony.〕
Examiner and Senior Compiler Shen comments: 〔Cohesively connected and fitting in style.〕
Examiner and Left Admonisher Shen comments: 〔Vigorous and clear.〕

By observing the Commentary on the Judgment [transcribed as 象 for 彖] and the Commentary on the Images of the hexagram Tai (Peace), one sees how Heaven and Man bring each other to completion. Now, the time of Tai is the flourishing juncture of Heaven and Man. The great sovereign exercises governance that assists transformation, and is it not upon this that Tai relies for its completion? It has been said that Heaven and Earth open the way before the sage, and the sage brings to completion the work of Heaven and Earth; this is why an era is praised as flourishing, and I see this in the Commentary on the Judgment and the Commentary on the Images of Tai.

The Commentary on the Judgment [象] states that the hexagram forms Tai through the interaction of Qian and Kun: thus the two vital forces joyfully unite, and great harmony prevails throughout the universe; sovereign and minister are of one mind, and great harmony prevails in the court. Consequently, the yang, the vigorous, and the noble man are constantly able to extend their Way—gradually flourishing and prospering, until all may become noble men; the yin, the compliant, and the petty man are unable to indulge their Way—gradually diminishing and vanishing, until there may be no petty men left at all. This is why it is called "the small departs and the great approaches," resulting in "good fortune and success."

Yet Heaven is not brought to completion without Man, and Man has nothing to build upon without Heaven. Therefore, the Commentary on the Images further states that at this juncture of harmonious interaction, the great sovereign ought to grasp his authority and bring about grand peace. Heaven and Earth interact, yet is there not that which remains profound, indistinct, and undifferentiated? He regulates and completes their Way in order to institutionally define what they cannot distinguish on their own, and thereby the minds of the people are enlightened. The myriad things flourish in communication, yet is there not that in which nourishment and sustenance remain incomplete…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
乎輔相其宜以補所不能爲而民用以利斯時
也上下所爲同心君子所稱道長者要以贊化
育而安民生耳然則天下之泰豈不在一人也
哉故合觀彖象而知泰運者天啓人泰治者人
成天天人交相成也蓋唐虞三代泰相仍也至
後世而無泰豈乏時哉人鮮裁成輔相之能而
補苴以爲日天無如人何也上志娛樂下志寵
利有一念在天地生民乎故秦漢以下邪正互
消長天亦否泰半矣
===
是故君子安而不忘危存而不忘亡治而
不忘亂是以身安而國家可保也
沈天啓
同考試官教諭曹　批〔苞桑之戒得是作而益明〕
同考試官學正祝　批〔語意警策是有關繫文字〕
同考試官教授錢　批〔切直之言思深之旨〕
考試官修撰沈　批〔善言保治意〕
考試官左贊善沈　批〔俊拔〕
君子所以保業者以其戒心勝也甚矣先事之
punctuated:
乎？輔相其宜，以補所不能爲，而民用以利。斯時也，上下所爲同心，君子所稱道長者，要以贊化育而安民生耳。然則天下之泰，豈不在一人也哉！故合觀彖、象，而知泰運者天啓人，泰治者人成天，天人交相成也。蓋唐、虞、三代，泰相仍也；至後世而無泰，豈乏時哉？人鮮裁成輔相之能，而補苴以爲日，天無如人何也。上志娛樂，下志寵利，有一念在天地生民乎？故秦、漢以下，邪正互消長，天亦否、泰半矣。

「是故君子安而不忘危，存而不忘亡，治而不忘亂，是以身安而國家可保也。」
沈天啓
同考試官教諭曹　批〔苞桑之戒，得是作而益明。〕
同考試官學正祝　批〔語意警策，是有關繫文字。〕
同考試官教授錢　批〔切直之言，思深之旨。〕
考試官修撰沈　批〔善言保治意。〕
考試官左贊善沈　批〔俊拔。〕

君子所以保業者，以其戒心勝也。甚矣，先事之
translation_en:
… Have the myriad things not yet been fully nurtured and sustained? He assists and regulates what is fitting among them to supplement what they cannot do for themselves, so that the people's livelihoods are benefitted. At this time, what motivates superior and inferior to be of one mind, and what the superior men call the waxing of their Way, is in essence simply to assist the transforming and nourishing powers of nature and to give peace to the people's livelihoods. This being so, does the great peace (Tai) of the world not rest upon the One Man alone! Therefore, viewing the Judgment (Tuan) and the Image (Xiang) together, we know that as for the fortune of Tai, Heaven opens the way for man, and as for the governance of Tai, man brings Heaven's work to completion; Heaven and man mutually complete one another. Indeed, during the ages of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, eras of Tai succeeded one another. When later ages lacked such peace, was it for want of the right time? Rather, men rarely possessed the ability to fashion and complete, to assist and regulate; they merely patched things together to get through the day, and Heaven could do nothing about man. When those above set their minds on pleasure and amusement, and those below set their minds on favor and profit, is there a single thought given to Heaven, Earth, and the living people? Thus from the Qin and Han dynasties onward, the crooked and the upright have alternately waxed and waned, and Heaven too has been half in obstruction (Pi) and half in peace (Tai).

"Therefore the superior man, when secure, does not forget danger; when preserved, does not forget ruin; when in a state of order, does not forget disorder. Thus his person is kept safe and the state and family can be preserved."
By Shen Tianqi 沈天啓.
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Cao 曹, comments: [The admonition of binding to the bushy mulberry becomes all the clearer through this composition.]
Associate Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng) Zhu 祝, comments: [The wording and meaning are incisive and admonitory; this is a piece of writing of genuine consequence.]
Associate Examiner, Prefectural Instructor (jiaoshou) Qian 錢, comments: [Earnest and forthright words, with a message of deep thought.]
Examiner, Senior Compiler (xiuzhuan) Shen 沈, comments: [Well expresses the meaning of preserving good order.]
Examiner, Left Admonisher (zuo zanshan) Shen 沈, comments: [Outstanding and elevated.]

The reason the superior man is able to preserve his patrimony is that his sense of caution prevails. Extreme indeed is the…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
戒不可忘也能戒則患不及身而國家其可保
矣夫子觀於否泰之際以爲治道不遠治心實
難心有所不忘則制否泰在我矣今夫安危存
亡治亂之間每同途而迭變此心爲之樞焉是
故君子知危生于安常居安而慮危不忘危焉
知存或可亡常處存而念亡不忘亡焉知亂伏
于治常當治而憂亂不忘亂焉身在尊安也而
畏天難諶憂勤常廑于夙宵不敢一日諱式微
之事國家泰寧也而畏命難保禍敗若起於旦
===
夕不敢須臾弛儆惕之防君子之心如此是以
祗畏之誠格乎上下足以祈天而保民倚伏之
慮精于幾微足以銷萌而杜隙殷憂故無憂而
德福萃于厥躬身其安矣無逸乃能逸而基緒
綿於奕世國家可保矣然則安其位者以不忘
危也保其存者以不忘亡也有其治者以不忘
亂也易戒苞桑不忘之謂也歟大抵天下神器
未嘗暫靜聖賢比之朽索馭馬蹈虎尾涉春冰
危亦至矣昔秦隋皆極盛之天下一朝而解何
punctuated: 戒不可忘也！能戒則患不及身，而國家其可保矣。夫子觀於否泰之際，以爲治道不遠，治心實難；心有所不忘，則制否泰在我矣。今夫安危、存亡、治亂之間，每同途而迭變，此心爲之樞焉。是故君子知危生于安，常居安而慮危，不忘危焉；知存或可亡，常處存而念亡，不忘亡焉；知亂伏于治，常當治而憂亂，不忘亂焉。身在尊安也，而畏天難諶，憂勤常廑于夙宵，不敢一日諱式微之事；國家泰寧也，而畏命難保，禍敗若起於旦夕，不敢須臾弛儆惕之防。君子之心如此。是以祗畏之誠格乎上下，足以祈天而保民；倚伏之慮精于幾微，足以銷萌而杜隙。殷憂故無憂，而德福萃于厥躬，身其安矣；無逸乃能逸，而基緒綿於奕世，國家可保矣。然則安其位者，以不忘危也；保其存者，以不忘亡也；有其治者，以不忘亂也。《易》戒苞桑，不忘之謂也歟！大抵天下神器，未嘗暫靜，聖賢比之朽索馭馬、蹈虎尾、涉春冰，危亦至矣。昔秦、隋皆極盛之天下，一朝而解，何…
translation_en: …precaution before the fact must never be forgotten! If one can be cautious, calamity will not reach one's person, and the state can be preserved. The Master observed the juncture between stagnation and prosperity and considered that while the way of governance is not far off, governing the mind is truly difficult; when the mind holds fast to what it does not forget, then control over stagnation and prosperity rests with us. Now, security and danger, survival and ruin, order and disorder frequently share the same path and alternate with one another, and this mind serves as the pivot. Therefore, the noble man knows that danger is born of security, so while dwelling in security he always contemplates danger, never forgetting danger; he knows that what survives may perish, so while situated in survival he always bears ruin in mind, never forgetting ruin; he knows that disorder lurks within order, so while in a time of order he always worries about disorder, never forgetting disorder. Though his person is in a position of exalted security, he stands in awe of a Heaven that is hard to trust, his anxious diligence is ever-present day and night, and he dares not for a single day諱 shun speaking of decline; though the state is in peace and tranquility, he fears that the Mandate is difficult to preserve, acting as though disaster and defeat might arise between morning and evening, and he dares not for a single moment relax the defenses of vigilance and wariness. Such is the mind of the noble man. Therefore, the sincerity of his reverent awe reaches above and below, sufficient to pray to Heaven and protect the people; his contemplation of how fortune and misfortune rely on and ambush each other is refined down to the subtlestincipient signs, sufficient to melt away buds of trouble and close up rifts. Because of deep anxiety he ends without anxiety, and virtue and blessing gather upon his person—thus his person is secure; because he takes no ease he is able to enjoy ease, and the foundational lineage extends for generations—thus the state can be preserved. This being so, he who makes his position secure does so by not forgetting danger; he who preserves his survival does so by not forgetting ruin; he who maintains his order does so by not forgetting disorder. When the Book of Changes (Yi) warns of "tying to a cluster of mulberry shoots," is it not speaking of never forgetting? On the whole, the sacred vessel of the empire is never quiet even for a moment; sages and worthies compared it to driving horses with rotten reins, treading on a tiger's tail, or crossing spring ice—the danger is extreme indeed. In the past, Qin and Sui were both empires at the height of flourishing, yet in a single morning they disintegrated; why…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
也失在恃恃則忘而不測者乘之故知明君之
慮在衆所易忘而曰其亡其亡乃善言乂安極
治者也
書
帝曰俞允若玆嘉言罔攸伏賢無遺賢萬
邦咸寧稽于衆舍已從人不虐無告不
廢困窮惟帝時克
沈學
同考試官教諭萬　批〔詞意精深得克艱之旨〕
同考試官推官徐　批〔體裁莊重語意峻潔〕
===
考試官修撰沈　批〔老成〕
考試官左贊善沈　批〔精約〕
聖君廣克艱之道而歸之前聖焉蓋惟聖人爲
能不自易也克艱之道而可易言哉帝舜有契
於禹謨故言曰君臣乃萬化之原艱難爲政理
之本旨哉克艱之謨信能此道矣特政乂民化
已乎吾見聽納宏而羣策兼收有揚而無伏焉
官使公而黎獻共臣有用而無遺焉政教同而
punctuated:
也？失在恃。恃則忘，而不測者乘之。故知明君之慮，在衆所易忘，而曰「其亡其亡」，乃善言乂安極治者也。

書
「帝曰：『俞！允若玆，嘉言罔攸伏，野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。稽于衆，舍已從人，不虐無告，不廢困窮，惟帝時克。』」
沈學
同考試官教諭萬　批〔詞意精深，得克艱之旨。〕
同考試官推官徐　批〔體裁莊重，語意峻潔。〕
考試官修撰沈　批〔老成。〕
考試官左贊善沈　批〔精約。〕

聖君廣克艱之道，而歸之前聖焉。蓋惟聖人爲能不自易也，克艱之道，而可易言哉？帝舜有契於禹謨，故言曰：君臣乃萬化之原，艱難爲政理之本。旨哉，克艱之謨！信能此道矣，特政乂民化已乎？吾見聽納宏而羣策兼收，有揚而無伏焉；官使公而黎獻共臣，有用而無遺焉；政教同而
translation_en:
… was that? Their failure lay in presumption. When one is presumptuous, one forgets danger, and the unforeseen takes advantage of it. Thus we know that the concern of an enlightened ruler lies in what the multitude easily forgets, and that saying "What if it be lost! What if it be lost!" is truly the best way to speak of lasting peace and supreme order.

Book of Documents (Shu)

"The Emperor said, 'Yes! Truly, if it be like this, then good words will nowhere be hidden, no worthy men will be left overlooked in the wilds [text has 賢 for 野], and all the myriad states will enjoy peace. But to consult with the multitude, to set aside one's own views and follow others, not to oppress the helpless, and not to neglect the distressed and impoverished—only the Emperor Yao was able to do this.'"

Shen Xue 沈學

Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Wan commented: 〔The wording and meaning are profound and precise, grasping the essential purport of "appreciating the difficulties."〕
Associate Examiner, Prefectural Judge (tuiguan) Xu commented: 〔The style and structure are dignified and grave; the language and thought are lofty and pure.〕
Examiner, Senior Compiler (xiuzhuan) Shen commented: 〔Mature and accomplished.〕
Examiner, Left Admonisher (zuo zanshan) Shen commented: 〔Refined and concise.〕

The sage ruler broadens the Way of appreciating the difficulties of rule and attributes its realization to the former sage. Indeed, only a sage is capable of not taking things lightly himself; how then could the Way of appreciating difficulties be lightly spoken of? Because Emperor Shun found himself in deep accord with the counsels of Yu, he spoke thus: Ruler and minister are the source of the myriad transformations, and appreciating difficulties is the foundation of governance and order. How meaningful is this counsel on appreciating difficulties! If one truly practices this Way, will the result merely be that governance is ordered and the people transformed? Rather, I see that when a ruler's receptiveness to advice is broad, all counsels are gathered in together—they are brought forth and never hidden away; when appointment to office is impartial, the wise among the multitude all serve as ministers—they are employed and never left overlooked; and when governance and instruction are unified, …

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
萬民得所有安而無危焉朝廷邦國泰道熈然
其一新而效固若斯之大也然言非苟聽之而
已必樂取如自已出而後嘉猷可達焉民非苟
仁之而已必哀矜切于窮民而後羣生可安焉
賢非苟用之而已必求賢逮乎側陋而後衆正
可集焉人已士庶精誠渾然其悉貫而事豈可
以易言也爲其事獲其效艱者乃克矣其惟帝
乎恭讓夙成每懷乎若時若采之益哲惠兼至
不病於知人安民之難此真所謂克艱厥后者
===
哉吁舜不自謂能也而歸美于堯克艱之實亦
可想矣抑世常有願治之君而賢人不親民生
寡遂其人主不自知難讜言不進而以天下娛
也帝堯稽衆舍已有如不及誠念官材民隱非
通言路不可耳噫斯又克艱之本歟
王敬作所不可不敬德我不可不監于有
夏亦不可不監于有殷
王廷實
同考試官教諭萬　批〔格正調高旨融詞綵〕
punctuated:
萬民得所，有安而無危焉。朝廷邦國，泰道熈然其一新，而效固若斯之大也。然言非苟聽之而已，必樂取如自已出，而後嘉猷可達焉；民非苟仁之而已，必哀矜切于窮民，而後羣生可安焉；賢非苟用之而已，必求賢逮乎側陋，而後衆正可集焉。人已士庶，精誠渾然其悉貫，而事豈可以易言也！爲其事，獲其效，艱者乃克矣，其惟帝乎！恭讓夙成，每懷乎若時若采之益；哲惠兼至，不病於知人安民之難。此真所謂「克艱厥后」者哉！吁，舜不自謂能也，而歸美于堯，克艱之實亦可想矣。抑世常有願治之君，而賢人不親，民生寡遂，其人主不自知難，讜言不進，而以天下娛也。帝堯稽衆舍已，有如不及，誠念官材民隱，非通言路不可耳。噫，斯又克艱之本歟！

「王敬作所，不可不敬德。我不可不監于有夏，亦不可不監于有殷。」
王廷實
同考試官教諭萬　批〔格正調高，旨融詞綵〕
translation_en:
… the myriad people all find their proper place, enjoying peace without peril. At court and throughout the realm, the Way of great peace shines forth in complete renewal—such is the magnitude of its efficacy! Yet as for words of counsel, one does not merely listen to them perfunctorily; one must delight in adopting them as though they had come from oneself, and only then can fine plans be carried through. As for the people, one does not merely treat them with perfunctory benevolence; one must feel earnest compassion for the destitute, and only then can all living beings be brought to peace. As for the worthy, one does not merely employ them perfunctorily; one must seek out worthies even among the obscure and humble, and only then can the host of upright men be gathered together. Between oneself and others, between officials and commoners, utmost sincerity seamlessly pervades all—how could such an undertaking be spoken of lightly! To carry out the undertaking and reap its results, thereby overcoming its difficulties—was this not achieved by the Sovereign Yao alone? Reverent and yielding from an early age, he constantly cherished the benefits of conforming to the times and attending to affairs; combining wisdom and kindness in full measure, he did not falter at the difficulty of knowing men and giving peace to the people. This is truly what is meant by "the sovereign being able to attend to the difficulties of his position"! Ah, Shun did not claim this ability for himself, but attributed the glory to Yao; from this, the true substance of attending to difficulties can also be imagined. Yet in the world there are often rulers who wish for good governance, and still worthy men are not drawn close and the people's livelihoods are rarely fulfilled; this is because the ruler himself does not recognize the difficulty, upright words are not presented, and he takes the empire as his plaything. Sovereign Yao consulted the multitude and set aside his own views as though he could never do enough, truly mindful that appointing men of talent and understanding the people's hidden sufferings were impossible without keeping the path of remonstrance open. Alas, is this not furthermore the very root of attending to difficulties?

"May the King make reverence his dwelling place; he cannot but be reverent of virtue. We cannot fail to take the Xia dynasty as our mirror, nor can we fail to take the Yin dynasty as our mirror."
By Wang Tingshi 王廷實.
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Wan 萬, comments: 〔The structure is upright and the tone lofty; the meaning is harmonious and the diction brilliant.〕

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官推官徐　批〔發居敬監古意明徹〕
考試官修撰沈　批〔詞意蒼然〕
考試官左賛善沈　批〔奘健〕
大臣惕王之敬德而示以所當監焉夫君德以
敬爲本也監於夏殷而益知敬之不可以已也
召公告成王之意曰天下之治在君身人君之
德大居敬王何以責臣爲哉亦有居敬而已大
國不敢言侈而無逸以宅其基元子不敢言尊
而有嚴以立其極臨御事如其所以對皇天而
===
兢兢乎與俱焉斯須之不敬秉之而大觀虧矣
不可也撫庶殷如其所以毖上下而翼翼乎與
游焉幾微之不敬絫之而化原塞矣不可也王
亦何所監乎先我而王者夏也殷所代也我之
一監也不監則胡所戒而玩心以生我亦夏矣
我不可不監於有夏焉先我而王者殷也周所
代也我之又一監也不監則胡所懲而懼心以
息我亦殷矣我不可不監於有殷焉有所惕然
深省於理亂興亡之際斯有所惺然常存於起
punctuated:
同考試官推官徐　批〔發居敬監古意明徹〕
考試官修撰沈　批〔詞意蒼然〕
考試官左賛善沈　批〔奘健〕

大臣惕王之敬德，而示以所當監焉。夫君德以敬爲本也，監於夏、殷，而益知敬之不可以已也。召公告成王之意，曰：天下之治在君身，人君之德大居敬。王何以責臣爲哉？亦有居敬而已。大國不敢言侈，而無逸以宅其基；元子不敢言尊，而有嚴以立其極。臨御事如其所以對皇天，而兢兢乎與俱焉，斯須之不敬秉之，而大觀虧矣，不可也。撫庶殷如其所以毖上下，而翼翼乎與游焉，幾微之不敬絫之，而化原塞矣，不可也。王亦何所監乎？先我而王者夏也，殷所代也，我之一監也。不監則胡所戒而玩心以生，我亦夏矣，我不可不監於有夏焉。先我而王者殷也，周所代也，我之又一監也。不監則胡所懲而懼心以息，我亦殷矣，我不可不監於有殷焉。有所惕然深省於理亂興亡之際，斯有所惺然常存於起
translation_en:
Associate Examiner, Prefectural Judge Xu, comments: [It brings out the meaning of dwelling in reverence and mirroring antiquity with clarity and penetration.]
Examiner, Senior Compiler Shen, comments: [The diction and intent have a venerable depth.]
Examiner, Left Admonisher Shen, comments: [Vigorous and robust.]

The great minister arouses the king to revere virtue and shows him what he ought to take as a mirror. Now, the ruler's virtue takes reverence as its foundation; by taking the Xia and Yin as mirrors, one knows all the more that reverence cannot be ceased. Such was the meaning of the Duke of Shao's announcement to King Cheng, saying: The governance of all under Heaven lies in the person of the ruler, and in the virtue of the ruler of men, nothing is greater than dwelling in reverence. Why should Your Majesty merely place demands upon your ministers? It is simply a matter of dwelling in reverence as the sole pursuit. Possessing a great state, one dares not speak of extravagance, but through freedom from idleness establishes its foundation; as the eldest son of Heaven, one dares not speak of exalted status, but through majestic severity sets up the supreme standard. In approaching the affairs of rule, let it be as when facing August Heaven, tremblingly cautious in keeping company with it; if a single moment's lack of reverence takes hold, the great spectacle of rule is impaired—this must not be! In pacifying the multitudinous people of Yin, let it be as when showing caution toward the spirits above and below, reverently careful in moving among them; if the slightest trace of irreverence accumulates, the source of moral transformation is blocked—this must not be! And what should Your Majesty take as a mirror? Those who ruled as kings before us were the Xia, whom the Yin replaced; they are our first mirror. If we do not mirror ourselves in them, whereby shall we take warning? A trifling mind will arise, and we too shall become like the Xia; we cannot fail to mirror ourselves in the lords of Xia. Those who ruled as kings before us were the Yin, whom the Zhou replaced; they are our next mirror. If we do not mirror ourselves in them, whereby shall we be chastened? A fearful mind will subside, and we too shall become like the Yin; we cannot fail to mirror ourselves in the lords of Yin. When there is that by which one is alarmingly moved to deep reflection upon the juncture of order and disorder, rise and fall, then there is that by which one remains alertly and constantly mindful amidst…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
居動靜之間不可不監于二代其可以不敬德
乎吁望王敬德諴民之意至矣抑召公誥王言
敬言監言夏殷必再三其說人主冲年未諳往
事遊佚淫樂不知可憂監往徵來存法戒焉嗚
呼自有宇宙非一代也人主柰何弗敬哉
詩
無怨無惡率由羣匹
陸化淳
同考試官教諭鄧　批〔造意清深摛文醇雅〕
===
同考試官教諭王　批〔發純心任賢意盡矣〕
同考試官教諭從　批〔明融雅健殆非經生語〕
同考試官學正鄭　批〔莊雅純粹聲詩之優者〕
考試官修撰沈　批〔俊潔〕
考試官左賛善沈　批〔明整〕
詩人願君嗣之用賢不以己與之也夫怨惡而
有己則私矣忌之以用賢斯德其至乎詩人以
是荅梟鷖有以也且人君之所與共治者惟賢
而其所以用賢者惟心爲王嫡嗣者其必崇假
punctuated:
居動靜之間。不可不監于二代，其可以不敬德乎？吁！望王敬德諴民之意至矣。抑召公誥王，言敬、言監、言夏殷，必再三其說。人主冲年，未諳往事，遊佚淫樂，不知可憂，監往徵來，存法戒焉。嗚呼！自有宇宙，非一代也，人主柰何弗敬哉？

詩
無怨無惡，率由羣匹。
陸化淳
同考試官教諭鄧　批〔造意清深，摛文醇雅。〕
同考試官教諭王　批〔發純心任賢，意盡矣。〕
同考試官教諭從　批〔明融雅健，殆非經生語。〕
同考試官學正鄭　批〔莊雅純粹，聲詩之優者。〕
