詩人願君嗣之用賢，不以己與之也。夫怨惡而有己，則私矣；忌之以用賢，斯德其至乎！詩人以是荅《梟鷖》，有以也。且人君之所與共治者，惟賢；而其所以用賢者，惟心。爲王嫡嗣者，其必崇《假
translation_en:
…daily life, in action and in rest. Since he must not fail to take the two dynasties as his mirror, how could he fail to revere virtue? Alas! His earnest hope that the king would revere virtue and bring harmony to the people was utmost indeed. Moreover, when the Duke of Shao (Shao Gong 召公) admonished the king, in speaking of reverence, of taking a mirror, and of the Xia and Yin dynasties, he invariably repeated his points two or three times. When a ruler is in his young years and not yet familiar with past affairs, he may indulge in idleness and excessive pleasure without knowing what is to be worried about; by mirroring the past to verify the future, one preserves models and warnings therein. Alas! Since the universe began, there has been more than a single dynasty—how could a ruler not be reverent?

Classic of Poetry (Shijing 詩經)
"Bearing no resentment, harboring no hatred, he follows the lead of all his peers."
By Lu Huachun 陸化淳.
Associate Examiner Instructor Deng 鄧 comments: [The conception is clear and profound, the composition pure and elegant.]
Associate Examiner Instructor Wang 王 comments: [In bringing forth the idea of entrusting worthies with a pure heart, the meaning is fully exhausted.]
Associate Examiner Instructor Cong 從 comments: [Lucid, harmonious, elegant, and vigorous—hardly the words of an ordinary examinee in the Classics.]
Associate Examiner Director of Studies Zheng 鄭 comments: [Dignified, elegant, and pure—an outstanding specimen among the essays on the Odes.]
Examiner Senior Compiler Shen 沈 comments: [Refined and incisive.]
Examiner Left Admonisher Shen 沈 comments: [Clear and well-ordered.]

The poet wishes for the royal heir to employ the worthy without letting his own self interfere in it. Now, if in resentment and hatred one allows the self to intrude, that is partiality; to abstain from [?] such feelings in order to employ the worthy—is this not the perfection of virtue! That the poet responded with this to the ode "Wild Ducks" (Fuyi 鳧鷖 [written 梟鷖]) was with good reason. Furthermore, those with whom a ruler shares in governing are none other than the worthy, and that whereby he employs the worthy is none other than his mind. title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
樂之範而興賢宅俊不以一己之私守宜人
之法而闢誠布公于以弘大君之度怨不以天
下之公者爲私怨私怨起則任使之際有顚錯
而拂經者非所以率由羣匹也當秩秩抑抑之
隆將正大之情通乎天地而豈其有是乎惡不
以天下之公者爲私惡私惡起則堂陛之間有
隔閡而弗通者非所以率由羣匹也當穆穆皇
皇之時將泰交之美同乎天地而豈其有是乎
位有小大而慶讓黜陟惟其公焉雖毀言日至
而無所容心見有異同而都俞吁咈惟其當焉
===
雖逆耳日聞而不以介意蓋羣匹所共者天位
吾奉天以率由之而已矣所治者民事吾爲民
以率由之而已矣夫奚怨惡之有哉此弼德凝
命之道而假樂詩人所以爲王嗣願也雖然是
道也養之貴豫不自今始也其在儲貳之際乎
道之以德義則德義道之以法律則法律幾固
不可不愼也古人之述君德曰其爲太子也朝
于嬰齊而夕于側也有味乎其言之此無怨無
punctuated: 樂之範，而興賢宅俊，不以一己之私；守宜人之法，而闢誠布公，于以弘大君之度。怨不以天下之公者爲私怨，私怨起則任使之際有顚錯而拂經者，非所以率由羣匹也。當秩秩抑抑之隆，將正大之情通乎天地，而豈其有是乎？惡不以天下之公者爲私惡，私惡起則堂陛之間有隔閡而弗通者，非所以率由羣匹也。當穆穆皇皇之時，將泰交之美同乎天地，而豈其有是乎？位有小大，而慶讓黜陟惟其公焉，雖毀言日至而無所容心；見有異同，而都俞吁咈惟其當焉，雖逆耳日聞而不以介意。蓋羣匹所共者天位，吾奉天以率由之而已矣；所治者民事，吾爲民以率由之而已矣。夫奚怨惡之有哉？此弼德凝命之道，而《假樂》詩人所以爲王嗣願也。雖然，是道也，養之貴豫，不自今始也，其在儲貳之際乎！道之以德義則德義，道之以法律則法律，幾固不可不愼也。古人之述君德，曰：「其爲太子也，朝于嬰齊而夕于側也。」有味乎其言之！此「無怨無…
translation_en: …model of the ode "Jia Le" (Felicitous and Joyous), elevating the worthy and placing theeminent in office without acting out of personal bias; he must uphold the way of "ordering well the people," opening his heart in sincerity and extending impartiality, thereby broadening the magnanimity of a great ruler. As for resentment, he does not turn what is public under Heaven into private resentment; if private resentment arises, then in appointing and employing officials there will be confusion, error, and violation of constant principles, which is not the way to follow and rely upon the host of peers. At the height of orderly and cautious virtue, his upright and great sentiments will communicate with Heaven and Earth—how could there be anything like this? As for dislike, he does not turn what is public under Heaven into private dislike; if private dislike arises, then between the throne hall and the steps below there will be estrangement and a lack of communication, which is not the way to follow and rely upon the host of peers. In an age of solemn and majestic splendor, the beauty of harmonious communion between ruler and ministers will equal that of Heaven and Earth—how could there be anything like this? Offices may be great or small, yet rewards, reprimands, demotions, and promotions are determined solely by impartiality; even if slanderous words arrive daily, he harbors no prejudice in his mind. Views may agree or differ, yet expressions of assent and dissent in council are judged solely by their appropriateness; even if words unpleasant to the ear are heard daily, he takes no offense. For what the host of peers share in common are the offices ordained by Heaven, and I merely revere Heaven in following and relying upon them; what they govern are the affairs of the people, and I merely act for the sake of the people in following and relying upon them. What resentment or dislike could there possibly be? This is the Way of assisting virtue and consolidating the Mandate, and it is what the poet of "Jia Le" wished for the royal heir. Even so, as for this Way, cultivating it requires foresight and does not begin only today—must it not take place when one is still the Heir Apparent? Guide him with virtue and righteousness, and he will turn to virtue and righteousness; guide him with laws and regulations, and he will turn to laws and regulations—the subtle beginnings must indeed be treated with caution! When the ancients recounted a ruler's virtue, they said: "When he was Heir Apparent, in the morning he was with Yingqi, and in the evening he was with Ce." How meaningful are these words! This is the root of "having neither resentment nor…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
畟率由羣匹之本也
濬哲維商長發其祥洪水芒芒禹敷下土
方外大國是疆幅隕既長有娀方將帝
立子生商玄王桓撥受小國是達受大
國是達率履不越遂視既發相土烈烈
海外有截帝命不違至于湯齊湯降不
遲聖敬日躋昭假遲遲上帝是祗帝命
式于九圍
華鈺
===
同考試官教諭鄧　批〔規摹宏壯語意超然〕
同考試官教諭王　批〔詞簡意足殆難復加〕
同考試官教諭從　批〔體格平雅思致縝密〕
同考試官學正鄭　批〔宏深簡古頌義斯備〕
考試官修撰沈　批〔善作長題者〕
考試官左賛善沈　批〔簡勁〕
有商以德受命歷觀三后可知也夫德者凝命
之本也觀三后之受命而世德之祥遠矣哉此
祫祭之所以歌也且一代天命非至德不承非
punctuated:
畟，「率由羣匹」之本也。

「濬哲維商，長發其祥。洪水芒芒，禹敷下土方。外大國是疆，幅隕既長。有娀方將，帝立子生商。玄王桓撥，受小國是達，受大國是達。率履不越，遂視既發。相土烈烈，海外有截。帝命不違，至于湯齊。湯降不遲，聖敬日躋。昭假遲遲，上帝是祗，帝命式于九圍。」
華鈺
同考試官教諭鄧批：〔規摹宏壯，語意超然。〕
同考試官教諭王批：〔詞簡意足，殆難復加。〕

有商以德受命，歷觀三后可知也。夫德者，凝命之本也。觀三后之受命，而世德之祥遠矣哉！此祫祭之所以歌也。且一代天命，非至德不承，非
translation_en:
… [恶][?] and “following all his peers.”

“Profoundly wise was Shang, and long had its auspicious signs been manifested. When the floodwaters were vast and boundless, Yu laid out the lands below in the four quarters. The great states beyond he bordered, and the territory became wide and long. Then the house of Yousong began to wax great, and the Lord on High established the son of its daughter to give birth to Shang. The Dark King vigorously governed; whether granted a small state, he brought it to success, or whether granted a great state, he brought it to success. He followed the path of礼 without transgression; wherever one looked, his influence was already manifest. Xiangtu was blazingly glorious, and beyond the seas all was brought into order. The mandate of the Lord on High never departed, down to the time when Tang came into full accord with it. Tang’s birth was not too late, and his sagely reverence daily ascended. His bright spirit reached on high unceasingly; the Lord on High he revered, and the Lord on High commanded him to be a model to the nine regions.” [Book of Odes, Shang Hymns, “Changfa”]

Hua Yu 華鈺

Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Deng comments: [Grand and magnificent in scale; transcendent in diction and conception.]
Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Wang comments: [Concise in wording yet full in meaning; one could scarcely add anything more.]
Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Cong comments: [Balanced and elegant in form; meticulous in thought.]
Associate Examiner Department Director of Studies Zheng comments: [Vast, profound, concise, and ancient in style; the meaning of the hymn is fully realized here.]
Examiner Senior Compiler Shen comments: [One who excels at composing on long topics.]
Examiner Left Admonisher Shen comments: [Concise and vigorous.]

That the house of Shang received the Mandate through virtue can be known by examining its three sovereigns in succession. Truly, virtue is the foundation for consolidating the Mandate. When we observe how the three sovereigns received the Mandate, how far-reaching were the auspicious signs of their hereditary virtue! This is why it was sung at the collective ancestral sacrifice (xia). Moreover, the Mandate of Heaven for a dynasty cannot be received without supreme virtue, nor…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
厚積不發我商則太和以萃世有濬哲之君景
命攸屬久兆興王之業成之者湯不自湯也傳
之者相土不自相土也蓋自禹甸既平之餘有
娀方將之際商室已造而玄王立矣玄王以桓
桓之德而著爲身教則小國大國罔不敬應焉
帝命之所以基也相土以烈烈之武而布之四
方則薄海內外罔不齊一焉帝命之所以延也
至乎成湯則生當聖作之期而天眷之有常者
適合維新之會德極昭格之至而聖敬之日躋
===
者益乎簡在之心實始作君師而式九圍焉帝
命之所以集其成也夫由湯而上則濬哲之德
奕世有光由契而下則長發之祥保世滋大登
歌之際敢忘所自哉雖然是詩也非徒侈祖德
而已也亦以垂後王之鑒焉蓋廟貌一啓則承
糦者四方執玉帛者萬國於斯之際主鬯受釐
易生侈心矣祖德之頌其亦著累世之艱難見
天命之不易乎故曰亦以垂後王之鑒也
春秋
punctuated:
厚積不發。我商則太和以萃，世有濬哲之君；景命攸屬，久兆興王之業。成之者湯，不自湯也；傳之者相土，不自相土也。蓋自禹甸既平之餘、有娀方將之際，商室已造，而玄王立矣。玄王以桓桓之德而著爲身教，則小國大國罔不敬應焉，帝命之所以基也。相土以烈烈之武而布之四方，則薄海內外罔不齊一焉，帝命之所以延也。至乎成湯，則生當聖作之期，而天眷之有常者適合維新之會；德極昭格之至，而聖敬之日躋者益乎簡在之心，實始作君師而式九圍焉，帝命之所以集其成也。夫由湯而上，則濬哲之德奕世有光；由契而下，則長發之祥保世滋大。登歌之際，敢忘所自哉？雖然，是詩也，非徒侈祖德而已也，亦以垂後王之鑒焉。蓋廟貌一啓，則承糦者四方，執玉帛者萬國，於斯之際，主鬯受釐，易生侈心矣。祖德之頌，其亦著累世之艱難，見天命之不易乎？故曰亦以垂後王之鑒也。

《春秋》
translation_en:
… deep accumulation, it does not burst forth. In our Shang dynasty, supreme harmony has gathered, so generation after generation there have been rulers of profound wisdom; where the great mandate belongs, it has long portended the enterprise of a rising king. He who brought it to completion was Tang, yet it did not begin with Tang; he who transmitted it was Xiangtu, yet it did not begin with Xiangtu. For ever since the lands ordered by Yu were pacified and the House of Yousong was just beginning to prosper, the House of Shang was already founded, and the Dark King [Xie] was established. When the Dark King manifested his martial virtue as personal instruction, the small states and large states alike responded with reverence—this is how the Sovereign's mandate was laid as a foundation. When Xiangtu spread hisblazing martial prowess to the four quarters, within and beyond the four seas all were brought into uniformity—this is how the Sovereign's mandate was extended. Coming down to Tang the Successful, he was born at a time when a sage was due to arise, and Heaven's constant favor coincided with the juncture of renewal; his virtue reached the utmost of bright communion with Heaven, and his sage reverence, ascending daily, further answered to the selective mind of the Sovereign [? reading 益乎 as 溢乎 or 契乎]. Thus he truly first became ruler and teacher and served as a model to the nine regions—this is how the Sovereign's mandate was brought to its grand completion. Tracing upward from Tang, the virtue of profound wisdom shone across successive generations; tracing downward from Xie, the auspiciousness that had long been manifest preserved the generations and grew ever greater. At the moment of ascending to sing this ode, how could one dare forget whence it came? Even so, this ode does not merely extol the virtue of the ancestors; it also hands down a mirror of warning for later kings. For once the ancestral temple is opened, those presenting sacrificial millet come from the four quarters, and those holding jade and silk number ten thousand states; at such a juncture, presiding over the fragrant sacrificial wine and receiving the blessings of the spirits, it is easy for a boastful heart to arise. Does not the eulogy of ancestral virtue also set forth the hardships of cumulative generations and show that the Mandate of Heaven is not easily kept? Therefore it is said that it also hands down a mirror of warning for later kings.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉
僖公元年
方嶽
同考試官訓導王　批〔發振威意明悉殆盡〕
考試官修撰沈　批〔筆勁格壯〕
考試官左贊善沈　批〔嚴整〕
伯主勤貳以振威其念之深可予也蓋威不振
則安攘之勢不張齊伯之念及此其成功也宜
哉且夫鄭中國之樞也南向則楚重東向則齊
===
重楚之敢于爭鄭者以華風之弗競而伯威之
未伸也桓公識明管仲多才其籌兹也審矣用
是因楚人伐鄭而于檉之會講焉糾合列辟共
爲勤恤之圖倡率友邦咸切簡書之畏謂門庭
之寇方亟不可以莫之禦也則思所以摧其鋒
而壇坫之間有勝筭謂懿親之禍方殷不可以
莫之拯也則思所以縫其闕而帷幄之内有壯
猷蓋所謀者雖止於一鄭而隱然有奪人之聲
所合者雖止於五國而赫然有難犯之勢不待
punctuated:
「八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉。」（僖公元年）
方嶽
同考試官訓導王　批：〔發振威意，明悉殆盡。〕
考試官修撰沈　批：〔筆勁格壯。〕
考試官左贊善沈　批：〔嚴整。〕

伯主勤貳以振威，其念之深可予也。蓋威不振，則安攘之勢不張。齊伯之念及此，其成功也宜哉！且夫鄭，中國之樞也。南向則楚重，東向則齊重。楚之敢于爭鄭者，以華風之弗競，而伯威之未伸也。桓公識明，管仲多才，其籌兹也審矣。用是因楚人伐鄭，而于檉之會講焉。糾合列辟，共爲勤恤之圖；倡率友邦，咸切簡書之畏。謂門庭之寇方亟，不可以莫之禦也，則思所以摧其鋒，而壇坫之間有勝筭；謂懿親之禍方殷，不可以莫之拯也，則思所以縫其闕，而帷幄之内有壯猷。蓋所謀者雖止於一鄭，而隱然有奪人之聲；所合者雖止於五國，而赫然有難犯之勢。不待
translation_en:
"In the eighth month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and a representative of Zhu at Cheng." (First year of Duke Xi)
By Fang Yue 方嶽.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Wang: [He brings out the idea of rousing prestige clearly and exhaustively.]
Comment by Examiner and Senior Compiler Shen: [Vigorous brush and grand structure.]
Comment by Examiner and Left Admonisher Shen: [Strict and well-ordered.]

When the Hegemon exerts himself on behalf of a wavering state in order to rouse his prestige, the depth of his concern is worthy of praise. For if prestige is not roused, the momentum for pacifying the interior and repelling the exterior cannot be expanded. Once the Hegemon of Qi turned his thoughts to this, how fitting it was that he achieved success! Moreover, Zheng was the pivot of the Central States. If it leaned south, Chu gained weight; if it leaned east, Qi gained weight. That Chu dared to contend for Zheng was because the ethos of the Central States was not competitive and the Hegemon's prestige had not yet been extended. Duke Huan had clear insight and Guan Zhong had abundant talent; their planning for this matter was thorough indeed. Therefore, occasioned by the people of Chu invading Zheng, the covenant meeting at Cheng was held. Bringing together the various rulers, they jointly formed plans for diligent relief; leading the friendly states, all keenly felt reverence for the bamboo dispatches calling for aid. Saying that the bandits at the courtyard gate were pressing hard and could not be left unresisted, they pondered how to break their vanguard, and amidst the covenant altar and banquet stands there were winning calculations; saying that the calamity of a close royal kinsman was at its height and could not be left unrescued, they pondered how to mend the breach, and within the command tent there were grand counsels. Thus, although what they planned for was limited to a single state of Zheng, there was implicitly a reputation that stripped the enemy of spirit; although those whom they united were limited to five states, there was awe-inspiringly a momentum difficult to violate. One did not need to wait until…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
陘亭厚集苞茅致詰而後知之矣噫于幽萃冠
裳之好志非不同也而積衰之風未奮純門逌
襲仇之師義非弗著也而華夏之氣未舒豈若
玆會也謀協於同仇而威振於外攘其事爲尤
偉也哉以桓仲君臣之經營於始者其念之深
若是顧伐陳之役又何其罔念耶良由量淺而
器不宏也嘗觀管仲之言曰功成者隳名成者
虧至其告桓公也亦拳拳於持盈守成之道乃
三歸之侈躬自蹈之又奚以匡其君怗楚之後
震矜萌而叛者九國固其所也故曰王道之外
無坦途舉皆荆棘仁義之外無功利舉皆險巇
諒哉
===
晉侯伐衞〔文公三年〕晉陽處父帥師伐楚
以救江〔文公三年〕
湯一龍
同考試官訓導王 批〔莊嚴典古 經學無踰此者〕
考試官修撰沈 批〔文有斷制〕
考試官左贊善沈 批〔古雅〕
punctuated:
陘亭厚集、苞茅致詰而後知之矣。噫！于幽萃冠裳之好，志非不同也，而積衰之風未奮；純門逌襲仇之師，義非弗著也，而華夏之氣未舒。豈若玆會也，謀協於同仇，而威振於外攘，其事爲尤偉也哉！以桓、仲君臣之經營於始者，其念之深若是，顧伐陳之役，又何其罔念耶？良由量淺而器不宏也。嘗觀管仲之言曰：「功成者隳，名成者虧。」至其告桓公也，亦拳拳於持盈守成之道。乃三歸之侈，躬自蹈之，又奚以匡其君？怗楚之後，震矜萌而叛者九國，固其所也。故曰：「王道之外無坦途，舉皆荆棘；仁義之外無功利，舉皆險巇。」諒哉！

晉侯伐衞〔文公三年〕晉陽處父帥師伐楚以救江〔文公三年〕
湯一龍
同考試官訓導王批〔莊嚴典古，經學無踰此者〕
考試官修撰沈批〔文有斷制〕
考試官左贊善沈批〔古雅〕
translation_en:
… wait until the massive muster at Xingting and the reprimand over the tribute of wrapped sedge to recognize it. Alas! When the covenant at You gathered the amity of cap and gown, their aims were not unaligned, yet the spirit of long-accumulated decline had not been roused; when the expedition at Chunmen marched against an invading foe, righteousness was not unmanifest, yet the vigor of the central Chinese states had not yet been unleashed. How could they compare to this meeting, where counsels were united against a common enemy and prestige vibrated in repelling foreign aggression—making the achievement all the more magnificent!

Given that ruler and minister—Duke Huan and Guan Zhong—planned so thoughtfully at the outset, why then, in the subsequent campaign against Chen, were they so heedless? Truly, it was because their capacity was shallow and their vessel lacked breadth. I have observed Guan Zhong's words: "What achieves success falls into ruin; what achieves fame suffers loss." And when he advised Duke Huan, he was likewise earnestly devoted to the way of preserving fullness and safeguarding accomplishment. Yet in the extravagance of his Three-Return Terrace (Sangui), he personally trod that very path—how then could he rectify his lord? After the pacification of Chu, arrogance sprouted and nine states rebelled; this was only to be expected. Therefore it is said: "Outside the Kingly Way there is no level road—all is thorns and brambles; outside benevolence and righteousness there is no true merit or profit—all is precipitous peril." How true!

"The Marquis of Jin attacked Wei" [Third Year of Duke Wen]; "Yang Chufu of Jin led a force to attack Chu in order to rescue Jiang" [Third Year of Duke Wen]
By Tang Yilong 湯一龍
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Wang, comments: [Solemn, classical, and antique; in classical scholarship, nothing surpasses this.]
Examiner, Senior Compiler Shen, comments: [The composition possesses decisive judgment.]
Examiner, Left Admonisher Shen, comments: [Antique and elegant.]

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
春秋紀事有明君重於師者有明將等於師者
夫君實有國而將與師皆所以衛之者也春秋
之立法有定衡已吾聞唐虞授受必稱元后爲
先蓋崇君道也夫子祖述之而於國君親將示
法焉彼當晉侯之伐衛也故絳之師從公于邁
豈有國者所可忽哉顧赫赫千乘之尊方躬臨
乎戰陣其操縱左右惟一人是瞻而師非所論
矣雖曰國保於民師固有時爲貴然自其分之
一定者言之則尊而象天卑而象地固有不容
===
僭差者使君將而言師師是冠履無別其何以
訓天下故獨稱晉侯不以師竝之也又聞周室
遣帥必與戍役同歌兼重師將也夫子憲章之
而於大夫帥師示法焉彼當處父之救江也斧
鉞之權專制閫外豈士卒之所敢望哉顧誂誂
征夫之衆方共事乎戎行其安危休戚殆一體
相關而將不得獨重矣雖曰師統於帥其分固
有常尊然自其情之聯屬者言之則曰公侯腹
心曰王之爪牙未有能軒輕之者使重將而輕
punctuated: 《春秋》紀事，有明君重於師者，有明將等於師者。夫君實有國，而將與師皆所以衛之者也，《春秋》之立法有定衡已。吾聞唐、虞授受，必稱「元后」爲先，蓋崇君道也。夫子祖述之，而於國君親將示法焉。彼當晉侯之伐衛也，故絳之師從公于邁，豈有國者所可忽哉？顧赫赫千乘之尊，方躬臨乎戰陣，其操縱左右惟一人是瞻，而師非所論矣。雖曰國保於民，師固有時爲貴，然自其分之一定者言之，則尊而象天，卑而象地，固有不容僭差者。使君將而言「帥師」，是冠履無別，其何以訓天下？故獨稱「晉侯」，不以師竝之也。又聞周室遣帥，必與戍役同歌，兼重師將也。夫子憲章之，而於大夫帥師示法焉。彼當處父之救江也，斧鉞之權專制閫外，豈士卒之所敢望哉？顧誂誂征夫之衆，方共事乎戎行，其安危休戚殆一體相關，而將不得獨重矣。雖曰師統於帥，其分固有常尊，然自其情之聯屬者言之，則曰「公侯腹心」，曰「王之爪牙」，未有能軒輕之者。使重將而輕…
translation_en:
In recording events, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) sometimes makes clear that the ruler is weightier than the army, and sometimes makes clear that the commander is on a par with the army. Now, the ruler truly possesses the state, while both the commander and the army are the means by which it is defended; the Spring and Autumn Annals has a fixed standard in establishing its principles.

I have heard that in the transmission of rule between Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], the "Supreme Sovereign" was always named first, which was to exalt the Way of the Ruler. The Master [Confucius] handed down this tradition and displayed this principle when a ruler of a state personally led his troops. At the time when the Marquis of Jin attacked Wei, the army of Old Jiang followed the duke on the march—how could the possessor of a state treat it lightly? Yet when the illustrious majesty of a lord of a thousand chariots personally approaches the battle lines, all direction and movement look solely to that one man, and the army is not what is under discussion. Although it is said that the state is preserved through the people and that the army is indeed at times precious, if we speak from the standpoint of their fixed stations, the noble corresponds to Heaven and the lowly corresponds to Earth, and there may be no僭 [usurpation or] confusion of rank. If, when the ruler commands in person, the text were to say "led the army" [instead of simply naming the ruler], there would be no distinction between cap and shoes—how then could one instruct the world? Therefore it solely names the "Marquis of Jin" and does not place the army alongside him.

I have also heard that when the House of Zhou dispatched commanders, songs were sung for them together with the garrison conscripts, giving weight to both army and commander alike. The Master modeled himself on this and displayed this principle when a Great Officer led the army. At the time when [Yang] Chufu went to rescue Jiang, the authority of the battle-axe gave him sole control beyond the threshold of the capital—how could the rank and file dare to compare themselves with him? Yet when the multitude of marching soldiers are sharing the enterprise in the ranks of war, their safety and peril, their joy and sorrow, are bound together as a single body, and the commander cannot alone be given all the weight. Although it is said that the army is governed by its commander and that his station naturally holds constant honor, if we speak from the standpoint of the bond of feeling uniting them, one is called the "heart and belly of the duke and marquis" and the other the "talons and fangs of the king," and neither can be elevated above or depressed below the other [reading 軒輕 as 軒輊]. If one were to attach weight to the commander and slight…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
師是將卒異心其奚以臨大敵故竝書于策明
將與師等也吁此可見春秋王道之權衡矣迺
至棐林之會則止言晉師而不書趙盾此其意
豈異哉不使臣疑於君者亦重君之意也不使
將掩乎師者是又重衆之義也惟此義不明而
僭逼凌上取民有衆者踵踵矣孔子爲此懼作
春秋也防之得無嚴乎
禮記
命大師陳詩以觀民風命市納賈以觀民
===
之所好惡
梅守峻
同考試官教授臧　批〔簡切精當無一長語〕
考試官修撰沈　批〔明淨有體〕
考試官左賛善沈　批〔融𧨟〕
王者命官凡以觀民而已夫民風民情與政通
矣此王者命官而先其所以觀之者且先王衆
建萬國以爲民也則其時巡萬國宜莫先於觀
民矣彼上有教化民感之而風成而詩則風之
punctuated:
師，是將卒異心，其奚以臨大敵？故竝書于策，明將與師等也。吁！此可見《春秋》王道之權衡矣。迺至棐林之會，則止言晉師而不書趙盾，此其意豈異哉？不使臣疑於君者，亦重君之意也；不使將掩乎師者，是又重衆之義也。惟此義不明，而僭逼凌上、取民有衆者踵踵矣。孔子爲此懼，作《春秋》也，防之得無嚴乎？

禮記
命大師陳詩以觀民風，命市納賈以觀民之所好惡。
梅守峻
同考試官教授臧　批〔簡切精當，無一長語。〕
考試官修撰沈　批〔明淨有體。〕
考試官左賛善沈　批〔融𧨟。〕

王者命官，凡以觀民而已。夫民風、民情，與政通矣，此王者命官而先其所以觀之者。且先王衆建萬國以爲民也，則其時巡萬國，宜莫先於觀民矣。彼上有教化，民感之而風成，而詩則風之…
translation_en:
… the troops, this would divide the hearts of general and soldiers—how then could they face a formidable enemy? Therefore, both are recorded together in the annals to make clear that the general and the army are on an equal footing. Ah! In this one can see the balance of the Kingly Way in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu). When it comes to the meeting at Feilin, it mentions only the army of Jin and does not record Zhao Dun. How could the intention here be any different? Not allowing a subject to rival his ruler in stature is also the intent of honoring the ruler; not allowing a general to overshadow the army is, in turn, the principle of valuing the multitude. Only when this principle became obscure did those who usurped authority, encroached upon and slighted their superiors, and seized the people to amass a following appear one after another. It was out of fear of this that Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals—could the safeguards he set up be anything less than strict?

Record of Rites (Liji)
"He ordered the Grand Music Master to present the poems in order to observe the customs of the people; he ordered the Director of Markets to submit the prices of goods in order to observe what the people liked and disliked."
By Mei Shoujun 梅守峻.
Associate Examiner Zang 臧, Instructor (jiaoshou), comments: "Concise, pertinent, and precise, without a single superfluous word."
Examiner Shen 沈, Senior Compiler (xiuzhuan), comments: "Clear, clean, and well-structured."
Examiner Shen 沈, Left Admonisher (zuo zanshan), comments: "Harmoniously integrated and thorough."

When the true king gives orders to his officials, it is all simply in order to observe the people. Now, the customs of the people and the sentiments of the people are directly connected with governance; this is why the true king, in giving orders to his officials, puts first the means by which to observe them. Moreover, the former kings established the myriad states in great numbers for the sake of the people; thus, during their seasonal tours of inspection through the myriad states, nothing should take precedence over observing the people. When there is moral transformation from above, the people are moved by it and customs are formed, while poetry is the [expression of] those customs…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
咏于言也詩而不陳民風隱矣而侯政之得失
吾將奚觀故聲詩之釆大師掌之而命之陳焉
里巷以歌其志朝廷以貢其俗詩之和矣風之
穆矣而政得可知也詩之靡矣風之漓矣而政
失可知也蓋民既有風不能以無聲惟即其聲
歌所播者一諷咏之而斯國之教化觀其深矣
上有趨向民感之而好惡著而價則好惡之徵
于物也價而不納民情隱矣而侯政之好惡吾
將奚觀故市價之平司市掌之而命之納焉低
===
昂別於日中欲惡徵於俗尚用物貴與是民之
奢也其國奢而示以奢者也侈物貴與是民之
儉也其國儉而示以儉者也蓋民既有情不能
以無形惟即其好尚所形者一獻納之而斯國
之趨向觀其槩矣夫民風觀而諸侯謹於風之
自民之好惡觀而諸侯慎於好惡之原故曰一
遊一觀為諸侯度也抑王者有天下者也天下
之化必自王者始王化弗端而求治於侯國難
已然則省方其先自省乎觀民其先自觀乎樹
punctuated: 咏于言也。詩而不陳，民風隱矣，而侯政之得失，吾將奚觀？故聲詩之釆，大師掌之，而命之陳焉。里巷以歌其志，朝廷以貢其俗。詩之和矣，風之穆矣，而政得可知也；詩之靡矣，風之漓矣，而政失可知也。蓋民既有風，不能以無聲，惟即其聲歌所播者一諷咏之，而斯國之教化觀其深矣。上有趨向，民感之而好惡著，而價則好惡之徵于物也。價而不納，民情隱矣，而侯政之好惡，吾將奚觀？故市價之平，司市掌之，而命之納焉。低昂別於日中，欲惡徵於俗尚。用物貴與？是民之奢也，其國奢而示以奢者也；侈物貴與？是民之儉也，其國儉而示以儉者也。蓋民既有情，不能以無形，惟即其好尚所形者一獻納之，而斯國之趨向觀其槩矣。夫民風觀而諸侯謹於風之自，民之好惡觀而諸侯慎於好惡之原，故曰「一遊一觀，為諸侯度」也。抑王者，有天下者也，天下之化，必自王者始。王化弗端，而求治於侯國，難已。然則省方其先自省乎？觀民其先自觀乎？樹
translation_en:
…chanting in words. If the poems are not presented, the customs of the people remain hidden, and how then shall I observe the successes and failures of the feudal lords' governance? Therefore, the collection of songs and poems is in the charge of the Grand Music Master (Dashi), and he is commanded to present them. The lanes and alleys sing of their aspirations, and the court offers up their customs. When the poems are harmonious and the customs are reverent, one can know that the governance is successful; when the poems are decadent and the customs are thin, one can know that the governance has failed. Indeed, since the people have customs, they cannot be without sound; only by reciting and chanting what is disseminated in their songs can the moral transformation of this state be observed in its depth.

When those above have inclinations, the people are moved by them and their likes and dislikes become manifest, while prices are the verification of those likes and dislikes in material goods. If the prices are not submitted, the feelings of the people remain hidden, and how then shall I observe the likes and dislikes of the feudal lords' governance? Therefore, the regulation of market prices is in the charge of the Supervisor of Markets (Sishi), and he is commanded to submit them. High and low prices are distinguished at the midday market, and desires and aversions are verified in popular fashions. Are useful goods expensive? This means the people are extravagant, and where the state is extravagant, one instructs it with extravagance [?]; are luxury goods expensive? This means the people are frugal, and where the state is frugal, one instructs it with frugality [?]. Indeed, since the people have feelings, they cannot be without outward form; only by presenting and submitting what takes form in their preferences and fashions can the inclinations of this state be observed in their general outline.

Now, when the customs of the people are observed, the feudal lords become careful about the source of those customs; when the likes and dislikes of the people are observed, the feudal lords become cautious about the origin of those likes and dislikes. Therefore it is said, "A single excursion, a single observation, sets the standard for the feudal lords." Yet the true king is the one who possesses All under Heaven, and the transformation of All under Heaven must begin with the true king. If the king's own transforming influence is not upright, to seek good order among the feudal states is difficult indeed. If that is so, then in inspecting the regions, should he not first inspect himself? In observing the people, should he not first observe himself? By establishing…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之風聲明之好惡而天下化之矣嗟乎必如是
而後可以觀哉
天子有善讓德於天
王之鼎
同考試官教授臧　批〔發讓德之意精密可錄〕
考試官修撰沈　批〔粹雅中有格力〕
考試官左贊善沈　批〔精錄〕
天弘化者也有善而必讓諸天其順天也一何
王者善則稱天可以觀順天之至矣夫天子體
===
至哉且夫今之言天子者尊無二上矣宜無所
於讓矣不知天子受命于天者也是故位極天
下而不敢以言尊善蓋天下而不敢以自尚皇
之不德懼其有愧于天矣幸而善自我積而四
海稱明后則非予一人之能也昊天有成命吾
特爲之靈承耳已予之無良懼其有負於天矣
幸而善自吾全而斯世稱聖主則非予小子之
良也唯天有明命吾特爲之奉若耳已聰明照
臨於萬國而天子弗居推而讓之于天曰其天
punctuated:
之風聲，明之好惡，而天下化之矣。嗟乎！必如是而後可以觀哉！

「天子有善，讓德於天。」
王之鼎
同考試官教授臧　批〔發讓德之意，精密可錄。〕
考試官修撰沈　批〔粹雅中有格力。〕
考試官左贊善沈　批〔精。錄。〕

天弘化者也，有善而必讓諸天，其順天也一何王者善則稱天，可以觀順天之至矣。夫天子，體至哉！且夫今之言天子者，尊無二上矣，宜無所於讓矣；不知天子受命于天者也。是故位極天下而不敢以言尊，善蓋天下而不敢以自尚。皇之不德，懼其有愧于天矣；幸而善自我積，而四海稱明后，則非予一人之能也，昊天有成命，吾特爲之靈承耳已。予之無良，懼其有負於天矣；幸而善自吾全，而斯世稱聖主，則非予小子之良也，唯天有明命，吾特爲之奉若耳已。聰明照臨於萬國，而天子弗居，推而讓之于天曰：「其天
translation_en:
… their moral reputation and clarify what is to be liked and hated, and the whole world will be transformed by it. Alas! Only when it is like this can one truly conduct an inspection!

"When the Son of Heaven has goodness, he yields the credit for the virtue to Heaven." (Book of Rites, "The Meaning of Sacrifices")
By Wang Zhiding 王之鼎
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zang 臧, comments: [He brings out the meaning of yielding credit for virtue; precise and worthy of recording.]
Examiner, Senior Compiler Shen 沈, comments: [Within its pure elegance there is structural vigor.]
Examiner, Left Admonisher Shen 沈, comments: [Precise. Recorded.]

[Note: the first two lines of the essay appear swapped in the transcription.] When a true king has goodness, he attributes it to Heaven; from this one may observe the utmost degree of compliance with Heaven. Now, the Son of Heaven is one who embodies Heaven to broaden transformation; when he possesses goodness and necessarily yields it to Heaven, how utmost is his compliance with Heaven!

Moreover, those who speak of the Son of Heaven nowadays say that in exaltedness he has no peer above him, so it would seem he has nothing to which he need yield. They do not know that the Son of Heaven is one who receives his mandate from Heaven. Therefore, though his position reaches the pinnacle of the world, he dares not speak of himself as exalted; though his goodness covers the world, he dares not vaunt himself. "Should I, the August One, lack virtue, I fear being ashamed before Heaven; if by good fortune goodness is accumulated through me, and the four seas acclaim me as an enlightened sovereign, that is not the ability of me, the One Man—vast Heaven has its settled mandate, and I merely attend to it with spiritual receptivity." "Should I lack goodness, I fear failing Heaven; if by good fortune goodness is perfected through me, and this age acclaims me as a sage ruler, that is not the goodness of me, the Little Child—Heaven alone has its bright mandate, and I merely reverently conform to it." title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
作之乎而歸美之誠著矣豈謂宸聰自啓也顧
無所與於天哉智勇表正於萬邦而天子弗任
舉而讓之于天曰其天錫之乎而推戴之志昭
矣豈謂乾綱獨斷也顧於天無與哉故自天下
而視天子其典之敦禮之庸德罪之命討而善
罔不備者咸以爲我后之德自天子而自視其
曰天敘曰天秩曰天命天討而德罔不臧者則
以爲帝降之休吁其順天也至矣書云有其善
喪厥善天子唯於天讓善則其心無所有矣無
===
所有乃能無所喪而德益格于皇天彼沾沾一
善者居之不疑輒自以爲兼三皇超五帝而不
知其心侈志盈天且棄之善於何有於乎唯舜
文其不可及也與
第貳場
論
王道本乎人情
梅守峻
同考試官教諭萬　批〔此論作者類多剿襲陳言而於〕
punctuated:
作之乎？」而歸美之誠著矣。豈謂宸聰自啓也，顧無所與於天哉？智勇表正於萬邦，而天子弗任，舉而讓之于天曰：「其天錫之乎？」而推戴之志昭矣。豈謂乾綱獨斷也，顧於天無與哉？故自天下而視天子，其典之敦、禮之庸、德罪之命討而善罔不備者，咸以爲我后之德；自天子而自視，其曰「天敘」、曰「天秩」、曰「天命」「天討」而德罔不臧者，則以爲帝降之休。吁！其順天也至矣。《書》云：「有其善，喪厥善。」天子唯於天讓善，則其心無所有矣；無所有乃能無所喪，而德益格于皇天。彼沾沾一善者，居之不疑，輒自以爲兼三皇、超五帝，而不知其心侈志盈，天且棄之，善於何有？於乎！唯舜、文其不可及也與！

第貳場
論
王道本乎人情
梅守峻
同考試官教諭萬批：〔此論作者類多剿襲陳言，而於〕
translation_en:
… "Did Heaven not bring it about?" And thus the sincerity of his attributing excellence to Heaven becomes manifest. How could he claim that his imperial intelligence opened of itself, without any involvement from Heaven? When wisdom and courage serve as a standard to rectify the myriad states, the Son of Heaven does not take the credit upon himself, but raises and yields it to Heaven, saying: "Did Heaven not bestow it?" And thus his resolve to revere and uphold Heaven becomes clear. How could he claim that his sovereign authority acts by its sole decision, having nothing to do with Heaven? Therefore, when the world looks upon the Son of Heaven—his thickening of the constant norms, his employment of the rites, his rewarding of virtue and punishing of guilt, such that no goodness is lacking—all regard it as the virtue of our sovereign. Yet when the Son of Heaven looks upon himself—speaking of "Heaven's arrangements," "Heaven's order," "Heaven's mandate," and "Heaven's punishment," whereby no virtue fails to be good—he regards it as the blessing sent down by the Supreme Ancestor. Ah! His compliance with Heaven is supreme indeed. The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "To lay claim to one's goodness is to lose that goodness." Only because the Son of Heaven yields goodness to Heaven does his mind lay claim to nothing; by laying claim to nothing, he is able to lose nothing, and his virtue reaches ever more unto August Heaven. As for those who are self-satisfied with a single good deed and claim credit for it without hesitation, readily fancying that they combine the Three August Ones and surpass the Five Emperors—they do not realize that as their minds grow extravagant and their ambitions self-satisfied, Heaven is about to cast them aside; what goodness will they have left? Alas! Only Shun and King Wen are beyond reach!

Mei Shoujun 梅守峻

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
本題之旨漫不相涉子獨根據無偏無黨之義代發軍明忠議論醇正深得
納王之心且格局冠裳意調高古氣度沖和才識兼到之士也尚薦
允宜
同考試官推官徐　批題意甚大說理者易窮入事者
多冗塲中作者難展所長獨此卷議論反覆千餘言皆根極經訓隱
括人情精徹宏暢深得王道蕩平氣象是必達於治體者錄之以式
多士宜也
考試官修撰沈　批立意正大開闔有度不事奇詭而綱條粲
然精理自著至說人情處有味哉
===
考試官左賛善沈　批〔曲盡人情〕
王道之所以爲大者在因人心之自然而無所
自用於天下所謂人心之自然者何也則天下
之情是也夫天下之人亦夥矣離而聽之棼乎
其乎若難盡狥其欲者是一人之私也非其合
而公者也其合而公者則至平也而同乎天至
渙也而統乎道愚不可欺弱不可攖久遠循習
而不可易此以明其出於自然也聖人知其然
其爲道也不任巳之情而常本於人之情不本
punctuated:
本題之旨漫不相涉。子獨根據無偏無黨之義，代發軍明忠，議論醇正，深得納王之心。且格局冠裳，意調高古，氣度沖和，才識兼到之士也。尚薦允宜。
同考試官推官徐　批：題意甚大，說理者易窮，入事者多冗，塲中作者難展所長。獨此卷議論反覆千餘言，皆根極經訓，隱括人情，精徹宏暢，深得王道蕩平氣象。是必達於治體者，錄之以式多士，宜也。
考試官修撰沈　批：立意正大，開闔有度，不事奇詭，而綱條粲然，精理自著。至說人情處，有味哉！
考試官左賛善沈　批：〔曲盡人情。〕
王道之所以爲大者，在因人心之自然，而無所自用於天下。所謂人心之自然者何也？則天下之情是也。夫天下之人亦夥矣！離而聽之，棼乎其乎若難盡狥其欲者，是一人之私也，非其合而公者也。其合而公者，則至平也，而同乎天；至渙也，而統乎道。愚不可欺，弱不可攖，久遠循習而不可易，此以明其出於自然也。聖人知其然，其爲道也，不任巳之情而常本於人之情，不本
translation_en:
… have nothing to do with the purport of this topic. You alone ground your argument in the principle of being without bias and without faction, speaking on behalf of and expounding with illuminating fidelity [? 代發軍明忠, likely garbled for 發揮明暢]. Your discourse is pure and upright, deeply grasping the heart of counseling a true king [? 納王之心, or perhaps 純王之心, the heart of a pure king]. Moreover, the structure is dignified as cap and robes, the tone lofty and ancient, and the bearing harmonious and mild—you are a scholar who combines both talent and insight. It is truly fitting to recommend this carefully.

Associate Examiner and Prefectural Judge Xu comments: The meaning of the topic is vast; those who expound on principles easily exhaust their arguments, while those who delve into historical events often become verbose, making it difficult for examinees in the compounds to display their strengths. This paper alone argues back and forth in over a thousand words, all rooted deeply in the teachings of the Classics and encompassing human feelings. It is penetrating, grand, and fluent, profoundly capturing the broad and level spirit of the Kingly Way. This must be someone who understands the essentials of governance; recording it to serve as a model for the many scholars is fitting indeed.

Examiner and Senior Compiler Shen comments: The central thesis is upright and grand, with measured openings and closings. It does not pursue the strange or deceitful, yet its main outlines and sub-points are resplendently clear, and refined principles naturally manifest themselves. When it comes to discussing human feelings, how rich in flavor it is!

Examiner and Left Admonisher Shen comments: [It thoroughly captures every nuance of human feelings.]

That by which the Kingly Way is great lies in following the spontaneity of the human mind, without imposing one's own self-will upon the world. What is meant by the spontaneity of the human mind? It is none other than the feelings of the world. Now, the people of the world are numerous indeed! If one listens to them separately, they are tangled and [? 棼乎其乎, likely garbled for 棼乎其殊, confusedly diverse], as though it were impossible to fully satisfy all their desires—that is because those are the selfish desires of single individuals, not what is shared in common when brought together. What is shared in common when brought together is utterly level and identical with Heaven; though utterly dispersed, it is unified by the Way. The foolish cannot be deceived, the weak cannot be violated, and what has been followed and practiced for a long time cannot be altered—this makes clear that it arises from spontaneity. The sage knows that this is so; therefore, in practicing his Way, he does not rely on his own feelings, but always takes the feelings of others as his foundation; he does not take as his foundation…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
一人之情而本天下之人之情天下之所欲吾
爲導達節制其間而未始以已逆之天下所不
欲吾爲區處禁禦遠其患害而未始以已彊之
如是則天下之情得而天下之心通其久也上
下交相凝固莫知其然此謂純王之道非伯者
可及也然則聖人者道德粹清一出于公豈其
才智之不足以治天下哉亦深察夫人情而已
宋儒程顥氏明王霸之辨爲神宗告曰王道如
砥本乎人情惟本乎人情此王道所以如砥也
===
夫王道之說何昉焉箕子之陳洪範曰無偏無
黨王道蕩蕩無黨無偏王道平平無反無側王
道正直所謂蕩平正直者何也人情之謂也天
下之人各受天之明命以爲性其見乎情者必
有大公至正之極焉建極於上則爲王道歸極
於下則爲人情人情爲王道之本所從來久蓋
二帝三王不能易也且夫帝王者履太上制六
合姑無論天下之人頫首以聽吾所欲爲苟出
其獨智求治于天下而縱横操切之亦奚不可
punctuated:
一人之情，而本天下之人之情。天下之所欲，吾爲導達節制其間，而未始以已逆之；天下所不欲，吾爲區處禁禦，遠其患害，而未始以已彊之。如是，則天下之情得而天下之心通。其久也，上下交相凝固，莫知其然，此謂純王之道，非伯者可及也。然則聖人者，道德粹清，一出于公，豈其才智之不足以治天下哉？亦深察夫人情而已。宋儒程顥氏明王霸之辨，爲神宗告曰：「王道如砥，本乎人情。」惟本乎人情，此王道所以如砥也。
夫王道之說何昉焉？箕子之陳《洪範》曰：「無偏無黨，王道蕩蕩；無黨無偏，王道平平；無反無側，王道正直。」所謂蕩平正直者何也？人情之謂也。天下之人，各受天之明命以爲性，其見乎情者，必有大公至正之極焉。建極於上，則爲王道；歸極於下，則爲人情。人情爲王道之本，所從來久，蓋二帝三王不能易也。且夫帝王者，履太上，制六合，姑無論天下之人頫首以聽吾所欲爲，苟出其獨智，求治于天下，而縱横操切之，亦奚不可？
translation_en:
… [not rooted in] the feelings of a single person, but rooted in the feelings of all the people in the world. What the world desires, I guide, channel, and regulate accordingly, without ever opposing it out of my own self-interest; what the world does not desire, I manage, prohibit, and ward off to keep its harms and dangers far away, without ever forcing it upon them out of my own self-interest. When it is thus, the feelings of the world are satisfied and the minds of the world are brought into harmony. Over time, superiors and inferiors become firmly bound to one another without even knowing how it came to be so. This is what is called the way of the pure True King, which no hegemon can attain. If this is so, then when the sages—whose moral virtue is pure and unsullied, and whose actions proceed entirely from impartiality—govern the world, is it because their talent and wisdom are insufficient to rule it? They simply examine human feelings deeply, and nothing more. The Song Confucian Cheng Hao 程顥, clarifying the distinction between the True King and the hegemon, told Emperor Shenzong 神宗: "The Kingly Way is as level as a whetstone, and is rooted in human feelings." It is precisely because it is rooted in human feelings that the Kingly Way is as level as a whetstone.

Now, where did the doctrine of the Kingly Way originate? When Jizi 箕子 set forth the Great Plan (Hongfan 洪範), he said: "Without偏 [partiality] and without faction, the Kingly Way is broad and vast; without faction and without partiality, the Kingly Way is level and easy; without perversity and without one-sidedness, the Kingly Way is straight and upright." What is meant by broad, level, straight, and upright? It refers to human feelings. The people of the world each receive the bright mandate of Heaven as their nature, and when it is manifested in their feelings, there is必ず [necessarily] a supreme standard of great impartiality and utmost rectitude therein. When this supreme standard is established above, it is the Kingly Way; when people turn to this supreme standard below, it is human feelings. That human feelings are the root of the Kingly Way has been so for a long time; indeed, the Two Emperors and Three Kings could not alter it. Moreover, emperors and kings occupy the highest position and hold sway over the six directions of the universe. Setting aside the fact that the people of the world bow their heads to obey whatever we wish to do, even if a ruler were to bring forth his own solitary intelligence to seek order in the world, manipulating and compelling it at will, why would that be impossible? …

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
乃孜孜俯狥天下惟恐一夫不獲其情者此曷
故哉蓋天之與人亦遠矣天生聖人宅之君師
予之聰明睿知使之通乎天與人之間以達其
情而代天以司平于天下其道固若懸衡虛至
之中付之善權者進退焉但不令爽一銖不以
指握加輕重如是焉耳矣然五權之變不可勝
窮低昂俯仰日有百變天下之情之難平也亦
若是耳是故奠九宇以爲安錯之在覆盂焉而
梘杌反側羅其中矣環四海以爲帶保之在襁
===
屬焉而闇黯垢汶藪其閒矣包萬彙以爲家寧
之在堂序焉而勢拏瑣劇宅其所矣生殊稟則
殊心土殊風則殊氣謠俗嗜好被服器械殊宜
則殊習均是人也九譯不能通焉而聖人者欲
以方寸而周環海以宥密而灼豐蔀以瞬息而
垂永世其智必有不周其勢必有不徧則天下
之情曷由以盡而聖人之治或幾乎窮夫使聖
人者果煦煦焉日求天下之情而狥之而悅之
誠有所不可繼然而聖人之所謂本人情者不
punctuated: 乃孜孜俯狥天下，惟恐一夫不獲其情者，此曷故哉？蓋天之與人亦遠矣，天生聖人，宅之君師，予之聰明睿知，使之通乎天與人之間，以達其情，而代天以司平于天下。其道固若懸衡虛至之中，付之善權者進退焉，但不令爽一銖，不以指握加輕重，如是焉耳矣。然五權之變，不可勝窮，低昂俯仰，日有百變，天下之情之難平也，亦若是耳。是故奠九宇以爲安，錯之在覆盂焉，而梘杌反側羅其中矣；環四海以爲帶，保之在襁屬焉，而闇黯垢汶藪其閒矣；包萬彙以爲家，寧之在堂序焉，而勢拏瑣劇宅其所矣。生殊稟則殊心，土殊風則殊氣，謠俗、嗜好、被服、器械殊宜則殊習，均是人也，九譯不能通焉。而聖人者，欲以方寸而周環海，以宥密而灼豐蔀，以瞬息而垂永世，其智必有不周，其勢必有不徧，則天下之情曷由以盡，而聖人之治或幾乎窮。夫使聖人者果煦煦焉，日求天下之情而狥之、而悅之，誠有所不可繼。然而聖人之所謂本人情者，不
translation_en: …yet instead they tirelessly stoop to accommodate the world, fearing only that a single man might fail to have his feelings fulfilled—why is this so? Truly, Heaven and man are far apart. Heaven gives birth to the sage, places him in the position of ruler and teacher, and endows him with keenness of ear and eye and perspicacious wisdom, causing him to communicate between Heaven and man so as to give expression to their feelings and to administer fairness across the world on Heaven's behalf. His Way is indeed like suspending a balance beam in a state of emptiness and impartiality and entrusting it to one skilled in weighing to slide the weights back and forth—merely ensuring that it does not err by a single grain and not adding weight or lightness by the grip of the fingers; it is just like this and nothing more. Yet the variations of the five weights are inexhaustible: tilting up and down, rising and falling, they undergo a hundred changes a day; the difficulty of bringing equilibrium to the feelings of the world is just like this too. Therefore, though one settles the nine regions to make them secure, placing them as steadily as an upturned bowl, precariously unsettled [?] and rebellious elements are ranged within; though one encircles the Four Seas as a girdle, cherishing them as infants bound in swaddling clothes, benighted, murky, and sullied elements gather in their midst; though one encompasses the myriad beings as a single household, giving them peace within the hall and side-chambers, tangled and petty complexities [?] dwell in their places. Because people are born with different endowments, they have different minds; because lands have different airs, they have different temperaments; because ballad-customs, tastes, clothing, and implements have different suitabilities, they have different habits. All are equally human, yet even through ninefold translation they cannot communicate with one another. Now if the sage wishes with a heart of one square inch to encompass the encircling seas, from the quiet profundity of the palace to see clearly through the thickest screens, and in the blink of an eye to hand down a legacy for eternal generations, his wisdom must inevitably fail to reach everywhere, and his authority must inevitably fail to cover everything. How then could the feelings of the world be fully fathomed, and would not the governance of the sage come close to exhaustion? Now, suppose the sage were indeed to go about with petty, anxious benevolence, daily seeking out the feelings of the world in order to accommodate them and please them—truly, this could not be sustained. However, what the sage calls taking human feelings as the foundation is not…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
然也一人之情億兆人之情是也億兆人之情
一人之情是也瞑吾之目而天下之共見在焉
傾吾之耳而天下之共聞通焉潛吾之思而天
下之是非欲惡無不備焉人情有公是非根于
秉彝之正而不可以勢奪也人情有同欲惡起
于生養之際而不可以力强也聖人者將有動
乎其慮必觀天下之公是非而無敢以己之適
莫與之將有加乎其民必察天下之同欲惡而
無敢以己之愛憎叅之本其公是而是之天下
===
莫不與焉本其公非而非之天下莫能違焉本
其同欲而趨之鼓舞者不終日焉本其同惡而
避之欣戴者不踰時焉冬日之陽夏日之陰莫
之召而人爭趨之者得其必至之情故也羣飛
之歸茂林也羣游之歸深瀨也孰招之而孰强
之夫非天機之自然耶昔者皇王之世開天統
而治人情若耒耜衣裳車馬宫室儷皮衣薪之
屬旣漸因夫物情之所宜而創爲之而五禮六
樂八政五教九伐五刑之屬又皆因世而推移
