punctuated: 然也。一人之情，億兆人之情是也；億兆人之情，一人之情是也。瞑吾之目，而天下之共見在焉；傾吾之耳，而天下之共聞通焉；潛吾之思，而天下之是非欲惡無不備焉。人情有公是非，根于秉彝之正，而不可以勢奪也；人情有同欲惡，起于生養之際，而不可以力强也。聖人者，將有動乎其慮，必觀天下之公是非，而無敢以己之適莫與之；將有加乎其民，必察天下之同欲惡，而無敢以己之愛憎叅之。本其公是而是之，天下莫不與焉；本其公非而非之，天下莫能違焉。本其同欲而趨之，鼓舞者不終日焉；本其同惡而避之，欣戴者不踰時焉。冬日之陽，夏日之陰，莫之召而人爭趨之者，得其必至之情故也。羣飛之歸茂林也，羣游之歸深瀨也，孰招之而孰强之？夫非天機之自然耶？昔者皇王之世，開天統而治人情，若耒耜、衣裳、車馬、宫室、儷皮、衣薪之屬，旣漸因夫物情之所宜而創爲之；而五禮、六樂、八政、五教、九伐、五刑之屬，又皆因世而推移，
translation_en: …so. The feelings of one person are the very feelings of hundreds of millions of people; the feelings of hundreds of millions of people are the very feelings of one person. Close my eyes, and what all under heaven see in common is present within; incline my ears, and what all under heaven hear in common is communicated within; immerse my thoughts, and what all under heaven hold to be right and wrong, or desire and abhor, is without exception complete within. Human feelings possess an impartial sense of right and wrong, rooted in the rectitude of our innate moral constancy, which cannot be wrested away by power; human feelings possess shared desires and aversions, arising from the circumstances of livelihood and sustenance, which cannot be coerced by force. When the sage is about to stir his deliberations, he must observe what all under heaven impartially hold to be right and wrong, never daring to interpose his own predispositions for or against; when he is about to apply measures to his people, he must examine what all under heaven commonly desire and abhor, never daring to mix in his own personal likes and dislikes. Grounding himself in what they impartially hold to be right and affirming it as right, none in the world fails to concur; grounding himself in what they impartially hold to be wrong and condemning it as wrong, none in the world is able to defy it. Grounding himself in what they commonly desire and pursuing it, they are roused to enthusiasm before the day is out; grounding himself in what they commonly abhor and shunning it, they joyfully pledge allegiance within a single season. The warmth of the winter sun and the shade of a summer day—none summons men to them, yet people vie to flock there, because these answer to the feelings they are bound to have. When flocks of birds on the wing return to dense forests, and shoals of swimming fish return to deep rapids, who beckons them and who compels them? Is this not the spontaneous working of Heaven's mechanism? In antiquity, during the ages of the August Ones and Kings, they inaugurated the Heavenly succession and governed human feelings. Things such as plows and shares, upper and lower garments, carriages and horses, dwellings, betrothal gifts of paired deerskins, and burials wrapped in firewood were gradually created in accordance with what was fitting to the nature of things and human feelings; while institutions such as the Five Rites, Six Musics, Eight Administrations, Five Teachings, Nine Punitive Expeditions, and Five Punishments all shifted in accordance with the age,…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
殊時而不相襲則以後世之情竇日開日巧聖
人代作敎之加切防之加密慮之加備亦莫不
因人情之自然者各有建置于天下而一慶賞
一誅罰一明揚一顯黜與夫一興革動止靡弗
觀人情而出之故安之者固情也有所勞而逸
之者亦情也養之者固情也有所節而愛之者
亦情也順之者固情也有所禁而衛之者亦情
也生之者固情也有所殺而全之者亦情也聖
人者操予奪生殺于萬民之上必順人情之自
===
然而應之聖人固曰吾何情哉吾司平于天下
猶牧者本牛之情御者本馬之情樹者本木之
情舟者本水之情然則治人者不本人之情而
何也嗟乎天下之情之不可勝窮也所求遂於
聖人者至殷繁也聖人所以本人之情者豈易
言哉其虛中以求之是慈母之撫嬰子扣以心
而不以言也其致忠愛悉聰明以察之是扶傷
捄溺詔聾而導瞽弗盡誠弗止也其順而導之
也是注物于流水之源其變而通之也是曦曜
punctuated: 殊時而不相襲，則以後世之情竇日開日巧，聖人代作，敎之加切，防之加密，慮之加備，亦莫不因人情之自然者各有建置于天下。而一慶賞、一誅罰、一明揚、一顯黜，與夫一興革、動止，靡弗觀人情而出之。故安之者固情也，有所勞而逸之者亦情也；養之者固情也，有所節而愛之者亦情也；順之者固情也，有所禁而衛之者亦情也；生之者固情也，有所殺而全之者亦情也。聖人者，操予奪生殺于萬民之上，必順人情之自然而應之。聖人固曰：「吾何情哉？吾司平于天下，猶牧者本牛之情，御者本馬之情，樹者本木之情，舟者本水之情；然則治人者，不本人之情而何也？」嗟乎！天下之情之不可勝窮也，所求遂於聖人者至殷繁也，聖人所以本人之情者，豈易言哉？其虛中以求之，是慈母之撫嬰子，扣以心而不以言也；其致忠愛、悉聰明以察之，是扶傷捄溺、詔聾而導瞽，弗盡誠弗止也；其順而導之也，是注物于流水之源；其變而通之也，是曦曜
translation_en: …differing with the times and not simply copying one another. This was because in later ages the outlets of human desires grew daily more open and daily more artful. As sages arose in succession, their instruction became more urgent, their precautions tighter, and their deliberations more thorough, yet none failed to establish their institutions across the realm on the basis of what was natural to human dispositions. Thus every bestowal of reward and every execution or punishment, every public promotion and every open demotion, as well as every initiative or reform, every action or cessation, was without exception issued only after observing human dispositions. Therefore, to give people安 (peace and security) is of course in accord with their dispositions, yet to put them to toil so as to bring them ease is also in accord with their dispositions; to nourish them is of course in accord with their dispositions, yet to restrain them so as to cherish them is also in accord with their dispositions; to comply with them is of course in accord with their dispositions, yet to impose prohibitions so as to protect them is also in accord with their dispositions; to keep them alive is of course in accord with their dispositions, yet to put some to death so as to preserve the rest is also in accord with their dispositions. The sage, wielding the power to give and to take away, to grant life and to inflict death above the myriad people, must respond in accordance with what is natural to human dispositions. Indeed, the sage says: "What personal feelings of my own do I have? My charge to maintain equity across the realm is just like the herdsman basing himself on the nature of cattle, the charioteer basing himself on the nature of horses, the arborist basing himself on the nature of trees, and the boatman basing himself on the nature of water; how, then, could one who governs human beings do anything other than base himself on human dispositions?" Alas! The dispositions of the world cannot be exhausted, and what people seek to fulfill from the sage is exceedingly abundant and manifold; how could the means by which the sage bases himself on human dispositions be easily spoken of? His emptying of his mind to seek them out is like a loving mother soothing an infant, inquiring with her heart rather than with words; his extending of utmost loyalty and affection and exhausting of his hearing and sight to examine them is like supporting the wounded and rescuing the drowning, instructing the deaf and guiding the blind, never stopping until utmost sincerity is reached; his following along and guiding them is like pouring things into the source of flowing water; his adapting and carrying them through is like the sunlight shining…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
于寒林之谷其優游以俟之是浸潤沃灌溫乎
不以旦夕迫也聖人者端拱穆清神動天隨不
煩指而自喻不戒令而自肅勞民而民忘勞使
民而民忘死戴之如日月拱之如北辰豈待發
徵期會哉天下熙熙欲得其情而來天下蕩蕩
各厭其情而往天下之人各得其情而民已治
矣化理畢矣故人情者聖人治天下之大本也
蓋其始也緣法以順人之情其中也經綸以盡
人之情其終也纏綿固結乎人情上下相忘遊
于大庭之天如野鹿標枝同歸無情而已故曰
心普萬物而無心不自用其心也情順萬事而
無情不自用其情也此王道之所以爲大歟古
今稱王道之備無如成周乃惟曰有關雎麟趾
之意以行周官之法度又曰平易近民民必歸
之其治內治外之道蓋莫詳于詩於伐木則道
及乾餱釃酧之微于四牡則體其將父將母之
念于采薇則敘其室家啓處饑渴寒暑之情而
東征一詩細及於往來感遇町疃蠨蛸聚樂離
punctuated: 于寒林之谷；其優游以俟之，是浸潤沃灌，溫乎不以旦夕迫也。聖人者，端拱穆清，神動天隨，不煩指而自喻，不戒令而自肅，勞民而民忘勞，使民而民忘死，戴之如日月，拱之如北辰，豈待發徵期會哉？天下熙熙，欲得其情而來；天下蕩蕩，各厭其情而往。天下之人各得其情，而民已治矣，化理畢矣。故人情者，聖人治天下之大本也。蓋其始也，緣法以順人之情；其中也，經綸以盡人之情；其終也，纏綿固結乎人情，上下相忘，遊于大庭之天，如野鹿標枝，同歸無情而已。故曰：「心普萬物而無心，不自用其心也；情順萬事而無情，不自用其情也。」此王道之所以爲大歟！古今稱王道之備，無如成周。乃惟曰：「有《關雎》、《麟趾》之意，以行《周官》之法度。」又曰：「平易近民，民必歸之。」其治內治外之道，蓋莫詳于《詩》。於《伐木》，則道及乾餱釃酧之微；于《四牡》，則體其將父將母之念；于《采薇》，則敘其室家啓處、饑渴寒暑之情；而東征一詩，細及於往來感遇、町疃蠨蛸、聚樂離…
translation_en: …in the valley of a wintry forest; and his patient waiting for them in unhurried ease is like soaking and irrigating the soil, gentle and unpressured by the demands of morning and evening. The sage sits with hands folded in serene purity, his spirit moving in accord with Heaven. Without the trouble of pointing, the people understand of themselves; without admonitions and orders, they become reverent of themselves. He puts the people to toil, yet they forget their toil; he sends them into service, yet they forget death. They look up to him as the sun and moon, and turn toward him as the North Star—what need is there to issue summonses or set appointed times for assembly? The realm bustles with people coming because they wish to fulfill their natural feelings, and the realm stretches vast as each goes forth satisfied in those feelings. When everyone in the world attains the fulfillment of their feelings, the people are already well governed and transformative ordering is complete. Therefore, human feelings are the great foundation upon which the sage governs the world. In the beginning, he relies on laws to accord with human feelings; in the middle stage, he orders the state to exhaust the full measure of human feelings; and in the end, he is so closely bound up with human feelings that superior and inferior forget one another, roaming beneath the sky of the ancient sovereign Dating, like wild deer below and lofty branches above, returning together to a state beyond conscious feeling. Thus it is said: "His mind encompasses the myriad things yet has no mind of its own, for he does not indulge his own mind; his feelings accord with the myriad affairs yet have no feelings of their own, for he does not indulge his own feelings." Is this not why the Kingly Way is so great! Past and present, none has been praised for the completeness of the Kingly Way more than the flourishing Zhou dynasty. Yet it was said only that "one must possess the spirit of the 'Ospreys Cry' (Guanju) and the 'Unicorn's Hoof' (Linzhi) in order to implement the institutions of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan)," and also that "when one is plain, easy, and approachable to the people, the people will surely turn to him." Its way of governing both the inner and the outer realms is nowhere set forth in greater detail than in the Book of Odes (Shi). In "Hewing Trees" (Famu), it speaks even of such small matters as dried provisions and strained wine offered to guests; in "Four Steeds" (Simu), it enters into the envoy's longing to care for his father and mother; in "Plucking Bracken" (Caiwei), it recounts the soldiers' feelings regarding their homes, their kneeling and resting, their hunger and thirst, and the cold and heat; and in the ode on the Eastern Expedition ("Dongshan"), it details even the emotions stirred in coming and going, the deer-trampled plots and long-legged spiders around the deserted house, the joys of reunion and the…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
合之思卽家人父子相爲慰勞者罔弗宣其意
而代言之抑何愛人之深而本人情之厚乎維
時品式詳明精意流貫所爲聯絡一世者若出
其一身閭師黨正以歲時鄉射讀法握手而告
語之朝覲會同集天下卿士大夫安樂綢繆以
盡其懽揚旌揭鼓徇鐸振鞀自士民與瞽靡不
得陳所懷來悉所欲言天下之情旣已無不遂
矣而約已裕人之念尤不弛銘于几席觀風采
謠之吏尤不絕迹于海澨慮天下或有難吐之
===
情必使宣鬯於兩間無復壅洳而後已其間雍
容款曲上下訢合自有愛卹保養之深意入人
心而人不知者一切束縛刻核懲膺及體之政
惻然有所不忍施故誦其詩者嘆曰先王以人
道使人曰太和在成周宇宙則周之道一本于
人情故也及周之衰而伯圖興王道幾乎熄矣
民生其時有情而不得伸鬱而後發天下遂一
散而不收則秦之季是已蓋嘗論之伯之術尚
詭貴所不知不見籠罩一世而自專利焉王道
punctuated: 合之思，卽家人父子相爲慰勞者，罔弗宣其意而代言之，抑何愛人之深而本人情之厚乎！維時品式詳明，精意流貫，所爲聯絡一世者，若出其一身。閭師、黨正以歲時鄉射、讀法，握手而告語之；朝覲、會同，集天下卿士大夫，安樂綢繆以盡其懽；揚旌、揭鼓、徇鐸、振鞀，自士民與瞽，靡不得陳所懷來，悉所欲言。天下之情旣已無不遂矣，而約已裕人之念，尤不弛銘于几席；觀風采謠之吏，尤不絕迹于海澨。慮天下或有難吐之情，必使宣鬯於兩間，無復壅洳而後已。其間雍容款曲，上下訢合，自有愛卹保養之深意，入人心而人不知者。一切束縛、刻核、懲膺及體之政，惻然有所不忍施。故誦其詩者，嘆曰：「先王以人道使人。」曰：「太和在成周宇宙。」則周之道一本于人情故也。及周之衰而伯圖興，王道幾乎熄矣。民生其時，有情而不得伸，鬱而後發，天下遂一散而不收，則秦之季是已。蓋嘗論之：伯之術尚詭，貴所不知不見，籠罩一世而自專利焉；王道…
translation_en: …and reunion; even what family members, fathers, and sons would say in mutual comfort and encouragement was without exception given voice and spoken on their behalf. How deep was their love for the people, and how generously grounded in human feeling! At that time, regulations and forms were detailed and clear, and a refined spirit flowed through them all; that by which the entire age was bound together was as though it issued from a single body. At the seasonal district archery rituals and readings of the laws, the Neighborhood Preceptors (lüshi) and District Magistrates (dangzheng) clasped hands with the people and instructed them; at court audiences and royal assemblies, the ministers, officers, and grandees of the realm were gathered in peace, joy, and close fellowship to exhaust their delight; and with banners raised, drums mounted, wooden-tongued bells sounded along the roads, and hand-drums shaken, from scholars and commoners down to blind musicians, there was no one who could not set forth what he harbored in his breast and say in full all that he wished to speak. Even when the feelings of all under Heaven had already been completely fulfilled, the thought of restraining oneself and enriching others was still never relaxed among the inscriptions on the ruler's armrests and mats, and officials sent to observe local customs and collect folk songs never ceased to leave their footprints even to the shores of the sea. Fearing that in the realm there might still be feelings difficult to utter, they insisted on making them flow freely between Heaven and Earth, not stopping until there was no longer any blockage or stagnation. Amidst this unhurried grace and warm solicitude, with superiors and inferiors harmoniously united, there was naturally a deep intent to cherish, pity, and nurture—entering into people's hearts without their even realizing it. All policies of binding restriction, harsh scrutiny, and bodily chastisement they felt a compassionate reluctance to impose. Therefore, those who recited their odes sighed and said, "The former kings employed people according to the way of humanity," and said, "Supreme harmony prevailed throughout the universe of the flourishing Zhou." This was because the Way of Zhou was wholly rooted in human feeling. When the Zhou declined and hegemonic ambitions arose, the Kingly Way was almost extinguished. The people living in those times had feelings that they could not express; pent up and only later bursting forth, the realm consequently scattered all at once and could not be gathered back together—such was the end of the Qin. Indeed, if we discuss it: the art of the hegemon prizes deceit, valuing what is unknown and unseen so as to hold the whole age in its grasp and monopolize the profit for itself; the Kingly Way…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
則否皎如白日朗朗洞洞人情而已伯之術尚
巧逶迤宛轉與時上下屈于所甚屈伸于所甚
伸王道則否直如引墨正正平平人情而已伯
之術尚捷令行禁止急於駭電王道則否舒如
遲日容容徐徐人情而已世未有遏人情而人
不知拂人情而人不怨人情和而不安人情怨
而不危者而俗乃謂王道迂遲伯圖敏速則何
不引周秦之故觀之乎故曰誠心而王則王矣
假之而伯則伯矣吁本人情言王道乃其所謂
===
本于誠意者歟雖然人之情每奮於作新靡於
無事約於始造泰於末流是以亂伏於治危倚
於安則以持情無道履盛而不知戒也聖人既
本人情以治天下而又修禮以耕之陳義以種
之講學以耨之本仁以聚之播樂以安之置天
下于仁義禮樂而常申之以敎學以節制人情
使之不至於極如田工有畔一日不敢忘鋤治
焉乃能久于其道而天下之治成故曰人情者
聖王之田也是王道之極也謹論
punctuated:
則否，皎如白日，朗朗洞洞，人情而已。伯之術尚巧，逶迤宛轉，與時上下，屈于所甚屈，伸于所甚伸；王道則否，直如引墨，正正平平，人情而已。伯之術尚捷，令行禁止，急於駭電；王道則否，舒如遲日，容容徐徐，人情而已。世未有遏人情而人不知、拂人情而人不怨、人情和而不安、人情怨而不危者。而俗乃謂王道迂遲、伯圖敏速，則何不引周、秦之故觀之乎？故曰：「誠心而王則王矣，假之而伯則伯矣。」吁！本人情言王道，乃其所謂本于誠意者歟！

雖然，人之情每奮於作新，靡於無事；約於始造，泰於末流。是以亂伏於治，危倚於安，則以持情無道，履盛而不知戒也。聖人既本人情以治天下，而又修禮以耕之，陳義以種之，講學以耨之，本仁以聚之，播樂以安之。置天下于仁義禮樂，而常申之以敎學，以節制人情，使之不至於極，如田工有畔，一日不敢忘鋤治焉，乃能久于其道而天下之治成。故曰：「人情者，聖王之田也。」是王道之極也。謹論。
translation_en:
…is not so; bright as the white sun, clear and transparent, it is nothing more than human feelings. The art of the hegemon prizes cleverness: winding and adaptable, rising and falling with the times, bending where it must bend most deeply and stretching where it can stretch furthest. The Kingly Way is not so; straight as a carpenter's inked cord, upright and level, it is nothing more than human feelings. The art of the hegemon prizes speed: orders are executed and prohibitions enforced more swiftly than startling lightning. The Kingly Way is not so; unhurried as the lengthening days of spring, unforced and gradual, it is nothing more than human feelings. Never in the world have human feelings been suppressed without people realizing it, or defied without people resenting it; never have human feelings been harmonious without bringing stability, or resentful without bringing peril. Yet vulgar opinion claims that the Kingly Way is circuitous and slow while hegemonic schemes are nimble and swift—why not adduce the precedents of Zhou and Qin and examine them? Therefore it is said: "If with a sincere heart one practices true kingship, one becomes a true king; if by borrowing its semblance one practices hegemony, one becomes a hegemon." Alas! To speak of the Kingly Way on the basis of human feelings—is this not what is meant by basing it upon making the intentions sincere?

Even so, human feelings are ever roused when things are newly begun and slacken when all is tranquil; they are restrained at the inception of an enterprise and extravagant in its later course. For this reason, disorder lurks within order and peril leans upon security; this comes from having no way to regulate feelings and treading upon prosperity without knowing how to be on guard. Once the sage bases himself upon human feelings to govern the world, he further cultivates ritual to plow them, sets forth righteousness to plant them, expounds learning to weed them, roots himself in benevolence to gather them, and disseminates music to give them peace. He places the world within benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music, and constantly reinforces them with instruction and learning so as to regulate and restrain human feelings, keeping them from running to extremes—just as a farmer's work has field boundaries and for not a single day dares forget hoeing and tending. Only then can he endure long in his Way and bring the governance of the world to completion. Therefore it is said: "Human feelings are the field of the sage king." This is the ultimate perfection of the Kingly Way. I respectfully set forth this discourse.

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
表
擬宋御邇英閣講讀寶訓尚書左僕射呂
大防等上御書解釋請寘于座右弁緝
乾興以來四十一事可爲勸戒者名聖
學以進表〔元祐四年〕
王士騏
同考試官教授臧　批〔題中條緒曲折頗難整贍獨是〕
〔作檃括典故發以忠愛之辭足備〕
===
黼座炯鑑且布格莊雅擒字精確不藻而麗不斷而工佳士佳士
考試官修撰沈　批〔文辭委婉有則取之〕
考試官左賛善沈　批〔舂容詳雅宜錄以式〕
伏以
聖聖相承茂衍萬齡之緒
明明在御重宣百疊之光
宸文竝
大訓以俱懸炯戒與芳規而交著對揚
鴻烈是乃
彝章陳說
punctuated:
表

擬宋御邇英閣講讀《寶訓》，尚書左僕射呂大防等上御書解釋，請寘于座右，弁緝乾興以來四十一事可爲勸戒者，名《聖學》以進表〔元祐四年〕
王士騏
同考試官教諭臧　批〔題中條緒曲折，頗難整贍。獨是〕〔作檃括典故，發以忠愛之辭，足備〕黼座炯鑑。且布格莊雅，擒字精確，不藻而麗，不斲而工。佳士，佳士！
考試官修撰沈　批〔文辭委婉有則，取之。〕
考試官左賛善沈　批〔舂容詳雅，宜錄以式。〕

伏以聖聖相承，茂衍萬齡之緒；明明在御，重宣百疊之光。宸文竝《大訓》以俱懸，炯戒與芳規而交著。對揚鴻烈，是乃彝章；陳說…
translation_en:
Memorial

Imitating a Song-dynasty memorial presented on the occasion of the Emperor attending the Eying Pavilion for the lecturing and reading of the Precious Instructions (Baoxun), by the Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Lü Dafang 呂大防 and others, submitting explanations of the Imperial Writings with a request to place them beside the throne, together with a compilation of forty-one historical events since the Qianxing reign (1022) that may serve as exhortations and warnings, entitled Imperial Learning (Shengxue) [fourth year of Yuanyou (1089)].

Wang Shiqi 王士騏

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zang: [The threads of the topic are intricate and winding, making it quite difficult to arrange with both order and richness. Yet this] [piece adapts the historical allusions and expresses them in words of loyalty and affection, sufficient to serve as] a bright mirror for the Imperial Throne. Moreover, its structural layout is dignified and elegant, and its choice of words is precise: beautiful without being overly ornate, skillful without showing the marks of carving [reading 斲 for 斷]. A fine scholar, a fine scholar!
Comment by Examiner Senior Compiler Shen: [The diction is tactful and adheres to proper rules; select it.]
Comment by Examiner Left Admonisher Shen: [Unhurried, detailed, and refined; it should be recorded as a model.]

Humbly considering that as sage succeeds sage, the lineage of ten thousand ages is richly extended; and as the illustriously enlightened sovereign reigns, the radiance of a hundred generations is proclaimed anew. Imperial writings are hung aloft alongside the Great Instructions, and bright warnings are mutually displayed with fragrant models. To extol and answer to the grand achievements is indeed the constant statute; to set forth and explain…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
燕清時惟
帝學〔臣大防〕等欣忭欣忭頓首頓首上言英辟
肇基詒孫謨而慮遠哲王嗣服繼治世者
道同荀懿範之如存諒前圖之足紹聿懷
成德宅師祗戒阿衡永念先王立政陳規
姬父監成憲而殷邦郅隆述遺風而周道
中粲蓋源流可接命脉相孚誠故久而必
徵美則傳之斯遠凡在守成之世宜以典
則爲師於惟
===
本朝邁蹤往昔陳綱常以立國積忠厚而開
源粤自
藝祖締搆以來逮我
仁宗重熙之會詒來昆而覆懿爍眞如堯授舜
舜授禹裒前緒而加光明宛若成法武武
法文百十餘年
四聖一道生民特盛近古所希
耿訓昭文圖書爍星華之府
寶章瑤版縹緗燿玉斗之墟布方册以有徵
punctuated: 燕清，時惟帝學。〔臣大防〕等欣忭欣忭，頓首頓首，上言：英辟肇基，詒孫謨而慮遠；哲王嗣服，繼治世者道同。荀懿範之如存，諒前圖之足紹。聿懷成德，宅師祗戒阿衡；永念先王，立政陳規姬父。監成憲而殷邦郅隆，述遺風而周道中粲。蓋源流可接，命脉相孚；誠故久而必徵，美則傳之斯遠。凡在守成之世，宜以典則爲師。於惟本朝，邁蹤往昔，陳綱常以立國，積忠厚而開源。粤自藝祖締搆以來，逮我仁宗重熙之會，詒來昆而覆懿爍，眞如堯授舜、舜授禹；裒前緒而加光明，宛若成法武、武法文。百十餘年，四聖一道，生民特盛，近古所希。耿訓昭文，圖書爍星華之府；寶章瑤版，縹緗燿玉斗之墟。布方册以有徵，
translation_en:
… in the tranquility of leisure, this truly is imperial learning. Your servant Dafang and others, rejoicing and exulting, bow our heads to the ground again and again and respectfully submit:

When heroic sovereigns lay the foundation of a dynasty, they bequeath counsels to their grandsons with far-reaching foresight; when wise kings succeed to the throne, those who continue an era of good governance follow the same Way. If the admirable models remain as though alive, surely the former plans are worthy of being carried on. Mindful of perfected virtue, in settling the multitude one reverently heeds the admonitions of the Counselor-in-Chief (Aheng 阿衡, i.e., Yi Yin 伊尹); ever thinking of the former kings, in establishing governance one sets forth the regulations of the Uncle of Ji (Jifu 姬父, i.e., the Duke of Zhou 周公). By taking the established constitutions as a mirror, the state of Yin reached the height of prosperity; by transmitting the bequeathed customs, the Way of Zhou shone anew in its revival. For when source and stream connect, the vital artery beats in harmony; because it is sincere, over time it is surely verified, and because it is admirable, its transmission reaches afar. In every age that preserves an established enterprise, one ought to take the canons and rules as one's teacher.

Oh, our reigning dynasty surpasses the tracks of bygone eras, setting forth the cardinal principles and constant virtues to found the state, and accumulating loyalty and generosity to open its source. From the time the Accomplished Progenitor (Yizu 藝祖, i.e., Emperor Taizu 太祖) first structured the empire, down to the juncture of redoubled radiance under our Emperor Renzong 仁宗, they have bequeathed counsels to posterity and sheltered them in resplendent virtue—truly like Yao 堯 handing down the succession to Shun 舜, and Shun handing it down to Yu 禹; they have gathered the former patrimony and added to its brilliance—just like King Cheng 成王 modeling himself on King Wu 武王, and King Wu modeling himself on King Wen 文王. For over a hundred years, the Four Sages have shared a single Way, and the flourishing of the people has been especially great, such as has rarely been seen in recent antiquity. Their luminous instructions and radiant writings—charts and books—sparkle in the treasury of stellar splendor; their precious compositions and jade tablets—pale-blue and light-yellow silk scrolls—shine in the realm of the Jade Dipper. Spread out in square tablets, they provide clear verification; …

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
率舊章其奚過玆蓋伏遇
○○○
神靈御極
睿哲紹天
膺龍敘之圖而謙光下濟
撫駿隆之運而泰德方新
長樂中安洩洩融融以交慶
玄旓紫幄孜孜業業以勤求玆
踐祚四年丁孝昭辨上官之歲維孟冬吉朔還
===
寶元解左傳之儀
玉輅晨興望迎陽而東駐
緹帷晝啓對延義以高譚謂當天聖之中嘗
允王曾之請倣十卷唐書而起例纂
三朝實錄以成編啓日曆于金縢已備六十年
之事採起居于恭館曾成三十卷之文瑤
席弘開乃萃耆儒以闡繹丹書在側令宣
美意以敷陳先讀首編而政體治原犂然
掌上接觀末簡而虜情邊備炳在目前披
punctuated: 率舊章其奚過？玆蓋伏遇○○○神靈御極，睿哲紹天；膺龍敘之圖，而謙光下濟；撫駿隆之運，而泰德方新。長樂中安，洩洩融融以交慶；玄旓紫幄，孜孜業業以勤求。玆踐祚四年，丁孝昭辨上官之歲；維孟冬吉朔，還寶元解《左傳》之儀。玉輅晨興，望迎陽而東駐；緹帷晝啓，對延義以高譚。謂當天聖之中，嘗允王曾之請，倣十卷《唐書》而起例，纂《三朝實錄》以成編；啓日曆于金縢，已備六十年之事；採起居于恭館，曾成三十卷之文。瑤席弘開，乃萃耆儒以闡繹；丹書在側，令宣美意以敷陳。先讀首編，而政體治原犂然掌上；接觀末簡，而虜情邊備炳在目前。披
translation_en:
…in following the established institutions, how could one err?

This is because we humbly encounter [Your Majesty], who with divine spirit ascends the throne, and with sagely wisdom succeeds to Heaven; receiving the dragon-ordered chart, yet with modest radiance reaching down to aid all below; presiding over an era of grand prosperity, with the virtue of Great Peace newly flourishing. Within the Changle Palace all is tranquil, in joyful and harmonious mutual celebration; beneath the dark banners and purple tent, you earnestly and diligently seek good governance. Now, in the fourth year of your reign, which corresponds to the age when Han Emperor Xiaozhao discerned the falsehood of Shangguan Jie; on the auspicious first day of the first month of winter, you revived the ritual of the Baoyuan era when the Zuo Commentary (Zuozhuan) was explicated. The jade carriage rose at dawn, gazing toward the Yingyang Gate and halting in the east; the crimson curtains opened by day, facing the Yanyi Hall in lofty discourse. You noted that during the Tiansheng era (1023–1032), the request of Wang Zeng 王曾 was granted: modeling guidelines on the ten-scroll Tang History (Tangshu), the Veritable Records of Three Reigns (Sanchao shilu) were compiled into a book; opening the Daily Calendars from the metal-bound coffers, the events of sixty years were already complete; gathering the Imperial Diaries from thereverent halls, a text of thirty scrolls was once formed. The precious mats were grandly spread, bringing together venerable Confucian scholars to elucidate and expound; with the cinnabar-inscribed books beside you, you ordered them to proclaim and set forth their fine meanings. First reading the opening chapters, the essentials of governance and the origins of order were as clear as on the palm of the hand; next viewing the final slips, the conditions of the northern caitiffs and the frontier defenses shone brightly before the eyes. Unfolding…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
皇圖稽帝文騰休明於典謨之右揚洪輝
播考烈凝孝思于几牘之間香篆隨風或
夜分其未已花磚度影殆日昃以靡遑葢
事稽往貫者藉旁求而法在當年者無遠
慕視彼宣和左闕衍易卦以窮神與夫崇
政西廡陳箕疇以建極方斯
盛舉孰忝前休然
仁宗臨御閱歲滋深而
先帝纘揚在位日淺
===
御書之藏于邃閣者未就編摩故事之副在
有司者尚多遺軼竝宜裒集簡續琳琅仰
贊緝熙功劘
日月〔臣大防〕等識慙窺管職列參衡誠戴負於
高深欲攄陳其萬一竊謂中興配天之烈
遠過漢文而盛德入人之深庶幾周后乃
掇四十餘年之治分爲四十一款之文赫
赫憲章弁包宏略煌煌
御墨濬發微詞自
punctuated: 皇圖、稽帝文，騰休明於典謨之右；揚洪輝、播考烈，凝孝思于几牘之間。香篆隨風，或夜分其未已；花磚度影，殆日昃以靡遑。葢事稽往貫者藉旁求，而法在當年者無遠慕。視彼宣和左闕，衍易卦以窮神；與夫崇政西廡，陳箕疇以建極。方斯盛舉，孰忝前休？然仁宗臨御，閱歲滋深；而先帝纘揚，在位日淺。御書之藏于邃閣者，未就編摩；故事之副在有司者，尚多遺軼。竝宜裒集，簡續琳琅，仰贊緝熙，功劘日月。〔臣大防〕等識慙窺管，職列參衡，誠戴負於高深，欲攄陳其萬一。竊謂中興配天之烈，遠過漢文；而盛德入人之深，庶幾周后。乃掇四十餘年之治，分爲四十一款之文。赫赫憲章，弁包宏略；煌煌御墨，濬發微詞。自
translation_en:
… the imperial charts and examining the sovereigns' writings, raising their resplendent brightness above the Canons and Counsels; exalting their vast radiance and proclaiming the deceased father's meritorious deeds, concentrating filial thoughts among the reading tables and tablets. As the curling incense smoke drifts with the breeze, perhaps even at midnight it has not ceased; as the shadows pass across the patterned tiles, almost till the sun inclines to the west there is no leisure to rest. For when investigating matters of past ages, one relies on wide-ranging inquiry; whereas when the models lie in recent years, there is no need to yearn for the distant past. Look back upon the Left Watchtower of the Xuanhe Gate, where the hexagrams of the Changes were expounded to fathom the numinous; and the West Veranda of the Chongzheng Hall, where the Nine Categories of Jizi were set forth to establish the Supreme Standard. Compared with this magnificent undertaking, how could it fall short of the glories of old?

Yet Renzong reigned over the empire through a long expanse of years, whereas the Late Emperor, who succeeded and carried forward his work, was on the throne for only a brief time. The imperial writings stored in the deep pavilions have not yet been compiled and polished, and the duplicate records of precedents kept by the authorities still suffer from many omissions and losses. All of these ought alike to be gathered together, so that the bamboo slips may continue those gems of literature, reverently assisting Your radiant diligence, a merit vying with the sun and moon.

Your servant [Lü] Dafang and others are ashamed of our narrow, tube-like vision, yet hold office in the ranks of the grand administration; truly sustained by Your lofty height and profound depth, we wish to set forth one part in ten thousand. We venture to say that Renzong's achievement of dynastic revival, matching Heaven, far surpassed that of Emperor Wen of Han, while the depth to which his abundant virtue entered men's hearts nearly equaled that of the rulers of Zhou. Accordingly, we have gathered the governance of more than forty years and divided it into a text of forty-one categories. Illustrious are the constitutional statutes, encompassing grand strategies; brilliant is the imperial ink, unlocking subtle words. From…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
祖訓恪遵至小瑕必錄巨若問安視膳細如愛
物存羊闕大體者悉在旁羅埀來裔者盡
從采輯事事無虧王度言言有補
聖修昔在乾興之初旭日方曦而雲簾半捲迨
夫嘉祐以後中天朗曜而太阿獨持故龍
德正中雖巳粹清無議而龜圖兼總似當
本末粗陳比政要于唐英繁簡差異參帝
學于祖禹勸戒兩存謹齋心而奏于
法筵敢拜手而寘諸
===
黻座
陟降在其左右
朝夕賜之覽觀儻蒙比金鏡以重明受綠圖而
祇若
日御邇英勸講之地神交無逸載屏之心耳目
精神彌近而師摹愈切語言政事竝列而
法監斯昭則
羣后在天共慰式詒于罔缺而千官對御咸忻
繼述之兼隆損益四代其可知禮樂百年
punctuated: 祖訓恪遵，至小瑕必錄；巨若問安視膳，細如愛物存羊。闕大體者，悉在旁羅；埀來裔者，盡從采輯。事事無虧王度，言言有補聖修。昔在乾興之初，旭日方曦而雲簾半捲；迨夫嘉祐以後，中天朗曜而太阿獨持。故龍德正中，雖巳粹清無議；而龜圖兼總，似當本末粗陳。比《政要》于唐英，繁簡差異；參《帝學》于祖禹，勸戒兩存。謹齋心而奏于法筵，敢拜手而寘諸黻座。陟降在其左右，朝夕賜之覽觀。儻蒙比金鏡以重明，受綠圖而祇若；日御邇英勸講之地，神交《無逸》載屏之心。耳目精神，彌近而師摹愈切；語言政事，竝列而法監斯昭。則羣后在天，共慰式詒于罔缺；而千官對御，咸忻繼述之兼隆。損益四代其可知，禮樂百年
translation_en:
… reverently abiding by ancestral injunctions, down to the mandatory recording of minor flaws; in great matters like inquiring after the Empress Dowager's health and attending to her meals, and in small matters like cherishing creatures and preserving the sacrificial sheep [for the announcement of the new moon]. Everything concerning the great principles of governance [reading 關 for 闕] is comprehensively gathered; all that sets a standard for future descendants is fully compiled. Every deed is without flaw in kingly measure; every word aids the cultivation of sagehood.

In the past, at the beginning of the Qianxing era (1022), the rising sun was just brightening while the cloud-curtain [of the Empress Dowager's regency] was half-rolled; by the Jiayou era (1056–1063) and after, the sun shone brightly in mid-heaven and the Tai'e sword [of sovereign authority] was wielded alone. Therefore, although his dragon-virtue was centered and upright, already pure, clear, and beyond reproach, yet in comprehensively summarizing the tortoise-charts, it seemed fitting to roughly set forth both root and branch. Compared to the Essentials of Government (Zhengyao) by Tang Ying 唐英 (Tang Jie 唐介), it differs in fullness and conciseness; consulted alongside the Imperial Learning (Dixue) by Fan Zuyu 范祖禹, it preserves both encouragement and admonition.

With purified hearts we reverently present it at the lecture mat, and bowing with clasped hands we dare to place it beside the imperial throne. As the spirits of the ancestors ascend and descend at Your Majesty's left and right, may You deign to peruse and examine it morning and evening. Should it be favored to be likened to the Golden Mirror to redouble brightness, and received like the Green Chart in reverent compliance; as You daily repair to the Erying Hall where lectures and expositions are held, Your spirit communing with the mind that inscribed Against Luxurious Ease (Wuyi) upon the screen—the nearer it is to Your ears, eyes, and spirit, the more earnest will be Your emulation; with words and deeds of governance arrayed side by side, the model and mirror will shine clearly. Then the former sovereigns in Heaven will all be comforted that the pattern bequeathed is without defect, and the thousand officials facing the throne will all rejoice that continuation and transmission both flourish. What to diminish or add from the Four Dynasties can thus be known; rites and music after a hundred years …

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而大備此〔臣〕等所爲圖繪化工輸流溟渤
者也伏願
新之又新
聖不自聖慎始終之好尚晰治忽於轉移
念令典成規戒紛更而務修復
思人心德澤動搖易而培植難讀其訓解其
書洋洋祖考之來格善可從違可弼昭昭
永監之在玆桑土貴未然寧恃百年無事
薰蕕本異味難令兩立爲朋惟精惟一中
道以凝作則作求下土斯式
===
秉靈樞而非泰王道遐均
握筌宰以有爲淳流旁洽
體堯蹈舜布馨烈于無疆
遵業揚功綿蘿圖于有永〔臣〕等無任瞻
天仰
聖欣忭激切之至謹以所緝書分上下篇隨
表上
進以
punctuated: 而大備。此〔臣〕等所爲圖繪化工，輸流溟渤者也。伏願新之又新，聖不自聖，慎始終之好尚，晰治忽於轉移；念令典成規，戒紛更而務修復；思人心德澤，動搖易而培植難。讀其訓，解其書，洋洋祖考之來格；善可從，違可弼，昭昭永監之在玆。桑土貴未然，寧恃百年無事；薰蕕本異味，難令兩立爲朋。惟精惟一，中道以凝；作則作求，下土斯式。秉靈樞而非泰，王道遐均；握筌宰以有爲，淳流旁洽。體堯蹈舜，布馨烈于無疆；遵業揚功，綿蘿圖于有永。〔臣〕等無任瞻天仰聖，欣忭激切之至。謹以所緝書分上下篇，隨表上進以
translation_en: … reach great completion. This is why your servants have sought to depict the workings of creation and channel a tiny stream into the vast ocean. We humbly pray that Your Majesty will renew yourself day after day, and though sage, never consider yourself sage enough: be cautious of your inclinations from beginning to end, and discern the turning points between order and neglect; bear in mind the fine statutes and established regulations, guarding against reckless alterations and devoting yourself to restoration; reflect upon how popular sentiment and the grace of virtue are easily shaken yet difficult to cultivate. When reading their injunctions and expounding their writings, it is as if the spirits of your royal ancestors are grandly descending and present; what is good can be followed and what goes awry can be rectified, for a bright and eternal mirror lies right here. Binding the mulberry roots with earth is valued before the rain comes—how could one rely on a hundred years of peace without incident? Fragrant and foul herbs are fundamentally different in scent—it is hard to let them stand side by side as companions. Be discerning and undivided, so that the Way of the Mean is consolidated; act as a model and seek to emulate your forebears, so that the land below takes you as its standard. Hold fast the numinous pivot without arrogance, and the Kingly Way will extend evenly afar; grasp the helm of governance with active resolve, and pure influences will spread widely on all sides. Embody Yao and tread in the footsteps of Shun, spreading fragrant renown without bound; follow the ancestral enterprise and exalt its achievements, prolonging the imperial chart for eternity. Your servants, looking up toward Heaven and gazing upon Your Sacred Majesty, are overwhelmed with the utmost joy and earnestness. We respectfully divide the book we have compiled into upper and lower parts and present it along with this memorial so as to…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聞
第叄場
策〔五道〕
第一問
王士騏
同考試官教諭萬　批〔我〕
祖
宗駿烈具在
訓錄
===
聖子
神孫所宜世守者我
皇上銳意紹述輯其大者陳諸
法筵豈直闡發休懿且將丕式而光大之矣此作敷對詳明思模雅頌末復歸重于思艱勵精
二語尤見忠讜其素懷伊周之志者耶
同考試官推官徐　批〔我〕
列祖
寶訓
寶錄創守相承功德備美真足以褆休萬禩者而我
punctuated:
聞。

第叄場

策〔五道〕

第一問

王士騏
同考試官教諭萬　批：〔我祖宗駿烈，具在《訓》《錄》，聖子神孫所宜世守者。我皇上銳意紹述，輯其大者陳諸法筵，豈直闡發休懿，且將丕式而光大之矣。此作敷對詳明，思模雅、頌，末復歸重于「思艱」、「勵精」二語，尤見忠讜。其素懷伊、周之志者耶！〕
同考試官推官徐　批：〔我列祖《寶訓》、《寶錄》，創守相承，功德備美，真足以褆休萬禩者。而我〕
translation_en:
…for the Emperor's information.

Third Session

Policy Essays [Five Questions]

Question One

Wang Shiqi 王士騏
Associate Examiner and Instructor Wan 萬 comments: "The grand achievements of our Imperial Ancestors are all contained in the Precious Instructions (Baoxun) and Veritable Records (Shilu), which Their Sacred Sons and Divine Grandsons ought to preserve for generations. Our Emperor is keenly determined to continue and transmit them, compiling their major points to present at the Classics Mat; how could this merely be to expound upon their fine beauty? Indeed, He is about to take them as a great model and gloriously magnify them! This essay sets forth its reply with detailed clarity, its thought patterned on the Odes and Hymns, and at the end it places final emphasis on the two phrases 'reflecting on difficulties' and 'rousing vigor,' which especially shows loyal and forthright counsel. Is he not one who has long cherished the ambitions of Yi Yin 伊尹 and the Duke of Zhou 周公!"
Associate Examiner and Prefectural Judge Xu 徐 comments: "In the Precious Instructions and Precious Records of our Successive Ancestors, founding and preservation succeeded one another, and their merits and virtues were completely perfected—truly sufficient to secure blessings for ten thousand generations. And our…"

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
皇上惓惓編述
進講輝映
扆几法
祖保泰之盛心蓋後先爲烈矣是策體義閎偉闡揚獨悉末所敷陳尤極忠款宜錄以式
考試官修撰沈　批〔我〕
列聖致治大經大法載在
訓錄
皇上繼序纘述此鉅典也是作對揚詳盡末復歸之艱難勵精尤見忠愛是涵泳
聖化而有得者宜錄之用裨法
祖之助
考試官左贊善沈　批〔草茅之士能敷揚〕
列聖
謨
訓暨我
皇上法
祖圖治之意甚悉而篇末二語尤有卓見亦可謂識其大者宜采之以
獻矣
大哉帝王之道觀於創守述作之際則槩
punctuated:
皇上惓惓編述，進講輝映扆几，法祖保泰之盛心，蓋後先爲烈矣。是策體義閎偉，闡揚獨悉，末所敷陳，尤極忠款，宜錄以式。
考試官修撰沈　批：〔我〕列聖致治大經大法，載在訓錄，皇上繼序纘述，此鉅典也。是作對揚詳盡，末復歸之艱難、勵精，尤見忠愛，是涵泳聖化而有得者，宜錄之，用裨法祖之助。
考試官左贊善沈　批：〔草茅之士能敷揚〕列聖謨訓，暨我皇上法祖圖治之意甚悉，而篇末二語尤有卓見，亦可謂識其大者，宜采之以獻矣。
大哉帝王之道！觀於創守述作之際，則槩…
translation_en:
…His Majesty earnestly compiles and recounts them, and the classical lectures shed their radiance upon the imperial screen and armrest; this grand intention of emulating the Imperial Ancestors and preserving great peace thus shines with equal brilliance across past and present. The structure and meaning of this policy essay are vast and magnificent, its exposition uniquely thorough, and what is set forth at the end is especially of the utmost loyalty and sincerity. It ought to be recorded as a model.

Examiner Shen, Senior Compiler, comments: The great principles and fundamental laws by which our successive Sage Emperors achieved good governance are recorded in the Precious Injunctions (Baoxun) and Veritable Records (Shilu). For His Majesty to succeed to the line and continue their transmission is a grand state canon. This composition responds to and extols the theme in exhaustive detail, and at the end returns once more to being mindful of difficulties and striving with vigor, which especially reveals loyalty and devotion. This is someone who has been steeped in the transformative influence of the Sages and gained true insight from it. It ought to be recorded, to serve as an aid in emulating the Imperial Ancestors.

Examiner Shen, Left Admonisher, comments: That a scholar from the rustic countryside is able to set forth and extol the counsels and injunctions of the successive Sage Emperors, together with our Sovereign's intention to emulate the Imperial Ancestors and plan for good governance, in such thorough detail—and that the two phrases at the end of the piece show particularly outstanding insight—may truly be called recognizing what is of great importance. It ought to be selected and presented to the throne.

Great indeed is the Way of Emperors and Kings! When one observes the juncture between founding and preserving, between transmitting and creating, then in general…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
然矣先天而創大業者將埀啓佑于萬世
必有萬世之訏謨焉後天而守丕圖者將
致熙平于一代必有一代之法守焉作之
于前屬統埀業動思可繼非聖人弗能也
述之于後紹光襲明秉綜前美又非聖人
弗能也夫惟茂明極哲乃知舊章之無愆
稟之若規繩而奉之若律度夫惟弘仁達
孝乃信世德之有賴道若列楹牖而見若
在羹墻故其神凝精注旣臨格之在前而
===
心一道同將感孚之無間思其志也所以
慕愛其言見其心也是以樂循其事知其
慮始之難守之惟恐失墜服其斟酌之盡
遵之如將不及古昔哲王能繩祖武罔敢
自用者豈徒跡其已事哉其中有所契合
而然也是知創守非殊途而述作非異軌
也得創者之道以守而守斯善焉會作者
之意以述而述斯善焉以此深思成德萬
世之訏謨紹矣以此仰參鉅典一代之法
punctuated: 然矣。先天而創大業者，將埀啓佑于萬世，必有萬世之訏謨焉；後天而守丕圖者，將致熙平于一代，必有一代之法守焉。作之于前，屬統埀業，動思可繼，非聖人弗能也；述之于後，紹光襲明，秉綜前美，又非聖人弗能也。夫惟茂明極哲，乃知舊章之無愆，稟之若規繩，而奉之若律度；夫惟弘仁達孝，乃信世德之有賴，道若列楹牖，而見若在羹墻。故其神凝精注，旣臨格之在前，而心一道同，將感孚之無間。思其志也，所以慕愛其言；見其心也，是以樂循其事。知其慮始之難，守之惟恐失墜；服其斟酌之盡，遵之如將不及。古昔哲王能繩祖武、罔敢自用者，豈徒跡其已事哉？其中有所契合而然也。是知創守非殊途，而述作非異軌也。得創者之道以守，而守斯善焉；會作者之意以述，而述斯善焉。以此深思成德，萬世之訏謨紹矣；以此仰參鉅典，一代之法
translation_en: … evident. Those who precede Heaven in founding a great enterprise, intending to hand down guidance and protection for ten thousand generations, must possess grand counsels for ten thousand generations; those who follow Heaven in preserving the vast patrimony, intending to bring about radiant peace for a dynastic era, must possess institutional models to maintain for a dynastic era. To initiate before—connecting the succession and handing down the enterprise, acting always with a thought to what can be continued—is something none but a sage can do; to transmit afterward—continuing the glory and inheriting the brilliance, holding fast to and synthesizing earlier splendors—is likewise something none but a sage can do. Only through flourishing intelligence and supreme wisdom can one know that the old statutes are without fault, receiving them like compass and ink-line and upholding them like pitch-pipes and measures; only through broad benevolence and far-reaching filial piety can one trust that the inherited virtue of generations is to be relied upon, as if the Way were arrayed before pillar and window, and as if one saw them in the broth and on the wall. Therefore, with spirit concentrated and essence focused, it is as though they are present before one; and with mind unified and the Way shared, mutual resonance and trust will be without gap. Because one ponders their intentions, one cherishes and loves their words; because one perceives their minds, one gladly follows their deeds. Knowing the difficulty of their planning at the beginning, one guards it only fearing lest it be lost or dropped; admiring the thoroughness of their deliberations, one complies with it as though fearing to fall short. When the wise kings of antiquity were able to tread in the footsteps of their ancestors and dared not rely on their own willful judgment, were they merely tracing bygone deeds? It was because there was an inner accord within them that made it so. Thus we know that founding and preserving are not separate paths, and that transmitting and initiating are not different tracks. If one grasps the Way of the founder in order to preserve, then the preserving is good; if one comprehends the intent of the initiator in order to transmit, then the transmitting is good. By means of this, deeply pondering the perfected virtue, the grand counsels for ten thousand generations are continued; by means of this, reverently consulting the great canons, the institutional models of a dynastic era…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
守陳矣然則茂烈光美鴻名顯爍焯乎與
日月俱懸也不亦宜乎執事發策以我
二祖
列聖
寶訓
實錄編輯進
御者下詢承學令其陳獻大義爲我
皇上思艱保大之助于萬一生也固陋何能及
此竊聞自唐虞夏三聖相禪面受微言始
===
開精一執中之傳自夏后氏六合爲家世
握大寶乃有典則貽謀之事成湯之興典
刑肅如也而太甲在冲齡維時伊尹明言
烈祖之德以訓于王載在伊訓一德諸篇
太甲以能率祖攸行克終允德爲商賢宗
有商一代之家法在乎此矣文武之興謨
烈炳如也而成王在襁褓維時周公推言
文武之德以訓于王載在無逸立政諸篇
成王以能覲揚文武緝熙光明爲周令主
punctuated: 守陳矣。然則茂烈光美，鴻名顯爍，焯乎與日月俱懸也，不亦宜乎！執事發策，以我二祖、列聖《寶訓》、《實錄》編輯進御者下詢承學，令其陳獻大義，爲我皇上思艱保大之助于萬一。生也固陋，何能及此？竊聞自唐、虞、夏三聖相禪，面受微言，始開精一執中之傳；自夏后氏六合爲家，世握大寶，乃有典則貽謀之事。成湯之興，典刑肅如也，而太甲在冲齡，維時伊尹明言烈祖之德以訓于王，載在《伊訓》、《一德》諸篇，太甲以能率祖攸行，克終允德，爲商賢宗，有商一代之家法在乎此矣。文、武之興，謨烈炳如也，而成王在襁褓，維時周公推言文、武之德以訓于王，載在《無逸》、《立政》諸篇，成王以能覲揚文、武，緝熙光明，爲周令主，
translation_en:
… maintaining the laws has been set forth. Such being the case, is it not fitting that their magnificent achievements shine in splendor and their great renown is illustrious, suspended in brilliance alongside the sun and moon!

You, Sir, in posing this policy question, inquire of us students regarding the Precious Instructions (Baoxun) and Veritable Records (Shilu) of our Two Ancestors and Successive Sacred Emperors that have been compiled and presented for imperial perusal, ordering us to set forth their overarching meaning so as to offer some slight assistance to His Majesty in reflecting on difficulties and preserving the great heritage. Crude and ignorant as I am, how could I be equal to this?

Yet I have heard that when the three sages of Tang, Yu, and Xia yielded the throne to one another, they personally received subtle words face to face, thus initiating the transmission of "refinement and singleness of mind, and holding fast to the mean." From the time the Lord of Xia made all within the six directions his family and held the great treasure from generation to generation, there arose the practice of handing down canons and rules as counsels for posterity.

When Cheng Tang arose, his canons and models were solemn indeed. Yet Tai Jia was at a tender age; at that time Yi Yin clearly expounded the virtue of the Meritorious Ancestor to instruct the king, as recorded in such chapters as the "Instructions of Yi" (Yi xun) and "Both Possessed Pure Virtue" (Yi de). Because Tai Jia was able to follow the path his ancestor had walked and bring his sincere virtue to completion, he became a worthy ancestral exemplar of the Shang; the family law of the entire Shang dynasty rested therein.

When Kings Wen and Wu arose, their counsels and achievements were resplendent indeed. Yet King Cheng was in swaddling clothes; at that time the Duke of Zhou extolled the virtue of Kings Wen and Wu to instruct the king, as recorded in such chapters as "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wu yi) and "The Establishment of Government" (Li zheng). Because King Cheng was able to display and extol the烈 [merits] of Wen and Wu, continuing and extending their radiant brightness, he became an admirable ruler of the Zhou; …

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
有周一代之家法在乎此矣夫湯以前堯
舜固皆可師也而商之孫子乃未若湯之
家法爲易遵周以前禹湯非無足法也而
周之後王尤不若文武之家法爲可守則
嘗論其義焉人主至尊然必畏天而嚴祖
臨之以尊極聳之以神靈雖在宴媮戲豫
有不矍然起而易容者乎是故稱祖以作
敬焉世綿邈則儆仰無繇道伊邇而音容
如接其慕悅者彌切其型摹也彌眞是故
稱祖以明親焉治九有若治大器亦各一
家之法耳易器治之扞格難操保成循習
事半功百是故稱祖以示守焉國體民宜
乆更乃備創圖托始意念精矣非鏡前規
何以待後事乎是故稱祖以廣志焉有斯
四美此以貴明聖故曰明聖者述作之謂
也漢唐及宋代有厥詒誼辟英君竝稱作
者維時繼體之主追復振興則小康汔濟
變易廢墜則喪亂荐臻雖道之粹精者或
punctuated: 有周一代之家法在乎此矣。夫湯以前，堯、舜固皆可師也，而商之孫子乃未若湯之家法爲易遵；周以前，禹、湯非無足法也，而周之後王尤不若文、武之家法爲可守。則嘗論其義焉：人主至尊，然必畏天而嚴祖。臨之以尊極，聳之以神靈，雖在宴媮戲豫，有不矍然起而易容者乎？是故稱祖以作敬焉。世綿邈則儆仰無繇，道伊邇而音容如接，其慕悅者彌切，其型摹也彌眞，是故稱祖以明親焉。治九有若治大器，亦各一家之法耳。易器治之，扞格難操；保成循習，事半功百，是故稱祖以示守焉。國體民宜，乆更乃備；創圖托始，意念精矣。非鏡前規，何以待後事乎？是故稱祖以廣志焉。有斯四美，此以貴明聖。故曰：「明聖者，述作之謂也。」漢、唐及宋，代有厥詒，誼辟英君，竝稱作者。維時繼體之主，追復振興，則小康汔濟；變易廢墜，則喪亂荐臻。雖道之粹精者，或
translation_en:
The dynastic family law of the entire Zhou house lay in this! Now, prior to Tang, Yao and Shun were certainly both worthy of emulation, yet for the descendants of the Shang, nothing was as easy to follow as the family law of Tang. Prior to the Zhou, Yu and Tang were not without much that was worthy of taking as a model, yet for the later kings of the Zhou, nothing was as suitable to preserve as the family law of Kings Wen and Wu.

I have tried to examine the principles behind this. The ruler of men is supremely exalted, yet he must stand in awe of Heaven and revere his ancestors. When overseen by supreme majesty and awed by divine spirits, even in moments of leisure, indulgence, play, and ease, could he fail to rise up in startled awe and compose his countenance? For this reason, one invokes the ancestors to arouse reverence. When generations are distant and remote, there is no way to look up to them in admonition; when the Way is near at hand and their voices and countenances seem almost present, one's admiration and delight grow all the more earnest, and one's modeling and imitation become all the more genuine. For this reason, one invokes the ancestors to make clear familial affection. Governing the Nine Regions is like fashioning a great vessel—each house simply has its own method. If one changes the vessel to work upon it, it is ill-fitting and difficult to handle; if one preserves what is already accomplished and follows established practice, with half the effort one achieves a hundredfold result. For this reason, one invokes the ancestors to demonstrate adherence to tradition. The institutions of the state and what is suitable for the people become complete only after long experience; in founding the enterprise and laying the beginnings, the intentions and deliberations of the ancestors were profound indeed. Without taking prior regulations as a mirror, how can one deal with later affairs? For this reason, one invokes the ancestors to broaden one's aspirations. Because it possesses these four virtues, we value the enlightened and sage. Thus it is said in the Record of Music: "'Enlightened' and 'sage' refer to transmitting and creating."

In the Han, Tang, and Song, each dynasty had the counsels it handed down, and righteous sovereigns and heroic rulers were alike acclaimed as creators. At those times, when succeeding rulers restored and revitalized their legacy, lesser tranquility was nearly achieved; when they altered it or let it fall into ruin, disorder and destruction repeatedly arrived. Although in the pure essence of the Way they perhaps…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
遠謝夫三五而法之畫一者自爲憲于當
年貞觀懿政旴列御屏宰臣令狐綯一爲
進讀宣宗以之端拱正容蓋哲性之所孚
也三朝寶書竝叅記注宰臣呂夷簡一爲
進御仁宗命於便殿觀覽亦彝訓之所迪
也他若陸贄奏故事而德宗比之楷模史
館進實錄而憲宗不能釋卷眞宗誦正法
謹罰之篇而歎深文之非政體孝宗覽正
心剛斷之篇而知君道之貴有爲自古有
===
===
天下者曷嘗不纂圖弘業皇皇于繼序之
思乎仰惟我
二祖握乾符造函夏張三綱紘五典而萬世丕
天之大律啓焉我
列聖昭休明篤龐固統萬方總羣略而一代彌

punctuated: 遠謝夫三五，而法之畫一者自爲憲于當年。貞觀懿政，旴列御屏，宰臣令狐綯一爲進讀，宣宗以之端拱正容，蓋哲性之所孚也；三朝寶書，竝叅記注，宰臣呂夷簡一爲進御，仁宗命於便殿觀覽，亦彝訓之所迪也。他若陸贄奏故事而德宗比之楷模，史館進實錄而憲宗不能釋卷，眞宗誦正法謹罰之篇而歎深文之非政體，孝宗覽正心剛斷之篇而知君道之貴有爲。自古有天下者，曷嘗不纂圖弘業，皇皇于繼序之思乎？仰惟我二祖握乾符、造函夏，張三綱、紘五典，而萬世丕天之大律啓焉；我列聖昭休明、篤龐固，統萬方、總羣略，而一代彌綸之大象構焉。神功駿烈，被格天壤，勒諸瑤函，小大畢載，是爲累朝之寶錄。蕩蕩巍巍，欽爲帝極，緘在麟臺之上，天下曾莫得而名也。
translation_en: …fall far short of the Three August Ones and Five Emperors, yet the uniformity of their laws naturally served as a model for their own times. The admirable governance of the Zhenguan era was displayed in detail upon the imperial screen; as soon as Chief Minister Linghu Tao 令狐綯 read it aloud before the throne, Emperor Xuanzong 宣宗 folded his hands in reverence and straightened his countenance—such was the resonance of his wise nature. The Precious Books of the Three Reigns (Sanchao baoshu 三朝寶書), compiled with reference to the court diaries, were no sooner presented to the throne by Chief Minister Lü Yijian 呂夷簡 than Emperor Renzong 仁宗 ordered them to be perused in a side palace—such too was the guidance imparted by constant instructions. As for other instances: when Lu Zhi 陸贄 presented precedents in his memorials, Emperor Dezong 德宗 likened them to a model; when the Historiography Institute presented the Veritable Records, Emperor Xianzong 憲宗 could not put the scroll down; when Emperor Zhenzong 真宗 recited the chapters on rectifying the laws and exercising caution in punishments, he sighed that harsh andnitpicking application of the law did not befit the substance of governance; and when Emperor Xiaozong 孝宗 perused the chapters on rectifying the mind and exercising firm resolve, he understood that the Way of the ruler values active achievement. Since antiquity, how could those who possessed the realm ever fail to carry forward the dynastic plan, expand the enterprise, and remain anxiously devoted to the thought of continuing the succession? Looking up in reverence, I reflect that our Two Founders grasped the heavenly tally and created the Chinese realm, stretched forth the Three Bonds and bound together the Five Canons, and thereby inaugurated the great standard matching Heaven for ten thousand generations; and our Successive Sacred Emperors manifested auspicious splendor and consolidated substantial stability, unified the ten thousand regions and gathered together all strategies, and thereby constructed the great emblem that encompasses the entire dynasty. Their divine achievements and magnificent accomplishments reached throughout Heaven and Earth; engraved and placed in jade caskets, matters great and small are recorded in full: these are the Precious Veritable Records of the Successive Reigns. Vast and lofty, they are revered as the imperial standard; sealed away atop the Unicorn Terrace (the imperial library), the realm has never been able to find words to name their greatness.

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
明謨睿藻焜燿星日傳諸金簡精微特陳是爲
累朝之寶訓燦燦爛爛森爲堯言烏乎册府之
墟天下曾莫得而窺也恭惟我
皇上明德日新
聖學日就講讀無間于燠寒疏擬日陳于
宵旰久矣猶夙夜孜孜慮明習之不易而思保
守之爲艱謂古先哲王之事旣遠稽而則
傚矣曷若近述我
祖宗之成憲尤咸正而易循乎古先哲王之訓
===
旣遡考而得師矣曷若誦法我
祖宗之訓典尤炳朗而易知乎顧以
訓錄浩繁時幾不暇乃俞輔臣所請特屬儒臣
檢詳故事分類編摩總其大凡爲四十事
首以創業艱難繼以勵精圖治修之躬也
有曰勤學敬天法祖端好戒佚節儉起居
儆戒之屬焉施之家也有曰崇孝謹祭睦
親官閫儆貳之屬焉次之以親賢遠奸納
諫守法務實紀綱近習外戚賞罰詔令名
punctuated: 明謨睿藻，焜燿星日，傳諸金簡，精微特陳，是爲累朝之《寶訓》。燦燦爛爛，森爲堯言，烏乎！册府之墟，天下曾莫得而窺也。恭惟我皇上明德日新，聖學日就，講讀無間于燠寒，疏擬日陳于宵旰，久矣。猶夙夜孜孜，慮明習之不易，而思保守之爲艱。謂古先哲王之事，旣遠稽而則傚矣，曷若近述我祖宗之成憲，尤咸正而易循乎？古先哲王之訓，旣遡考而得師矣，曷若誦法我祖宗之訓典，尤炳朗而易知乎？顧以《訓》、《錄》浩繁，時幾不暇，乃俞輔臣所請，特屬儒臣檢詳故事，分類編摩，總其大凡，爲四十事。首以「創業艱難」，繼以「勵精圖治」。修之躬也，有曰「勤學」、「敬天」、「法祖」、「端好」、「戒佚」、「節儉」、「起居」、「儆戒」之屬焉；施之家也，有曰「崇孝」、「謹祭」、「睦親」、「官閫」、「儆貳」之屬焉；次之以「親賢」、「遠奸」、「納諫」、「守法」、「務實」、「紀綱」、「近習」、「外戚」、「賞罰」、「詔令」、「名
translation_en:
Their luminous counsels and sagely writings shine as brightly as the stars and the sun; transmitted on golden tablets where their subtle profundities are specially set forth, these constitute the Precious Injunctions (Baoxun) of the successive reigns. Resplendent and brilliant, arrayed like the words of Yao—alas, stored in the precincts of the imperial archives, the world has never been able to catch a glimpse of them!

Reverently we reflect that Your Majesty’s illustrious virtue is daily renewed and Your sagely learning daily advances; Your lectures and readings have continued without interruption through heat and cold, and memorials and draft rescripts have been presented daily as You dress before dawn and eat after dusk, for a long time now. Yet day and night You remain untiringly diligent, concerned that clear mastery is not easy and mindful that preservation is difficult. You considered that since the deeds of the wise kings of antiquity have already been investigated from afar and taken as models, how could that compare to recounting nearby the established constitutions of Our Ancestors, which are entirely upright and even easier to follow? And since the instructions of the wise kings of antiquity have already been traced back and taken as teachers, how could that compare to reciting and emulating the admonitions and canons of Our Ancestors, which are resplendently clear and even easier to understand?

However, because the Precious Injunctions and Veritable Records are vast and voluminous, and the pressing affairs of state leave little leisure, You approved the request of the Grand Secretaries and specially charged the Confucian courtiers to examine the historical precedents in detail, compiling and editing them by category, and summarizing their general outlines into forty topics. They begin with “The Hardships of Founding the Dynasty” and continue with “Rousing Vigor to Seek Good Governance.” Regarding the cultivation of the ruler’s person, there are sections such as “Diligence in Learning,” “Revering Heaven,” “Emulating the Ancestors,” “Rectifying Preferences,” “Guarding Against Idleness,” “Frugality,” “Daily Conduct,” and “Vigilant Self-Admonition”; regarding application to the imperial family, there are sections such as “Exalting Filial Piety,” “Care in Sacrifices,” “Harmony Among Imperial Relatives,” “The Inner Palace” [reading 宮閫 for 官閫], and “Admonishing the Heir Apparent”; next come “Drawing Close to the Worthy,” “Keeping Evil Men at a Distance,” “Accepting Remonstrance,” “Upholding the Laws,” “Pursuing Practical Realities,” “Maintaining the Fundamental Guidelines,” “Close Attendants,” “Consort Clans,” “Rewards and Punishments,” “Imperial Edicts and Commands,” “Names…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
分貢獻賞賚而行乎朝廷者靡弗具次之
以保民審官重農理財久任守令興敎褒
德愼刑異端飭武御夷而推諸宇夏者靡
弗詳事歸其目則一編一簡創守咸陳代
列其事則明例成規
訓錄具在雖提要纂玄未足盡乾坤之浩大然
治天下之大經大法幾乎備矣蓋我
二祖
列聖之有天下也旣櫛霜沐雨躬擐介胄而有
===
之又竭心殫慮求寧者定而守之禹域之
跋涉區分不劬于此矣旣經天條地苞桑
緝戶以圖之又著憲申令丁寧儆戒以詒
之豳風之拮据勤閔不怒於此矣宅八荒
以爲大故其規摹弘以遠更數世而潤色
故其意義精以深參古今而垂範故其樞
機周以愼備經制以宜民故其品式詳以
明于是焉悉搴其精菁書其粹宏綱鉅目
次第就編若以銘軒几鏤禹玉遂成一代
punctuated: 分、貢獻、賞賚，而行乎朝廷者靡弗具；次之以保民、審官、重農、理財、久任、守令、興敎、褒德、愼刑、異端、飭武、御夷，而推諸宇夏者靡弗詳。事歸其目，則一編一簡，創守咸陳；代列其事，則明例成規，訓錄具在。雖提要纂玄，未足盡乾坤之浩大，然治天下之大經大法，幾乎備矣。蓋我二祖、列聖之有天下也，旣櫛霜沐雨、躬擐介胄而有之，又竭心殫慮、求寧者定而守之，禹域之跋涉區分，不劬于此矣；旣經天條地、苞桑緝戶以圖之，又著憲申令、丁寧儆戒以詒之，豳風之拮据勤閔，不怒於此矣。宅八荒以爲大，故其規摹弘以遠；更數世而潤色，故其意義精以深；參古今而垂範，故其樞機周以愼；備經制以宜民，故其品式詳以明。于是焉悉搴其精菁，書其粹，宏綱鉅目，次第就編，若以銘軒几、鏤禹玉，遂成一代
translation_en:
… Distinctions of Rank, Tribute Offerings, and Bestowals of Rewards—so that nothing practiced within the imperial court is omitted. Next follow Protecting the People, Scrutinizing Officials, Emphasizing Agriculture, Managing Finances, Long Tenures in Office, Prefects and Magistrates, Promoting Education, Commending Virtue, Exercising Caution in Punishments, Heterodoxies, Ordering Military Affairs, and Controlling the Barbarians—so that nothing extended across the empire is left unexamined in detail. As events are grouped under their headings, within every scroll and tablet the principles of both founding and preserving are set forth together; as matters are arrayed chronologically by reign, the clear precedents and established regulations of the ancestral instructions and veritable records are all present. Although summarizing the essentials and compiling the profundities cannot suffice to exhaust the vastness of Heaven and Earth, the great standards and great laws for governing the empire are nearly complete.

Indeed, when our Two Ancestors (Taizu and Taizong) and the Successive Sage Emperors came to possess the empire, they first combed their hair with frost and bathed in the rain, personally donning armor and helmets to win it, and then exhausted their hearts and thoughts, seeking tranquility and settlement to preserve it; the trudging across mountains and rivers to divide the nine regions of Yu was no more toilsome than this. They first ordered the patterns of heaven and earth, binding the mulberry roots and weaving the doors to plan for its security, and then promulgated statutes and reiterated ordinances, repeatedly admonishing and warning to bequeath it to posterity; the toil and anxious diligence described in the "Odes of Bin" (Binfeng) were no more strenuous [?] than this. Because they took the eight wildernesses as their dwelling, their grand design is vast and far-reaching; because it was refined over several generations, its meaning is subtle and profound; because they consulted both antiquity and the present to hand down a model, its pivotal mechanisms are comprehensive and cautious; and because they prepared regular institutions to suit the people, its grades and formulas are detailed and clear. Therefore, by gathering all their finest essence and writing down their purest elements, the grand principles and major headings have been compiled in order, as if to be inscribed upon the armrests of the Yellow Emperor (Xuan) or carved into the jade tablets of Yu, thus becoming for a whole dynasty…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之寶書此眞萬年之朗鑑也昔我
太祖高皇帝嘗自述創業之艱製
祖訓一書凡十三章丁寧諄復以爲百世而下
雖有聖人一字不可易至
宣宗皇帝仰思盛美遡遡淵源製述
祖德之詩凡九章迨我
皇祖世宗皇帝褒揚功德丕闡光華製和續
祖德之詩凡十四章今我
皇上又類編
===
訓錄四十事進講于
便殿
祖宗之德于焉益顯
祖宗之訓于焉益光將與大明長發共炳天壤
而耀無窮然則修德致治豈徒爲企慕陳
說之文哉儻於進講之際超然自得于言
外
興一念惕乎思艱大之在躬
垂一問凜乎知作法之不易
punctuated: 之寶書，此眞萬年之朗鑑也。昔我太祖高皇帝嘗自述創業之艱，製《祖訓》一書，凡十三章，丁寧諄復，以爲百世而下，雖有聖人，一字不可易。至宣宗皇帝仰思盛美，遡遡淵源，製《述祖德》之詩凡九章；迨我皇祖世宗皇帝褒揚功德，丕闡光華，製《和續祖德》之詩凡十四章。今我皇上又類編《訓錄》四十事，進講于便殿，祖宗之德于焉益顯，祖宗之訓于焉益光，將與《大明》、《長發》共炳天壤而耀無窮。然則修德致治，豈徒爲企慕陳說之文哉？儻於進講之際，超然自得于言外，興一念，惕乎思艱大之在躬；垂一問，凜乎知作法之不易。
translation_en: …precious book of the dynasty; this is truly a bright mirror for ten thousand years. In the past, our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu, the Hongwu Emperor), once personally recounted the hardships of founding the dynasty and composed the Ancestral Injunctions (Zuxun), a book of thirteen chapters in all, repeatedly and earnestly instructing that for a hundred generations to come, even if a sage should arise, not a single character might be altered. Later, Emperor Xuanzong (the Xuande Emperor), looking up in contemplation of their glorious beauty and tracing back to their deep source, composed the poems "Recounting Ancestral Virtue" (Shu zude) in nine chapters. Coming down to our Imperial Grandfather, Emperor Shizong (the Jiajing Emperor), he praised and extolled their merits and virtues, and greatly revealed their brilliance, composing the poems "Harmonizing with and Continuing Ancestral Virtue" (He xu zude) in fourteen chapters. Now our Emperor has further classified and compiled forty matters from the Ancestral Injunctions and Veritable Records (Xunlu) to be presented and expounded in the side palaces. Through this, the virtues of the ancestors are made ever more manifest, and the instructions of the ancestors are made ever more glorious; together with the odes "Daming" (Great Brightness) and "Changfa" (Long-Appearing Omen), they shall shine between heaven and earth and gleam endlessly. This being so, how could cultivating virtue and bringing about good governance be merely a matter of admiring and reciting texts? If, on the occasion of these lectures and expositions, His Majesty transcends the literal words and grasps their deeper meaning for himself—arousing a single thought, he will anxiously reflect upon the arduous and great responsibility resting upon his own person; condescending to ask a single question, he will with awe understand that establishing laws and institutions is no easy matter. …

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
□謨承烈見聞洽矣而以注措為精神謨明弼
諧勸講勤矣而以規模為運量撫萬全之
輿圖如見削平統一之難焉今所為式固
而奠安之者盡思其永休乎陳大定之紀
綱如見參稽建始之難焉今所為執守而
振揚之者盡思其易壞乎察久固之人心
如見安集長養之難焉今所為培溉而固
結之者盡思其易渙乎覽不移之國勢如
見尊全鎮定之難焉今所為鞏固而增廓
===
之者盡思其彌茂乎人才士習視昔孰淳
孰盛敎化風俗視昔孰美孰隆德澤恩施
視昔孰閎孰廣民生國用視昔孰厚孰充
疆圉甲馬視昔孰强孰練議論法紀視昔
孰明孰行事事以
祖宗為法觀委而推其源念念以
祖宗為師考跡而求其意以
皇上之睿明試一加
聖心焉將得其精一而萬善可兼也覩其全書
punctuated: □謨承烈，見聞洽矣，而以注措為精神；謨明弼諧，勸講勤矣，而以規模為運量。撫萬全之輿圖，如見削平統一之難焉，今所為式固而奠安之者，盡思其永休乎？陳大定之紀綱，如見參稽建始之難焉，今所為執守而振揚之者，盡思其易壞乎？察久固之人心，如見安集長養之難焉，今所為培溉而固結之者，盡思其易渙乎？覽不移之國勢，如見尊全鎮定之難焉，今所為鞏固而增廓之者，盡思其彌茂乎？人才士習，視昔孰淳孰盛？敎化風俗，視昔孰美孰隆？德澤恩施，視昔孰閎孰廣？民生國用，視昔孰厚孰充？疆圉甲馬，視昔孰强孰練？議論法紀，視昔孰明孰行？事事以祖宗為法，觀委而推其源；念念以祖宗為師，考跡而求其意。以皇上之睿明，試一加聖心焉，將得其精一而萬善可兼也，覩其全書
translation_en: [displaying?] the counsels and inheriting the achievements, what is seen and heard is already extensive, yet practical implementation should be made its vital spirit; in making counsels clear and aiding in harmony, the exhortations and lectures are already diligent, yet broad vision should be made their guiding capacity. In presiding over a wholly secure territory, it is as if witnessing the difficulties of pacification and unification: in what is done today to strengthen and settle it in peace, should one not fully ponder how to make its blessings eternal? In setting forth the fundamental order of the great settlement, it is as if witnessing the difficulties of consulting and establishing its beginnings: in what is done today to uphold and invigorate it, should one not fully ponder how easily it may decay? In examining the long-allegiant hearts of the people, it is as if witnessing the difficulties of gathering them in peace and nurturing their growth: in what is done today to cultivate and bind them fast, should one not fully ponder how easily they may disperse? In surveying the unshakable posture of the state, it is as if witnessing the difficulties of preserving its supremacy and calming it: in what is done today to consolidate and expand it, should one not fully ponder how to make it ever more flourishing? As for human talent and literati customs, compared to the past, which is purer and which more flourishing? As for moral transformation and popular mores, compared to the past, which is finer and which more thriving? As for virtuous beneficence and the bestowal of grace, compared to the past, which is grander and which broader? As for the people's livelihood and state finances, compared to the past, which is more generous and which more abundant? As for the frontiers and armored cavalry, compared to the past, which is stronger and which better trained? As for deliberations and laws and discipline, compared to the past, which is clearer and which more effectively put into practice? In every matter take the Imperial Ancestors as the model, observing the downstream flow to trace its source; in every thought take the Imperial Ancestors as the teacher, examining their traces to seek their intent. With Your Majesty's sagely intelligence, if You but apply Your Sacred Mind to this, You will grasp its pure unity and be able to encompass ten thousand goods; You will behold the complete book…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而萬微可貫也日思之而日習矣歳習之
而歳更矣寧獨四十事者足備旃厦之陳
與所稱四美者足盡繩武之道已乎生也
仰瞻
鉅典莊捧無階何辭以置對儻所謂擇言于
四十事之中掇其大者必也創業艱難乎
必也厲精圖治乎知艱難則必不自逸矣
能厲精則必知難矣斯二者相須焉今夫
履高危則不見下久娛樂則不聞憂自非
===
蚤夜皇皇專精治理夫孰知創業者之果
艱難乎如欲知創業之果難豈必在觀圖
鑒史間臨淵而知懼履氷而知危羣情庶
事大有類此其必自親事而後知也今夫
多能小技聖人弗留聰明庶慎繁儀聖人
弗兼問察自非深識艱難安危注念夫孰
知厲精神于所當用乎如欲厲精神于所
當用豈必在夕稽晝考間挈畧者振綱挈
衣者持領馭衆裁幾大有類此亦必知其
punctuated: 而萬微可貫也。日思之而日習矣，歳習之而歳更矣。寧獨四十事者足備旃厦之陳，與所稱四美者足盡繩武之道已乎？生也仰瞻鉅典，莊捧無階，何辭以置對？儻所謂擇言于四十事之中，掇其大者，必也創業艱難乎？必也厲精圖治乎？知艱難則必不自逸矣，能厲精則必知難矣，斯二者相須焉。今夫履高危則不見下，久娛樂則不聞憂。自非蚤夜皇皇，專精治理，夫孰知創業者之果艱難乎？如欲知創業之果難，豈必在觀圖鑒史間？臨淵而知懼，履氷而知危，羣情庶事，大有類此，其必自親事而後知也。今夫多能小技，聖人弗留聰明；庶慎繁儀，聖人弗兼問察。自非深識艱難，安危注念，夫孰知厲精神于所當用乎？如欲厲精神于所當用，豈必在夕稽晝考間？挈畧者振綱，挈衣者持領，馭衆裁幾，大有類此，亦必知其
translation_en: … and every subtlety can be threaded together. Contemplate them daily, and daily one grows practiced in them; practice them yearly, and yearly one renews oneself. Could it merely be that these forty matters suffice to furnish what is set forth on the felt rug of the palace hall, or that what are called the four excellences suffice to exhaust the Way of following in the ancestors' footsteps? As a student looking up toward this grand canon, having no stair by which to reverently hold it in my hands, with what words could I frame a reply? Yet if one were to speak of choosing expressions from among the forty matters and plucking out the greatest of them, must it not be "the hardships of founding the enterprise"? Must it not be "rousing one's spirit to strive for good governance"? If one knows the hardships, one will certainly not indulge in ease; if one is able to rouse one's spirit, one will certainly know the difficulties. These two depend upon one another. Now then, one who stands upon a lofty height does not see what lies below, and one who lingers long in pleasure does not hear of sorrow. Unless one is anxiously diligent from morning to night, focusing one's spirit wholly on the principles of governance, who could truly know how arduous the founding of the enterprise really was? If one wishes to know that founding the enterprise was truly difficult, why must it only be in the midst of viewing illustrations and examining histories? Looking down into an abyss, one knows fear; treading upon thin ice, one knows peril. The sentiments of the multitude and the myriad affairs of state are largely like this—one must personally attend to affairs before one can know it. Now then, on manifold abilities and minor skills, the sage does not linger with his intelligence; into sundry cautions and elaborate ceremonies, the sage does not trouble to inquire and investigate. Unless one deeply recognizes the hardships and fixes one's thoughts upon security and peril, who could know how to rouse one's spirit for that to which it ought to be applied? If one wishes to rouse one's spirit for that to which it ought to be applied, why must it only be in the midst of evening verifications and daytime examinations? One who lifts a net shakes its headrope; one who lifts a robe grasps its collar. Governing the multitude and deciding upon the subtle springs of action are largely like this—one must also know their…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
眞難而後能也芹獻杞憂過計若是儻可
稱萬分之一乎虞箴夏鐸將不廢之矣昔
孔子告君以文武之政在方冊人存則政
舉三德以修身九經以治天下所以行之
者一也而宋臣司馬光惓惓於保業惜時
首之以仁明武終之以務實猶之乎孔子
之意焉
皇上法
祖思艱
===
勵精保大守成法持大體謹任人本之以至誠
發之以聰明神武堯舜之治可幾而覩也
已謹對
第二問
陸化淳
同考試官敎諭鄧　批〔天人感應甚微是策獨持論析〕
〔衷明必然之理非淺識可及〕
同考試官敎諭王　批〔休咎不虛惟人所召言天乃以〕
〔著人事也文辭博贍蔚焉可觀必有識者〕
punctuated:
眞難而後能也。芹獻杞憂，過計若是，儻可稱萬分之一乎？虞箴、夏鐸將不廢之矣。昔孔子告君，以文、武之政在方冊，人存則政舉；三德以修身，九經以治天下，所以行之者一也。而宋臣司馬光惓惓於保業、惜時，首之以仁、明、武，終之以務實，猶之乎孔子之意焉。皇上法祖思艱，勵精保大，守成法，持大體，謹任人，本之以至誠，發之以聰明神武，堯、舜之治可幾而覩也已。謹對。

第二問
陸化淳
同考試官敎諭鄧　批〔天人感應甚微，是策獨持論析衷，明必然之理，非淺識可及。〕
同考試官敎諭王　批〔休咎不虛，惟人所召，言天乃以著人事也。文辭博贍，蔚焉可觀，必有識者。〕
translation_en:
…true difficulty before one is capable of it. If my humble offering and excessive worries, overly calculating as they are, might match even one ten-thousandth of what is needed, then the admonitions of the虞 (Yu) and the warning bell of the Xia would not cast them aside. In the past, Confucius told his lord that the governance of Kings Wen and Wu was recorded on wooden and bamboo tablets, and that when the right men are present, such governance flourishes; the Three Virtues by which one cultivates the self and the Nine Standard Rules by which one governs the world are put into practice through a single principle: sincerity. Likewise, the Song minister Sima Guang 司馬光 was earnestly devoted to preserving the dynastic achievement and cherishing the opportune moment; he began with benevolence, discernment, and martial vigor, and concluded with attending to practical realities, which was quite in keeping with the intent of Confucius. If Your Majesty emulates Your Imperial Ancestors and reflects upon their hardships, rouses Your spirit to preserve this great enterprise, upholds the established laws, maintains the great fundamentals, exercises care in employing men, roots all of this in utmost sincerity, and manifests it through sagely intelligence and divine martial vigor, then the governance of Yao and Shun may soon be witnessed! I respectfully reply.

Second Question
Lu Huachun 陸化淳

Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Deng comments: 〔The resonance between Heaven and man is exceedingly subtle. This policy essay alone maintains a balanced argument and analyzes the core truth, elucidating the inevitable principles in a way that shallow understanding cannot reach.〕
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Wang comments: 〔Good fortune and calamity do not arise in vain, but are summoned solely by human action; to speak of Heaven is in fact to make manifest human affairs. The diction is broad and rich, flourishing and worthy of admiration—certainly the work of a man of insight.〕

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭從　批〔攄奇闡奥以健筆而運宏詞是究心於天人者〕
同考試官學正鄭　批〔天人筲矣書事則泥譚理則虛是能洞悉幽微者爲定論家遂養〕
考試官修撰沈　批〔知天固儒者事卽子言庶幾近之董生對天人爲舉首甚有望焉〕
考試官左贊善沈　批〔天人之際茫昧難言子能斷之以理卓有定見足以破諸說紛紛矣〕
夫天人之際蓋若交與然豈不灼然甚近
哉而說者謂天道遠人道邇天人一耳遠
===
者不得獨言天也邇者不得獨言人也獨
言天不言人其弊之乎幽渺虛曠與人不
相徵象其法使人拘而易怠獨言人不言
天其弊之乎習翫具文與天不相符契其
法使人誕而無忌故天動于上而人應之
者不甚切以爲直言其理未必遽有其應
也人應于下而天監之者亦若甚藐則人
之神明不足達其際而天亦未可以虛文
punctuated:
同考試官教諭從批：〔攄奇闡奥，以健筆而運宏詞，是究心於天人者。〕
同考試官學正鄭批：〔天人筲矣。書事則泥，譚理則虛，是能洞悉幽微者，爲定論家遂養。〕
考試官修撰沈批：〔知天固儒者事，卽子言庶幾近之。董生對天人爲舉首，甚有望焉。〕
考試官左贊善沈批：〔天人之際，茫昧難言。子能斷之以理，卓有定見，足以破諸說紛紛矣。〕

夫天人之際，蓋若交與然，豈不灼然甚近哉？而說者謂天道遠、人道邇。天人一耳，遠者不得獨言天也，邇者不得獨言人也。獨言天不言人，其弊之乎幽渺虛曠，與人不相徵象，其法使人拘而易怠；獨言人不言天，其弊之乎習翫具文，與天不相符契，其法使人誕而無忌。故天動于上而人應之者不甚切，以爲直言其理，未必遽有其應也；人應于下而天監之者亦若甚藐，則人之神明不足達其際，而天亦未可以虛文
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Instructor Cong comments: "Expressing what is extraordinary and elucidating what is abstruse, wielding a vigorous brush to deploy grand diction—this is someone who has devoted his mind to the study of Heaven and Man."
Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Zheng comments: "The relation between Heaven and Man is subtle [? 筲矣, likely for 杳矣 or 微矣]. Those who record events get bogged down in details, while those who discuss principles become empty and abstract; this candidate is able to thoroughly comprehend the subtle and hidden, showing the accomplished cultivation of a master of definitive discourse."
Examiner and Senior Compiler Shen comments: "Understanding Heaven is assuredly the business of a Confucian scholar; judging from your words, you have nearly approached it. Master Dong [Dong Zhongshu] placed first in the examination for his responses on Heaven and Man; I have high hopes for you indeed."
Examiner and Left Admonisher Shen comments: "The boundary between Heaven and Man is indistinct and difficult to speak of. You are able to judge it through principle, possessing an outstanding and settled view that is sufficient to dispel the welter of competing theories."

Now, the interaction between Heaven and Man is like a mutual give-and-take; is it not brilliantly clear and very close indeed? Yet commentators say that the Way of Heaven is distant while the Way of Man is near. Heaven and Man are one and the same: one cannot speak solely of Heaven as what is distant, nor solely of Man as what is near. If one speaks solely of Heaven without speaking of Man, the defect tends toward the obscure, remote, empty, and vast, having no verifiable correspondence with human affairs; its method makes people constrained and easily neglectful. If one speaks solely of Man without speaking of Heaven, the defect tends toward habitual trifling and mere formalities, having no tallying agreement with Heaven; its method makes people presumptuous and unrestrained. Therefore, when Heaven stirs above and Man's response to it is not particularly earnest—assuming that one is merely stating a principle in theory and that there will not necessarily be an immediate correspondence—and when Man responds below while Heaven's supervision of him also seems quite remote, then human intelligence and spirit are insufficient to reach that juncture, and Heaven likewise cannot [be moved] by empty formalities…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
動也古聖人通天人一性命後世言天言
人皆眇說耳烏足以幾爕理代天之義中
和參贊之指乎昔之言天者以爲盛衰之
數人實召之故曰我不敢知及其人事一
定曰應惟影響曰貫若草木如此其捷也
及爾出王上帝臨汝帝命與人直在爾汝
間親亦至矣不媿屋漏神鬼察焉一酗酒
淫刑威怒加焉孰云人近天遠耶故璣衡
七政堯實欽若在察之虞典以爲第一義
===
孔子稱堯則天焉後乃屬之星官曆師耳
裨竈梓愼以天可禳而弭則亦可諂而得
殆非若天之指矣公孫僑晏嬰斥之以爲
人主宜修德正事務民之義云耳博達如
二子要非不知天也至宋王安石著洪範
五行傳論一切以天行歸之氣數及其論
對遂以天變爲不足畏水旱爲不足恤當
時有識者歎焉然則洪範庶徵之學亦君
子所宜紹其遠緒而使之弗墜者也蓋自
punctuated: 動也。古聖人通天人、一性命，後世言天言人皆眇說耳，烏足以幾爕理代天之義、中和參贊之指乎？昔之言天者，以爲盛衰之數，人實召之，故曰：「我不敢知。」及其人事一定，曰：「應惟影響」，曰：「貫若草木」，如此其捷也。「及爾出王，上帝臨汝」，帝命與人，直在爾汝間，親亦至矣。不媿屋漏，神鬼察焉；一酗酒淫刑，威怒加焉。孰云人近天遠耶？故璣衡七政，堯實欽若在察之，《虞典》以爲第一義，孔子稱「堯則天」焉，後乃屬之星官曆師耳。裨竈、梓愼以天可禳而弭，則亦可諂而得，殆非若天之指矣。公孫僑、晏嬰斥之，以爲人主宜修德正事，務民之義云耳。博達如二子，要非不知天也。至宋王安石著《洪範五行傳論》，一切以天行歸之氣數；及其論對，遂以天變爲不足畏，水旱爲不足恤，當時有識者歎焉。然則《洪範》庶徵之學，亦君子所宜紹其遠緒而使之弗墜者也。蓋自
translation_en:
… be moved [by empty formalities]. The ancient sages united Heaven and humanity and made human nature and Heaven's decree one. In later ages, those who speak of Heaven or of humanity offer only petty explanations—how could they approach the meaning of harmonizing and governing on behalf of Heaven, or the purport of achieving equilibrium and harmony to assist in the transforming and nourishing powers of cosmic order?

Those in antiquity who spoke of Heaven held that the cycle of flourishing and decline is truly summoned by human beings; hence it was said, "I dare not claim to know." Yet once human affairs are settled, it is said that "[the response] follows like shadow and echo," and that "it penetrates like the growth of grasses and trees"—so swift is its response! "In all your goings and comings, the Supreme Lord looks down upon you"—the Lord's decree and human beings address one another as intimately as "you" and "thou"; nothing could be closer. When one is free from shame even in the solitary corner of a room, spirits and ghosts observe it; the moment one indulges in drunkenness or excessive punishments, [Heaven's] majestic wrath is visited upon him. Who, then, can say that humanity is near while Heaven is far?

Therefore, the armillary sphere, the sighting tube, and the Seven Regulators were reverently accorded with and examined by Yao himself; the Canon of Yu (Yudian) treated this as the foremost principle, and Confucius praised Yao for "modeling himself on Heaven." Only later were such matters relegated to astrologers and calendar-masters. Pi Zao 裨竈 and Zi Shen 梓愼 supposed that Heaven's warnings could be averted through exorcistic prayers, which implied that Heaven's favor could also be won by flattery—surely this missed the true meaning of according with Heaven. Gongsun Qiao 公孫僑 (Zichan) and Yan Ying 晏嬰 rebuked them, maintaining simply that a ruler ought to cultivate virtue, rectify governance, and attend to what is due to the people. Learned and perceptive as those two masters were, in essence it was not that they failed to understand Heaven.

Down to the Song dynasty, Wang Anshi 王安石 composed his Discourse on the Commentary to the Five Phases of the Great Plan (Hongfan wuxing zhuan lun), attributing all movements of Heaven entirely to the operations of vital force and fate (qishu). And when he presented his discussions at court, he consequently declared that celestial anomalies were not worth fearing and that floods and droughts were not worth worrying over—at which persons of insight in his day sighed in lamentation. This being so, the learning of the "Various Verifications" (shuzheng) in the Great Plan (Hongfan) is indeed a distant heritage that the noble man ought to carry forward and keep from falling into ruin. For ever since …

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
天錫禹以洪範敘爲九疇武王首訪于箕
子惟庶徵之疇言之蓋詳其休徵曰肅之
時雨乂之時暘哲之時燠謀之時寒聖之
時風以類若之其咎徵曰狂之恒雨僭之
恒暘豫之恒燠急之恒寒蒙之恒風亦以
類若之其文未嘗牽合不明也而儒者乃
多諱言事應夫使盡如卜祝之譚固不足
道使盡如箕子本意一一自吾五事者而
考稽修省則雖精言之奚不可焉故嘗妄
===
論之曰八卦九疇吐於天地之苞符含有
神理後世皆神而明之設曰貌言視聽思
之配金木水火土而未必然也則乾首坤
腹離目坎耳之屬非乎設曰肅乂哲謀聖
之配雨暘燠寒風而未必然也則震雷巽
風離日坎雨之屬非乎設曰五徵僅言天
人之理非必一事配一行一事得失配一
休咎也則一爻配一象一象配一占一占
應一事非乎故八卦之配德也五行之配
punctuated: 天錫禹以《洪範》，敘爲九疇，武王首訪于箕子，惟庶徵之疇言之蓋詳。其休徵曰：肅之時雨，乂之時暘，哲之時燠，謀之時寒，聖之時風，以類若之。其咎徵曰：狂之恒雨，僭之恒暘，豫之恒燠，急之恒寒，蒙之恒風，亦以類若之。其文未嘗牽合不明也，而儒者乃多諱言事應。夫使盡如卜祝之譚，固不足道；使盡如箕子本意，一一自吾五事者而考稽修省，則雖精言之，奚不可焉？故嘗妄論之曰：八卦、九疇，吐於天地之苞符，含有神理，後世皆神而明之。設曰貌、言、視、聽、思之配金、木、水、火、土而未必然也，則乾首、坤腹、離目、坎耳之屬非乎？設曰肅、乂、哲、謀、聖之配雨、暘、燠、寒、風而未必然也，則震雷、巽風、離日、坎雨之屬非乎？設曰五徵僅言天人之理，非必一事配一行，一事得失配一休咎也，則一爻配一象，一象配一占，一占應一事非乎？故八卦之配德也，五行之配
translation_en: … Heaven bestowed upon Yu 禹 the "Great Plan" (Hongfan 洪範), arranged into the Nine Categories (jiuchou 九疇), and King Wu 武王 first inquired about it from Viscount of Ji (Jizi 箕子), it was the category of the "Various Verifications" (shuzheng 庶徵) that was explained in the greatest detail. Its auspicious verifications (xiuzheng 休徵) state: gravity (su 肅) is met by timely rain, orderliness (yi 乂) by timely sunshine, wisdom (zhe 哲) by timely warmth, deliberation (mou 謀) by timely cold, and sageness (sheng 聖) by timely wind—each responding according to its kind. Its inauspicious verifications (jiuzheng 咎徵) state: wildness (kuang 狂) is met by constant rain, arrogance (jian 僭) by constant sunshine, indolence (yu 豫) by constant warmth, haste (ji 急) by constant cold, and obtuseness (meng 蒙) by constant wind—likewise responding according to its kind. Its text was never forced or unclear, yet Confucian scholars largely shy away from speaking of correspondences with human affairs. Now, if it were entirely like the chatter of diviners and invocators, it would certainly not be worth discussing; but if it is entirely in accord with the original intent of the Viscount of Ji—examining, verifying, cultivating, and reflecting one by one starting from our own Five Demeanors (wushi 五事)—then even if we speak of it in minute detail, why would that be inadmissible? Therefore, I have ventured to argue thus: the Eight Trigrams (bagua 八卦) and the Nine Categories were brought forth from the mystic tallies of Heaven and Earth and contain divine principles, which later generations have allcomprehended through spiritual insight and illuminated. Suppose someone says that the matching of demeanor (mao 貌), speech (yan 言), sight (shi 視), hearing (ting 聽), and thought (si 思) with metal, wood, water, fire, and earth is not necessarily so—then are the associations of Qian 乾 with the head, Kun 坤 with the belly, Li 離 with the eyes, and Kan 坎 with the ears wrong? Suppose someone says that the matching of gravity, orderliness, wisdom, deliberation, and sageness with rain, sunshine, warmth, cold, and wind is not necessarily so—then are the associations of Zhen 震 with thunder, Xun 巽 with wind, Li 離 with the sun, and Kan 坎 with rain wrong? Suppose someone says that the five verifications merely express the general principle of Heaven and humanity, and do not necessarily match one specific affair to one phase, or the success and failure of one affair to one auspicious or inauspicious verification—then is the matching of one hexagram line to one image, one image to one prognostication, and one prognostication corresponding to one affair wrong? Therefore, the matching of the Eight Trigrams with virtues, the matching of the Five Phases with…

title: 萬曆十年應天府鄉試錄
text:
事也曆師之配應也蓍龜之配占也其揆
一也有是氣則有是應應不應合不合法
之密疏則學之精粗爲之天地間實理自
然豈得謂盡無也孔子作春秋書災異至
衆矣而不書事應寧與洪範異指哉洪範
明道之書故推天人之際爲甚精春秋紀
事獨可載其災異耳或天降災于前人事
應于後或人事失于前天降災于後近者
旬月遠者數十年聖人以事繫日月安得
===
牽連而書之既屬其辭比其事必曰某事
致某災某災應某事也豈春秋之體哉故
春秋事皆於傳中發之非特不著災應也
洪範事應乃箕子明言之又非漢儒之妄
也其法則兩漢之史略具矣班固氏本劉
向之意作五行志五卷范曄氏踵固之例
作五行志六卷而司馬彪成之皆以五行
之沴繫之五事以五事之應合之五行雜
采左國世本兩漢近事發明庶徵要歸人
punctuated: 事也，曆師之配應也，蓍龜之配占也，其揆一也。有是氣則有是應；應不應、合不合，法之密疏，則學之精粗爲之。天地間實理自然，豈得謂盡無也？孔子作《春秋》，書災異至衆矣，而不書事應，寧與《洪範》異指哉？《洪範》明道之書，故推天人之際爲甚精；《春秋》紀事，獨可載其災異耳。或天降災于前、人事應于後，或人事失于前、天降災于後，近者旬月，遠者數十年，聖人以事繫日月，安得牽連而書之？既屬其辭、比其事，必曰「某事致某災，某災應某事」也，豈《春秋》之體哉？故《春秋》事皆於傳中發之，非特不著災應也。《洪範》事應，乃箕子明言之，又非漢儒之妄也。其法則兩漢之史略具矣。班固氏本劉向之意，作《五行志》五卷；范曄氏踵固之例，作《五行志》六卷，而司馬彪成之。皆以五行之沴繫之五事，以五事之應合之五行，雜采《左》、《國》、《世本》、兩漢近事，發明庶徵，要歸人
translation_en: … with human affairs, the calendar masters' matching with correspondences, and yarrow stalks and tortoise shells' matching with prognostications—their underlying principle is one and the same. Where there is this vital force (qi), there is this correspondence. As for whether a correspondence holds or not, whether a match fits or not, and whether the method is precise or loose—that is determined by the refinement or crudeness of one's learning. The real principle between Heaven and Earth is spontaneously so; how could one claim that it does not exist at all? When Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), he recorded calamities and anomalies in great numbers, yet he did not record the human affairs to which they corresponded. Could his aim possibly differ from that of the "Great Plan" (Hongfan)?
